1.meaning: A formal disavowal or declaration of immunity — the state of being clear of, and released from, all ties, obligations, and accountability toward someone; a renunciation that severs a prior bond.
1.grammar: A feminine verbal noun. The final -tun (tā' marbūṭa plus nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite ('a disavowal'); the -un nunation signals an unspecified, standalone noun rather than one bound to a following word.
1.root: ب-ر-ء (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, or quit of something

2.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
2.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
4.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

5.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
5.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

6.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
6.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

7.meaning: To enter into a binding covenant or pact with another party — to pledge mutual commitment, the act being reciprocal between two sides.
7.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form III (the pattern with a long ā after the first root letter, conveying a mutual, reciprocal action between parties). The suffix -tum marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine plural) who completed the action.
7.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, compact

8.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
8.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

9.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
9.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

1.meaning: A command to travel freely and move about through the land — to journey, roam, or go to and fro across the earth.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to a group. The prefixed fa- means 'so' or 'then', linking it to what precedes as a consequence. The -ū ending directs the order to 'you all' (masculine plural).
1.root: س-ي-ح (s-y-ḥ) — to flow, travel, roam over the land

2.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
2.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
2.root: — (particle)

3.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
3.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').

4.meaning: The cardinal number 'four' (feminine form). It counts a set of four items.

parts.en: accusative ending (t of the tā' marbūṭa + fatḥa)

4.grammar: A cardinal number meaning 'four.' The feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is the form used when counting masculine things (Arabic number-gender reversal). When a case vowel follows, the tā' marbūṭa is pronounced as 't', so the accusative ending here is -ta. The accusative is the form a noun takes when it is the object of a verb or otherwise governed into the accusative.

5.meaning: 'Months' — the plural of 'month'.
5.grammar: A plural noun (a 'broken'/internal plural of shahr, 'month'). The -in ending is genitive with tanwīn, marking it as indefinite ('months') and is the form used after a preposition or counting word, or when linked to a preceding noun.
5.root: ش-ه-ر (sh-h-r) — month; new moon

6.meaning: A command to know, be aware, and take firm cognizance of something — to hold it as established knowledge.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group. The prefixed wa- means 'and' or 'but'. The -ū ending makes it an order to 'you all' (masculine plural). The initial alif is a helping vowel that appears when the verb begins a word.
6.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing, awareness

7.meaning: 'That you …' — a particle anna ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'you,' used to introduce an emphasized statement as the content of a thought, knowledge, or speech ('… that you …').
7.grammar: The particle anna introduces a subordinate noun-clause ('that …') and adds emphasis; it puts the following subject in the accusative. The attached pronoun -kum ('you,' masculine plural) is the accusative subject of that clause. Together: 'that you (all) …'

8.meaning: 'Other than, except, not' — a word of exception or difference that sets one thing apart from another, or negates an attribute ('non-…').
8.grammar: A noun of exclusion meaning 'other than.' It governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than ___ '). The '-u' nominative ending typically reflects its agreement with, or role describing, a preceding nominative noun.

9.meaning: One who renders another powerless or frustrates and escapes him — a thwarter who eludes capture and leaves a pursuer unable to overtake or overcome him.

parts.en: construct/genitive ending (kasra; the yā' spells a short -i here)

9.grammar: An active participle in Form IV (the doer of the action 'to render incapable'), from a sound root. The final element is the short kasra (-i) of the construct/genitive — the form a noun takes after a preposition or when bound to a following word ('… of …'). Although written with a yā', in this spelling it stands for the short vowel -i, not a long -ī.
9.root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z) — to be incapable, powerless; (Form IV) to render incapable, to frustrate

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: And that — a linking expression introducing a fact or clause ('and that …'); it combines 'and' with a particle that sets up and emphasises the statement that follows.
11.grammar: A connective made of wa- ('and') plus anna ('that'). Anna introduces a noun clause — a fact being asserted — and gives it emphasis, roughly 'and (it is the case) that …'. As a governing particle, anna puts the noun right after it into the accusative case.

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
12.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

13.meaning: One who disgraces, humiliates, and brings to shame — the agent who exposes another to abasement and ignominy.

parts.en: one who disgraces (Form IV active participle, defective root)
final yā' = the third root letter realised in the participle

13.grammar: An active participle in Form IV (the doer of 'to disgrace') from the defective root خ-ز-ي, whose third root letter is yā'. The final yā' (مُخۡزِ → مُخۡزِى) is that third radical surfacing in the active-participle pattern of defective verbs, not an added case ending. The word here is in a construct/genitive position ('disgracer of …').

14.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
14.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
14.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: A proclamation or public announcement — an authoritative notice made openly so that all may hear and be informed.
1.grammar: A masculine verbal noun. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite ('a proclamation'), a standalone noun not bound to a following word.
1.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear, to hear, to give notice/permission

5.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

6.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
6.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
6.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

7.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
7.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

8.meaning: The major pilgrimage to the Sacred House — the great rite of journeying to Mecca at its appointed season.
8.grammar: A definite singular noun. The -i ending is genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …').
8.root: ح-ج-ج (ḥ-j-j) — to head for, to make pilgrimage, to argue/present proof

9.meaning: The greatest, the most great — the superlative form expressing supreme magnitude or rank above all others.
9.grammar: A superlative/comparative adjective ('greatest') on the pattern 'afʿal'. The prefixed al- means 'the'. The final -i marks the genitive case — the form taken after a preposition or when describing a noun that is itself genitive.

10.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
10.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

11.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
11.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
11.root: — (proper name)

12.meaning: Free, clear, and quit of something — being innocent of and disassociated from any tie or obligation, having no part in it.
12.grammar: An adjective on the pattern 'faʿīl' describing a fixed state ('clear/free of'). The final -un (nunation) marks it as nominative and indefinite, a standalone descriptive word.
12.root: ب-ر-ء (b-r-ʾ) — to be free, clear, or quit of something

13.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
13.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

14.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — people who set up others alongside Him in worship or divinity, the opposite of pure monotheists.
14.grammar: An active participle (Form IV, 'one who ascribes partners') in the masculine plural. The prefixed al- means 'the'. The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative or genitive form (used as object of a verb, after a preposition, or in a construct).
14.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — sharing, partnership; ascribing partners (to Allah)

15.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
15.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
15.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

16.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
16.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

17.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'you (all) repented, turned back.' It conveys turning away from wrongdoing and returning to Allah in remorse and amendment.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb with the subject-ending -tum, meaning 'you all' (a group of males or a mixed group) did the action. The action is presented as completed.

18.meaning: A two-part phrase: the connector 'then / so' plus the standalone pronoun 'he / it,' used to point back and resume with 'then he…' or 'so it…'
18.grammar: The connector 'fa' ('then/so') plus the detached subject pronoun 'huwa' ('he/it'), 3rd-person masculine singular. Both are indeclinable, with no case ending; the pronoun typically begins or emphasizes a statement about 'he/it.'

19.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
19.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
19.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

20.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
20.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

21.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
21.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

22.meaning: "You turned away / turned your backs / took charge" — the verb means to turn away, turn aside, or turn one's back; in another sense to take charge of or befriend. The form carries a 'you' (plural) subject.
22.grammar: A past-tense reflexive/intensive verb with the attached subject suffix '-tum' ('you all'), marking a completed action done by the plural addressees. The '-tum' ending is what makes the verb mean 'you (all) did it'.
22.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near / turn toward or away / take charge

23.meaning: "then know! / so be aware!" — a command to a group to know or recognize a fact, introduced by a connector meaning "then/so."
23.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a group of males, prefixed by "fa-" ("then/so"), which links it to a preceding statement as a result or consequence. The "-ū" ending marks the plural addressee ("you all"); the imperative drops the present-tense "ta-" prefix and takes a helping initial vowel.

24.meaning: 'That you …' — a particle anna ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'you,' used to introduce an emphasized statement as the content of a thought, knowledge, or speech ('… that you …').
24.grammar: The particle anna introduces a subordinate noun-clause ('that …') and adds emphasis; it puts the following subject in the accusative. The attached pronoun -kum ('you,' masculine plural) is the accusative subject of that clause. Together: 'that you (all) …'

25.meaning: 'Other than, except, not' — a word of exception or difference that sets one thing apart from another, or negates an attribute ('non-…').
25.grammar: A noun of exclusion meaning 'other than.' It governs a following noun in the genitive ('other than ___ '). The '-u' nominative ending typically reflects its agreement with, or role describing, a preceding nominative noun.
25.root: غ-ي-ر (gh-y-r) — otherness, difference, change

26.meaning: One who renders another powerless or frustrates and escapes him — a thwarter who eludes capture and leaves a pursuer unable to overtake or overcome him.

parts.en: construct/genitive ending (kasra; the yā' spells a short -i here)

Although written with a yā', in this spelling it stands for the short vowel -i, not a long -ī.
26.root: ع-ج-ز (ʿ-j-z) — to be incapable, powerless; (Form IV) to render incapable, to frustrate

28.meaning: A two-part word: 'and' + a command 'give glad tidings, bring good news.' The verb means to announce something joyful that shows on the face — to cheer someone with happy news. It is the standard word for delivering good tidings.
28.grammar: A conjunction 'wa' + an imperative (command) verb, addressed to a single male ('you, give good news'). The base form is bashshir; the final -i here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word, not a case ending. The doubled middle letter marks an intensive/causative sense: actively bringing good news to someone.

29.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
29.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

30.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
30.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
30.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

31.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
31.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

32.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
32.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: To enter into a binding covenant or pact with another party — to pledge mutual commitment, the act being reciprocal between two sides.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form III (the pattern with a long ā after the first root letter, conveying a mutual, reciprocal action between parties). The suffix -tum marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine plural) who completed the action.

4.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
4.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

5.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
5.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.
5.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, partner

6.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
6.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

7.meaning: A negating particle, 'not', used specifically to deny that an action happened in the past, even though it attaches to a present-tense verb form. It turns 'you do X' into 'you did not do X'.

parts.en: did not (negation of a completed act)

7.grammar: An indeclinable particle that governs the verb after it, putting that verb into the jussive (clipped) mood and giving it past-time meaning. In short: lam + a present-form verb = 'did not [verb]'.
7.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

8.meaning: To diminish, reduce, or fall short toward someone — to cut back from what is due, leaving a deficit or shortfall in fulfilling an obligation.
8.grammar: A present/future-tense verb. The ya-…-ū frame marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or henceforth. The attached -kum is the object, 'you all', the ones affected.
8.root: ن-ق-ص (n-q-ṣ) — to decrease, diminish, fall short

9.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
9.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'

10.meaning: A two-part particle: the connector 'and' joined to 'lam', the negating word that turns a following present-tense verb into a completed past negation — 'and … did not'.

parts.en: did not (negates and puts the verb in the past)

10.grammar: Connector 'wa' ('and') plus the particle 'lam'. 'lam' negates a present-tense verb but shifts its meaning to the past, so 'lam + he finds' means 'he did not find'. It also puts the following verb into the jussive mood (clipping its ending).
10.root: — (particles; no root)

11.meaning: To back, support, and lend aid against another — to stand at someone's back as a reinforcing ally, the action being directed mutually.
11.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form III (the long ā signalling a mutual or directed action, here 'to back one another / aid against'). The yu-…-ū frame marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural).
11.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back, to appear; (Form III) to back up, support

12.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
12.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

13.meaning: Anyone / a single one: 'one' used to mean a sole individual, especially in negative or conditional contexts ('not anyone', 'any single person').
13.grammar: A noun meaning 'one / a single one', frequently used for 'anyone' when paired with a negation. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the accusative case, the case typically used for a verb's object.

14.meaning: A command to complete, fulfil, and carry through to the end — to bring something to its full, finished measure without falling short.
14.grammar: A command (imperative) in Form IV ('to bring to completion'). The prefixed fa- means 'so' or 'then'. The -ū ending directs the order to 'you all' (masculine plural).
14.root: ت-م-م (t-m-m) — to be complete; (Form IV) to complete, fulfil

15.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
15.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
15.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

16.meaning: 'Their covenant / their pledge' — an ʿahd is a solemn binding commitment, promise, or treaty; with the attached pronoun it means that pledge as belonging to them.
16.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -a ending on the noun is accusative, the form typically used when the word is the object of a verb. The -hum suffix means 'their' (masculine plural).

17.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
17.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

18.meaning: A fixed term, span, or appointed period of time — a duration with a defined extent, here belonging to them.
18.grammar: A feminine noun (the tā' marbūṭa appears as 't' before the suffix) joined to a possessive pronoun. The -i is the genitive ending, expected because the noun is bound to a following possessor. The attached -him means 'their' (masculine plural).

19.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
19.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

20.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
20.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

21.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
21.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

22.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

22.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.
22.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield (oneself)

1.meaning: A connecting phrase meaning 'then when / and when', introducing a circumstance whose occurrence triggers a following response. 'Fa-' links it to what precedes; 'idhā' sets up a 'when … (then) …' condition for something expected to happen.
1.grammar: A particle cluster, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. 'Idhā' is a conditional/temporal particle ('when') used for events regarded as bound to occur, and it normally introduces a clause followed by a main response. The prefixed fa- ('then/so') ties the whole condition to the preceding statement.

2.meaning: To slip away, peel off, and pass — said of a span of time that strips itself off and elapses, as a covering is drawn away.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form VII (the in- prefix gives a reflexive sense — the action happening to the subject itself: it 'slipped/peeled away'). With no added subject suffix, it is third-person masculine singular, 'it/he'.
2.root: س-ل-خ (s-l-kh) — to skin, strip off; (of time) to elapse

3.meaning: The months — plural of 'month', the lunar periods by which time is reckoned.
3.grammar: A plural noun ('months') on the broken-plural pattern 'afʿul'. The prefixed al- means 'the'. The final -u marks the nominative case, typically used when the word is the subject or the thing being described.

4.meaning: Sacred, inviolable, forbidden to violate — describing that which is set apart under a sanctity that bars transgression against it.
4.grammar: A plural adjective ('sacred/inviolable') on the pattern 'fuʿul', agreeing with a plural noun. The prefixed al- means 'the'. The final -u marks the nominative case, the form used when describing a nominative noun.

5.meaning: A command to fight against and slay — to engage and kill an adversary in combat.
5.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group. The prefixed fa- means 'so' or 'then', marking it as a consequence of what precedes. The -ū ending directs the order to 'you all' (masculine plural); the initial alif is a helping vowel for the opening cluster.
5.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — killing, slaying, fighting

6.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
6.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.
6.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, partner

7.meaning: Wherever / in whatever place — an adverb pointing to an unspecified location, 'in the place where ...'.
7.grammar: An invariable adverb of place ('where / wherever'). Although it ends in -u, it is fixed in form and does not change for case; it is normally followed by a clause stating the situation tied to that place.

8.meaning: To find, come upon, or discover someone — to encounter them or locate them wherever they may be.
8.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine plural); its vowel is lengthened to -tumū to carry the following pronoun. The attached -hum is the object, 'them', the ones found.
8.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon; to feel

9.meaning: A command to take, seize, or grasp — to lay hold of someone or something firmly.
9.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. The -ū ending directs the order to 'you all' (masculine plural), and the attached -hum is the object, 'them', the ones seized.

10.meaning: A command to confine, besiege, or hem in — to surround and restrict someone so their movement is blocked.
10.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. The -ū ending directs the order to 'you all' (masculine plural); the attached -hum is the object, 'them'. The initial alif is a helping vowel for the opening cluster.
10.root: ح-ص-ر (ḥ-ṣ-r) — to confine, hem in, besiege

11.meaning: A command to sit, remain, or lie in wait — to take up a fixed position and stay put, as in lying in ambush.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) to a group. The prefixed wa- means 'and'. The -ū ending directs the order to 'you all' (masculine plural); the initial alif is a helping vowel for the opening cluster.
11.root: ق-ع-د (q-ʿ-d) — to sit, remain, stay put

12.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
12.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

13.meaning: All, every, the whole of — totality. When followed by a singular it means 'every (one)'; when followed by a definite plural or whole it means 'all of.'
13.grammar: A noun of totality, almost always joined to a following noun in the genitive ('every … / all of …'). The final -a is the accusative case, the form used when the word functions as an object of a verb.

14.meaning: A place of lookout or ambush — a vantage point or waypoint where one lies in wait and watches for the approach of another.
14.grammar: A noun of place on the pattern 'mafʿal' (a place where an action happens — here, where one watches/ambushes). The final -in (nunation) marks it as genitive and indefinite, the form taken after a preposition or when bound to a preceding word.
14.root: ر-ص-د (r-ṣ-d) — to watch, lie in wait, observe

15.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
15.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

16.meaning: They turned back in repentance — a third-person masculine plural past verb meaning 'they repented,' i.e. they returned to Allah, abandoning sin and re-orienting the heart toward Him.
16.grammar: Past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they' (a group of males or mixed). As a perfect verb it presents the action as completed: 'they turned (back) in repentance.'

17.meaning: And they established / set up and kept up — they put a thing firmly in place and maintained it duly. Often used of upholding prayer, i.e. performing it properly and consistently.
17.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a causative pattern (Form IV, 'to make stand, to set up and keep up'); the -ū ending is the subject 'they' (masculine plural), marking a completed action they performed.
17.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; (causative) to set up, uphold

18.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
18.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

19.meaning: And they gave / handed over — they brought and delivered something to its recipient. The verb means to come with a thing and present it, i.e. to give.
19.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb on a causative pattern (Form IV, 'to bring/give'); the plural 'they' ending appears here as -awū because the verb's last root letter is weak (vowel-like). It marks a completed action performed by 'they.'
19.root: أ-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (causative) to bring, give

20.meaning: The purifying alms (zakāt) — the obligatory portion given from one's wealth that purifies it and causes it to grow; an act of worship and social due.
20.grammar: A definite feminine noun (the tied tā' marks the feminine). The final -a is the accusative ending, typically marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('the alms').
20.root: ز-ك-و (z-k-w) — to be pure; to grow, increase, be blessed

21.meaning: A command to let go, set free, and leave clear — to release someone and clear the way for them, removing all restraint.
21.grammar: A command (imperative) in Form II (the doubled middle root letter intensifies the sense, 'to set quite free / clear the way'). The prefixed fa- means 'so' or 'then'. The -ū ending directs the order to 'you all' (masculine plural).
21.root: خ-ل-و (kh-l-w) — to be empty, free, clear; (Form II) to let go, release

22.meaning: The compound 'their way/path' — a noun meaning a road, path, course, or way of life, joined to a possessive pronoun marking it as belonging to a group of males (or a mixed group): 'their way'. The base noun denotes both a literal road and, figuratively, a manner, means, or cause one pursues.
22.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The final -a on the noun-stem (before the pronoun) is the accusative case, which generally marks a word as the direct object of a verb or as otherwise governed in that role. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a group that is masculine or mixed in gender.
22.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, course

23.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
23.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

24.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
24.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
24.root: — (proper name)

25.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
25.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.
25.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, veil, forgive

26.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
26.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').
26.root: ر-ح-م (r-ḥ-m) — mercy, compassion, womb-like tenderness

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
1.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

2.meaning: One, a single one, anyone — denotes an individual unit; in negative or questioning contexts it often means 'anyone at all'.
2.grammar: An indefinite noun. The '-un' ending (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('one'/'anyone') and in the nominative case, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence.
2.root: ء-ح-د (ʾ-ḥ-d) — oneness, a single one

3.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
3.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

4.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
4.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

5.meaning: 'He sought protection / asked for refuge from you' — a past-tense verb from a stem that means to seek sanctuary, ask for safe-conduct, or request to be taken under someone's protection, with an attached object pronoun 'you' (a single male). The seeking-pattern (Form X) turns the root sense of 'granting protection' into 'asking for it'.
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the 'seeking' pattern (Form X, is-ta-...), which characteristically means to seek or ask for the action of the root. The ending -a marks 'he' as the one who did it (third-person masculine singular). The attached -ka is the object 'you', addressing a single male: 'he sought protection from you'.
5.root: ج-و-ر (j-w-r) — to give protection, grant refuge, be a neighbor

6.meaning: 'Then grant him protection / give him refuge' — a command (imperative) telling a single male to take someone under his protection or give him safe-conduct, with an attached object pronoun 'him'. The leading 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then / so', linking this instruction to what precedes.
6.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male, built on the protection-giving (Form IV) pattern, which makes the root sense transitive: 'cause him to be protected'. The verb has no case ending (its base imperative form, ending in a silent consonant); the attached -hu is the object 'him'. The prefixed fa- means 'then' or 'so', tying the order to a preceding condition.
6.root: ج-و-ر (j-w-r) — to give protection, grant refuge

7.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
7.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: '(That) he may hear / listen to' — a present/future-tense verb meaning to hear, perceive by ear, or listen, referring to a single male. In its subjunctive form it conveys purpose or potential: 'so that he hears', 'for him to hear'.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking the doer as 'he' (third-person masculine singular). The final -a is the subjunctive mood, which typically appears after particles meaning 'so that / in order to / until', giving the sense of purpose or a hoped-for outcome rather than a plain statement of fact.

9.meaning: 'Speech, words, discourse' — a noun for that which is spoken: utterance, talk, or a connected piece of speech. As a verbal noun of the root it denotes the act and content of speaking, ranging from a single saying to an entire address.
9.grammar: A noun whose final -a is the accusative case. This ending generally marks the noun as the direct object of a verb (the thing being heard, said, etc.) or otherwise as the receiver of an action. It is also the form a noun takes when followed by a possessor ('the speech OF …').

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
11.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

12.meaning: 'Convey him / deliver him / escort him to safety' — a command to a single male meaning to make someone reach a destination, to see him safely through, or to deliver him there, with an attached object 'him'. The base root sense is 'to reach / arrive', and this causative pattern means 'cause to reach'.
12.grammar: A command (imperative) addressed to one male, in the causative (Form IV) pattern, which gives the meaning 'make (him) reach / bring (him) to'. The verb stands in its base imperative form ending in a silent consonant, with no case vowel; the attached -hu is the object 'him'.
12.root: ب-ل-غ (b-l-gh) — to reach, attain, arrive at

13.meaning: 'His place of safety / his secure refuge' — a noun naming a place of security and safety (a 'place-of-safety'), joined to a possessive pronoun 'his'. The noun is formed on the root for safety and security, denoting the location where one is safe.
13.grammar: A place-noun (a noun of location formed with the ma- prefix, meaning 'place of …') carrying an attached possessive 'his'. The -a before the pronoun is the accusative case, which broadly marks the word as a verb's object or destination. The suffix -hu means 'his', referring to a single male.

14.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
14.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

15.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
15.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

16.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.
16.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
16.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

17.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
17.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

18.meaning: They know / they have knowledge — an ongoing or habitual knowing by a group.
18.grammar: Present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they'). The ya- prefix marks the third person; plurality is supplied by the -ūna ending, which together with the prefix gives 'they'. The full -ūna ending also marks the ordinary indicative mood — a plain statement of present or ongoing action.

1.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
1.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

2.meaning: 'It is / it comes to be' — the present-tense verb of being and becoming (from kāna). It expresses that something is the case, exists, or comes about.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he/it is, becomes'. The ya- prefix means 'he/it', and the final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain factual statement (as opposed to a command or a negated/subjunctive form).
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

3.meaning: The compound 'for / belonging to the idolaters' — the preposition 'for, to, belonging to' joined to 'the polytheists': those who associate partners with Allah, ascribing divinity to others alongside Him. The base participle names one who commits such association (shirk).

parts.en: those who associate partners (with Allah) — oblique masculine plural

3.grammar: A preposition li- ('for/to/belonging to') plus the definite article 'the' plus a masculine plural active participle. The undivided ending -īna is the form sound masculine plurals take after a preposition or as a verb's object (the oblique/object case), contrasting with the nominative ending -ūna. The whole denotes 'for / to the ones who associate partners with Allah'.
3.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, associate, ascribe a partner

4.meaning: 'A covenant, pact, treaty, binding agreement' — a noun for a solemn compact or pledge between parties, often with the sense of a guarantee of safe-conduct or a commitment that must be honored. The indefinite form means 'a covenant' (some covenant, not a specific one).
4.grammar: A noun. The ending -un (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a covenant') and in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing whose existence is being affirmed (as in 'there is a covenant').
4.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, to commit oneself

5.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
5.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').
5.root: — (adverb of place)

6.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
6.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

7.meaning: The compound 'and with / and in the presence of' — the connector 'and' joined to a word meaning 'with, near, in the presence of, in the sight of'. This locational/possessive term points to something being held, present, or reckoned in someone's estimation.

parts.en: with, near, in the presence of

7.grammar: The connective 'and' (wa-) prefixed to the locational word ʿinda. ʿinda is an adverb of place/possession ('with, at, in the presence of') that always stands in the accusative-looking form ending in -a and is followed by a noun or pronoun it relates to, giving 'with/in the sight of …'.
7.root: — (no triliteral verbal root; ʿinda is a locational particle)

8.meaning: 'His Messenger' — a messenger or envoy, one sent with a message, here possessed by 'Him'.
8.grammar: A noun ('messenger') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, typically signalling that the word follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …'); the pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because of that preceding i vowel.
8.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sending, message, messenger

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
10.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

11.meaning: To enter into a binding covenant or pact with another party — to pledge mutual commitment, the act being reciprocal between two sides.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in Form III (the pattern with a long ā after the first root letter, conveying a mutual, reciprocal action between parties). The suffix -tum marks the subject as 'you all' (masculine plural) who completed the action.
11.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, compact

12.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
12.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

13.meaning: The place of prostration; a mosque — literally the spot where one bows down (sajda) in worship. With the following 'sacred', it names the Sacred Mosque.
13.grammar: A noun of place on the form mafʿil ('the place where prostration is done'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the possessed/qualified noun after another ('… OF the mosque').
13.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — prostration, bowing down in worship

14.meaning: The sacred, inviolable, forbidden; that which is set apart and protected, whose violation is prohibited out of reverence. Describes something hallowed.
14.grammar: An adjective on the form faʿāl ('sacred/forbidden'), prefixed with al- ('the'). The final -i ending is the genitive case; an adjective takes the same case as the noun it describes, so this -i matches a preceding genitive noun ('the … sacred').
14.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — being forbidden, sacred, set apart, inviolable

15.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
15.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

16.meaning: 'They stood firm / were upright / kept straight' — a past-tense verb meaning to be or become straight and upright, to hold a steady, correct course, or to remain firmly committed, referring to a group of males (or a mixed group). The Form X pattern here carries the sense of standing oneself upright and steadfast.
16.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the Form X (is-ta-…) pattern, here meaning to make oneself upright / hold a straight course. The ending -ū means 'they', a group of males or a mixed group (third-person masculine plural). The final silent alif (-ū + ا) is just a spelling convention after this plural ending.
16.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

17.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
17.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

18.meaning: 'So stand firm / be upright / keep straight' — a command to a group of males to be steadfast, hold a straight and correct course, and remain firmly committed. The leading 'fa-' means 'then / so', linking the order to what came before.
18.grammar: A command (imperative) in the Form X (is-ta-…) pattern, addressed to a group of males (or a mixed group), meaning 'make yourselves upright / hold a straight course'. The ending -ū marks the plural addressees 'you all'. The prefixed fa- means 'then' or 'so', connecting the command to a preceding clause.
18.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright

19.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
19.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

20.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
20.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

21.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
21.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
21.root: — (proper name)

22.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
22.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

23.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

23.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.

1.meaning: An interrogative meaning 'how?' — asking about the manner, condition, or state of something ('how?', 'in what way?'). It can also express astonishment.
1.grammar: An interrogative particle (kayfa) ending in an invariable -a; it does not change for case. It asks about the manner or state of an action ('how…?') and is sometimes used rhetorically to express wonder or rebuke rather than a genuine question.

2.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
2.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

3.meaning: '(That) they prevail / gain the upper hand / become dominant' — a present/future verb whose root sense is to appear or come out on top; in this form it means to overcome, gain mastery over, or become dominant over an opponent. It refers to a group of males.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ya- prefix marking a masculine subject; the plural ending here is -ū (a group of males), and the dropped final -na (compared with the full -ūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form used after particles of purpose, negation, or condition, rather than a plain factual statement.
3.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — to appear, become manifest, prevail

4.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
4.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.

5.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
5.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

6.meaning: '(They do not) heed / observe / keep watch over / respect' — a present/future verb meaning to watch, keep an eye on, observe, or pay regard to something (such as a bond or obligation), referring to a group of males. The root carries the idea of vigilant watching and, by extension, mindful respect.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb; the ya- prefix marks a masculine subject and the ending -ū marks a male plural 'they'. The absence of the final -na (full form -ūna) signals the subjunctive/jussive mood, which appears after particles of negation, condition, or purpose — so it does not stand alone as a simple statement.
6.root: ر-ق-ب (r-q-b) — to watch, observe, keep guard

7.meaning: Among you / in you: locates something within a group of people addressed in the plural.
7.grammar: A preposition 'in/among' with an attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' for a group of males (or mixed group). Words after the preposition fī stand in the genitive, which is why the pronoun takes this object form. The whole expresses presence or location within the addressed group.

8.meaning: 'Ties of kinship; a bond / pact; a covenant-relationship' — a noun denoting a relationship that obliges loyalty, such as blood-kinship or a sworn pact. It names the binding tie itself that ought to be respected between parties.
8.grammar: A noun. The ending -an (nunation/tanwīn with alif) marks it as indefinite ('a tie / any bond') and in the accusative case — the case that generally marks the direct object of a verb (the thing observed, respected, etc.).

9.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
9.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

10.meaning: 'A pledge of protection; a bond of obligation; an obligation of safe-conduct' — a noun for a guarantee or covenant of protection that places the protector under a binding duty toward the protected. It conveys both the obligation and the honor at stake in keeping it.
10.grammar: A feminine noun (marked by the tā' marbūṭa). The ending -tan (the feminine ending plus nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a pledge of protection') and in the accusative case, which typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing not observed, not honored, etc.).
10.root: ذ-م-م (dh-m-m) — protection, obligation, blame upon default

11.meaning: 'They please you / seek to satisfy and gratify you' — a present/future verb meaning to make someone content, to win their approval, or to gratify them, with an attached object 'you' (plural). The causative (Form IV) pattern gives 'cause you to be pleased'.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb in the causative (Form IV) pattern, shown by the yu- prefix; it means 'make … pleased'. The -ūna ending (here -ū + -na) marks a male plural subject 'they' and, by keeping its final -na, signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact. The attached -kum is the object 'you all' (masculine plural).
11.root: ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-y) — contentment, approval, to be pleased

12.meaning: With their mouths — by means of what they utter or speak aloud (often contrasted with what their hearts truly hold).
12.grammar: A noun preceded by 'bi-' ('with/by') with an attached possessive pronoun. 'Afwāh' is the broken (irregular) plural 'mouths.' The '-i' ending is genitive after the preposition 'bi-'; the suffix '-him' means 'their,' so the whole reads 'with their mouths.'

13.meaning: The compound 'but/and it (she) refuses / is unwilling / declines' — the connector 'and/but' joined to a present-tense verb meaning to refuse, decline, or be unwilling, referring to a single female (or a grammatically feminine subject). The root expresses firm refusal and withholding of consent.
13.grammar: The connective 'and/but' (wa-) prefixed to a present-tense verb. The ta- prefix marks the doer as a single feminine subject ('she / it'). The verb ends in a long -ā (a 'defective' verb whose final root-letter is a weak vowel), and in this indicative form it states an ongoing fact: 'and she refuses'.
13.root: ا-ب-ي (ʾ-b-y) — to refuse, decline, be unwilling

14.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
14.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
14.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

15.meaning: 'And most of them / the greater part of them' — the larger number among a group of people. 'akthar' is the comparative/superlative 'more / most'.
15.grammar: Joined by 'wa' ('and'). 'akthar' is an elative ('more/most, the greater part') on the pattern 'afʿal'. The '-u' ending is nominative, generally marking the word as a subject. The attached '-hum' means 'of them / their' (a group of males), so the whole means 'and most of them'.
15.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

16.meaning: 'Ones who are defiantly disobedient, transgressors' — those who break out of obedience to Allah and overstep the bounds of His law. The root sense is of something departing from its proper place or rind; the term denotes deliberate rebellion against the sacred order.
16.grammar: An active participle ('one who transgresses') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks masculine plural in the nominative case — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate ('they are transgressors').
16.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to forsake obedience, deviate from the right path

1.meaning: 'They bought / sold / exchanged, bartered away' — a past-tense verb meaning to engage in a transaction of buying or selling; the root covers both sides of a trade, so it can mean acquiring something at a price or giving something away in exchange. It refers to a group of males. The Form VIII pattern marks it as a transaction undertaken for oneself.
1.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in the Form VIII (i-…-ta-) pattern, which often gives the sense of doing the action for one's own benefit — here trading/exchanging. The ending -aw is the 'they' marker for a group of males (the plural ending of a verb whose final root-letter is weak). The trailing silent alif is a spelling convention.

2.meaning: 'With/in the signs of…' — the preposition bi- joined to a plural noun meaning 'signs', 'tokens', or 'verses': evidences that point to a truth beyond themselves.
2.grammar: bi- is a preposition meaning 'with/in' and always takes the genitive. āyāt is a sound feminine plural; its -i ending here is genitive, the case required after the preposition, and it typically also links to a following noun ('signs OF …').
2.root: ء-ي-ي / ء-و-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, mark, or token

3.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
3.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

4.meaning: A price, a payment, the value or sum given in exchange for something.
4.grammar: An indefinite noun. The -an ending is the indefinite accusative, commonly marking the noun as the direct object of a verb ('a price').

5.meaning: 'A little / a small amount' — an adjective/noun meaning small in quantity, few, scant, or trifling.
5.grammar: A noun/adjective 'little' in the accusative case with indefinite marking (the -an ending, tanwīn). The accusative commonly marks an object or specifies amount/manner; the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite, 'a little.'
5.root: ق-ل-ل (q-l-l) — fewness; being little, scant, or small in amount

6.meaning: The compound 'and they barred / turned away / hindered' — the connector 'and/so' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to turn (people) away, block, obstruct, or divert them from a path or purpose, referring to a group of males. The root expresses both turning oneself away and turning others back.
6.grammar: The connective 'so/then' (fa-) prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The ending -ū marks 'they', a group of males (third-person masculine plural). The doubled middle consonant (ṣadd-) reflects the geminate root. The fa- links this action as a consequence or sequel to what precedes.
6.root: ص-د-د (ṣ-d-d) — to turn away, bar, obstruct

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

7.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

8.meaning: "His way / His path" — the noun for a road, path, or way, here carrying the attached pronoun "His" (referring to Allah); idiomatically, the path or cause of Allah.
8.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive pronoun "-hi" ("his/His"). The pronoun appears in its "-hi" form (with the "i" vowel), which is used when the noun is in the genitive — i.e., after a preposition or when linked in an "of"-type relation to a preceding word.

9.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
9.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

10.meaning: 'It was evil / how evil it is' — a past-tense verb of blame expressing that something is bad, wretched, or wicked. As a verb of dispraise it conveys strong condemnation of a thing.
10.grammar: A Form I past-tense (perfect) verb, 3rd person masculine singular ('he/it'). The final -a is not a separate grammatical ending: it is the third root letter (the hamza, ء) carrying its default fatḥa in the 3rd-person masculine singular perfect. As a frozen verb of blame it functions much like 'how evil is …!'
10.root: س-و-أ (s-w-ʾ) — to be bad, evil, to grieve or distress

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
12.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

13.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
13.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
13.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: 'They heed / observe / keep watch over / respect' — a present/future verb meaning to watch, keep an eye on, observe, or pay regard to something (such as a tie or obligation), referring to a group of males. It conveys vigilant watching and, by extension, mindful respect for a bond.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb; the ya- prefix marks a masculine subject and the ending -ūna marks a male plural 'they'. Keeping the final -na shows the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing fact ('they observe/heed'), as opposed to the shortened forms used after particles of purpose or negation.
2.root: ر-ق-ب (r-q-b) — to watch, observe, keep guard

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
