The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-party subject; the '-ūna' ending marks the masculine plural 'they' in the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of fact ('they are equal'). The stem 'staw' is the contracted form of this final-weak root, to which the plural '-ūna' attaches (yastawūna). Its pattern carries a reflexive/mutual sense ('to be equal to one another').
17.root: س-و-ي (s-w-y) — to be even, equal, level, in proportion

18.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
18.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
20.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
20.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

22.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
22.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

23.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
23.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
23.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

24.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
24.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.
24.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — darkness; wrongdoing, injustice

1.meaning: Those who / the ones who — a plural relative pronoun (masculine) introducing a description: 'those (people) who …'.
1.grammar: A relative pronoun, masculine plural, meaning 'those who / the ones who'. It refers back to a group already in view and introduces a clause describing them. Its form is fixed and does not change for case.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
2.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.
2.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, trust, faith

3.meaning: And they emigrated — they migrated, departing from their homes and severing ties for a cause; the verb carries the sense of forsaking one place and people to go to another. Joined by 'and.'
3.grammar: 'wa-' ('and') + a past-tense verb in the mutual/effortful (fāʿala) form, with the subject ending '-ū' meaning 'they' did it. It reports a completed migration.

4.meaning: And they strove / struggled / exerted themselves — they put forth utmost effort and struggled, including in the way of Allah.
4.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and'. The stem is a past-tense verb of the mutual/effortful (form III) pattern, 'to exert utmost effort / struggle against'. The -ū ending means 'they' (masculine plural) as the doers of a completed action. (The written final alif is a silent spelling convention.)

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
6.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
6.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: 'With their wealth/possessions' — by means of the property and riches belonging to them.
8.grammar: The preposition 'bi-' ('with/by means of') + a broken plural 'wealth/properties' + the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). Words following 'bi-' take the genitive, here shown by the '-i' before the pronoun; '-him' identifies the owners as a group of males.

9.meaning: 'And their selves/lives/souls' — and their own persons; the inner self or soul, and by extension one's very life.
9.grammar: 'And' + a broken plural of nafs ('self/soul') + the attached pronoun '-him' ('their'). The '-i' before the pronoun is the genitive ending, typical when a noun is owned by a following pronoun or governed by a preceding preposition; '-him' marks the owners as a group of males.

10.meaning: Greater, mightier, more immense — the comparative/superlative form of 'great/mighty', expressing that something surpasses others in magnitude, weight, or grandeur.
10.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective ('greater / greatest') built on the pattern 'aCCaCu'. The opening 'a-' is part of this 'more/most' pattern, not a separate word. The '-u' ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('… is greater').
10.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

11.meaning: A degree, rank, level, or step — a place on a graded scale, denoting elevation or a stage above another.
11.grammar: A feminine noun ('a degree/rank'). The final '-an' (nunation) is accusative and indefinite; this ending often marks a noun specifying respect or measure ('by a degree,' 'in rank') or otherwise the object of an action.
11.root: د-ر-ج (d-r-j) — to ascend by steps; gradation, rank, degree

12.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
12.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

13.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
13.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

14.meaning: 'And those' — the connective 'and' joined to the demonstrative 'those'. It both links to what precedes and points out a group ('and it is those who…').
14.grammar: A connecting particle wa ('and') prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. The wa simply joins what follows to what came before. The demonstrative is fixed in form (no case endings), and its -ka element marks distance; it may refer to people of either gender.

15.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
15.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

16.meaning: The triumphant, the winners — those who attain what they sought and are saved from what they feared; the truly successful who achieve ultimate salvation and reward.
16.grammar: An active participle ('one who triumphs') with the article 'al-' ('the'), in the masculine plural. The '-ūna' ending marks the nominative plural — the case typically used for the subject or predicate of a sentence ('they are the triumphant').
16.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to succeed, triumph, win salvation, attain

1.meaning: To give glad tidings — to announce good news that makes the face light up with joy. The verb conveys delivering joyful news to someone.
1.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third person masculine singular ('he'), in an intensive/causative pattern (doubled middle root letter) meaning 'to convey good news'. The 'yu-' prefix marks a single third-party subject; the stem keeps its indicative '-u' vowel ('bashshiru') before the attached object pronoun '-hum' ('them') — 'he gives them glad tidings'.
1.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — good news, glad tidings; the skin/face that brightens with joy

2.meaning: 'Their Lord' — the noun 'Lord' (Master, Sustainer, Nurturer who owns, provides, and brings to maturity) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
2.grammar: A noun with a possessive pronoun. The -u vowel before -hum is the nominative ending, typically marking the word as the subject/doer. The suffix -hum means 'their', referring to a masculine plural group.
2.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to be lord, master, to nurture and sustain

3.meaning: With mercy / by mercy: tender compassion and active kindness that relieves and benefits. The noun names mercy as a quality and an outpouring of grace.
3.grammar: A feminine noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The -in ending is the genitive case with nunation — genitive because it follows a preposition, and the final -n marks it as indefinite ('a mercy').

4.meaning: A prepositional phrase, 'from him/it' — indicating origin or source, that something proceeds out of him/it.
4.grammar: The preposition min ('from') with the attached pronoun -hu ('him/it', third-person masculine singular). As the object of a preposition the pronoun stands in the genitive; the combination indicates source or origin.

5.meaning: Good pleasure, acceptance, and approval — especially the gracious good pleasure of Allah, His being pleased with someone, which is the highest of favors.
5.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. The word is a verbal noun ('good pleasure'). The ending '-in' (with tanwīn, an unattached 'n' sound) marks the genitive case and indefiniteness — typically following a preposition or linked after another noun ('… of good pleasure').
5.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w / r-ḍ-y) — to be pleased, content, satisfied

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'and gardens' — lush, walled enclosures of trees and greenery; a place of abundant growth.
6.grammar: A feminine plural noun prefixed with wa- ('and'). The -in ending (tanwīn) marks it indefinite ('gardens,' not 'the gardens') and genitive — the case taken after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
6.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — covering, concealing; hence a garden whose foliage covers the ground

7.meaning: 'For them / to them / theirs' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the pronoun 'them,' expressing that something pertains, belongs, or is owed to that group.
7.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to'), whose vowel becomes -a before an attached pronoun, joined to -hum ('them'). It commonly expresses possession or benefit — 'theirs / for them.' Particles like this carry no case or tense of their own.

8.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
8.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

9.meaning: Bliss, delight, and abundant comfort — a state of luxuriant ease and lasting enjoyment, the soft and pleasant living of those favored with blessing.
9.grammar: A noun in an intensive pattern denoting abundant comfort. The ending '-un' (with tanwīn, an unattached 'n' sound) marks the nominative case and indefiniteness — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate ('… is bliss').
9.root: ن-ع-م (n-ʿ-m) — softness, ease, blessing, favor, delight

10.meaning: "lasting, enduring, permanent, abiding" — an active participle describing something that stays in place, persists, or is established and ongoing.
10.grammar: An active participle (form IV) functioning as an adjective/noun ("one that stays, abiding"). The "mu-" prefix marks the doer/agent of the action. The final "-un" (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative ending, marking the word as indefinite ("a lasting one") and as a subject or predicate rather than an object.
10.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, remain, establish

1.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
1.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

2.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
2.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.
2.root: — (particle plus pronoun; no root)

3.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
3.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

4.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
4.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
5.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
5.root: — (proper name)

6.meaning: 'With him / in his keeping / that he has' — combining the locational word 'ind ('at, with, in the presence/possession of') with the pronoun 'him'. It conveys that something is held by, present with, or belongs to him.
6.grammar: 'ʿinda' is an adverb of place/possession that always governs a following word in the genitive; here it takes the attached pronoun -hu ('him/his'). The -a on 'ʿinda' is its fixed accusative-style ending as an adverbial. The pronoun -hu means the thing is located with, or owned by, a single male.

7.meaning: Means 'a reward, a wage, a recompense'. The word denotes the due return for work or deeds — payment earned, compensation, or a reward.
7.grammar: A noun in the nominative, indefinite ('a reward'). The -un ending (a doubled-vowel tanwīn) marks both indefiniteness ('a/some') and the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a thing being asserted to exist ('there is a reward').
7.root: ا-ج-ر (ʾ-j-r) — reward, wage, recompense

8.meaning: Great, immense, mighty — vast in magnitude or importance. Describes something tremendous, whether in size, weight, or gravity.
8.grammar: An adjective on the intensive 'faʿīl' pattern, conveying a strong, established quality. The '-un' ending marks it nominative and indefinite; as an adjective it typically agrees with and describes an indefinite noun ('a great …').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
4.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

5.meaning: That you take, that you adopt — a present-tense verb (form VIII) meaning to take for oneself, to choose or adopt something. Addressed to a group ('you all'), and in a form used after particles meaning 'that' or 'to'.
5.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive (form VIII) pattern, 'to take for oneself'. The ta- prefix with the plural ending means 'you all'. The ending is -ū (the final 'n' of -ūna has dropped), which marks the subjunctive or jussive mood — the form used after particles like 'that', 'to', or 'not'.
5.root: ء-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize

6.meaning: Fathers, forefathers, ancestors — male parents, and by extension the line of forebears.
6.grammar: A plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessive pronoun '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-a' between the noun and the pronoun marks the accusative case (typically a direct object); '-kum' adds the possessor 'of you all' (ābāʾakum).
6.root: ء-ب-و (ʾ-b-w) — father, fatherhood

7.meaning: Brothers — and more broadly kinsmen, brethren, or close companions bound by ties of blood, faith, or fellowship.
7.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. The word is a plural noun ('brothers') with the attached possessive '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-a' before the pronoun marks the accusative case (typically a direct object); '-kum' supplies the possessor 'of you all' (ikhwānakum).
7.root: ء-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brother, brotherhood

8.meaning: Allies, protectors, intimate friends — those taken as close supporters, patrons, or guardians, with whom one stands in mutual loyalty (plural of walī).
8.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'walī.' Being a 'diptote' (a noun that resists the usual full set of endings), it takes a single final '-a' here for the accusative case, which commonly marks the direct object of a verb or signals 'as / being' something — and notably without the usual '-n' (no nunation).

9.meaning: If — a particle introducing a condition: it sets up 'if X (happens), then Y'.
9.grammar: A conditional particle ('if') that introduces a supposed case and typically puts the following verb into the jussive (conditional) form. Its base shape is 'in', whose final nūn carries a sukūn and is fully pronounced. When the next word begins with a sukūn-bearing cluster, the otherwise-quiescent nūn is given a kasra (-i) to avoid two consecutive sukūns meeting (the 'meeting of two quiescents'); this helping vowel eases pronunciation and carries no grammatical meaning of its own.

10.meaning: To love more, to prefer, to hold dearer — to give one thing precedence in affection over another, choosing it because it is more beloved.
10.grammar: A past-tense verb, third person masculine plural ('they'), in a 'seeking' pattern (the 'ista-' shape) that here conveys deeming something more beloved. The long '-ū' ending marks the masculine plural subject 'they' in completed time ('they preferred').
10.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection, to hold dear

11.meaning: 'Disbelief / rejection' — the act of refusing faith, denying the truth, and being ungrateful toward Allah and His signs; the opposite of belief.
11.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the'. The noun kufr ('disbelief') carries an -a ending, the accusative case, which typically marks the direct object of a verb ('… perceived/found THE disbelief').
11.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover up, to reject faith, to be ungrateful

12.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
12.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
12.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

13.meaning: Faith — heartfelt belief and trusting acceptance; the inner conviction and security of the heart in Allah, joined with affirmation and trust. More than mental assent, it is a settled faith that gives the heart peace.
13.grammar: A verbal noun ('believing, faith') with the article 'al-' ('the'). The final '-i' marks the genitive case: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('the … OF faith') or follows a preposition. The pattern carries the sense of granting security/trust.
13.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust, to be at peace and believe

14.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
14.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.

15.meaning: He takes (someone) as a close ally, befriends and allies himself with them, gives them his loyalty and turns to them for support. The Form V verb adds the sense of deliberately choosing and embracing that allegiance for oneself.

parts.en: take as ally (Form V, reflexive stem)

15.grammar: A present-tense Form V verb for 'he', with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them'). The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject; the long -ā stem is characteristic of this verb pattern, and -hum names the people receiving the action.
15.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — nearness, alliance, guardianship, loyalty

16.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
16.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.

17.meaning: A pointing word meaning 'those' — used to indicate a group already mentioned or in view, often emphatically singling them out as 'those very ones'.
17.grammar: The prefix fa- means 'so/then', often introducing a result. The remainder is a demonstrative pronoun, 'those', pointing to a plural group at a distance. Demonstratives of this kind are fixed in form and do not change for case; the final -ka is an intrinsic deictic element of the pronoun itself, not a separable suffix.

18.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
18.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

19.meaning: The wrongdoers; those who do wrong, act unjustly, or place things where they do not belong. The underlying image is one who oppresses, transgresses limits, and deals unjustly with others or with themselves.
19.grammar: An active participle (the doer of the action) made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative (subject) case, the form used when the word functions as the doer of a verb or the subject of a sentence.
19.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — wrongdoing, injustice, oppression

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
2.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

3.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

3.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.

4.meaning: Your fathers / forefathers / parents; the plural 'fathers' joined to a 'your (plural)' possessor, denoting the male ancestors or, more broadly, the parents of a group.
4.grammar: A broken plural noun ('fathers') with the attached possessor -kum ('your', addressing several people). The -u case-vowel before the suffix is nominative, typically marking the word as the doer or subject of a sentence. The ending -kum specifically addresses a group of males or a mixed group.

5.meaning: And your sons / children; the plural 'sons' joined to a 'your (plural)' possessor, with a leading 'and' connecting it to what precedes.
5.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a broken plural noun ('sons') bearing the possessor -kum ('your', for a group). The -u case-vowel before the suffix is nominative, typically marking a subject or an item in a list of subjects. The -kum addresses several people.
5.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — son, offspring; to build

6.meaning: Brothers — and more broadly kinsmen, brethren, or close companions bound by ties of blood, faith, or fellowship.
6.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. The word is a plural noun ('brothers') with the attached possessive '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-u' before the pronoun marks the nominative case — typically the subject or predicate of a sentence; '-kum' supplies the possessor 'of you all' (ikhwānukum).
6.root: ء-خ-و (ʾ-kh-w) — brother, brotherhood

7.meaning: Spouses — husbands or wives; mates and partners. The word denotes one of a pair, the marriage partner who completes the other.
7.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. The word is a plural noun ('spouses, mates') with the attached possessive '-kum' ('your', addressing a group). The '-u' before the pronoun marks the nominative case — typically the subject or predicate of a sentence; '-kum' supplies the possessor 'of you all' (azwājukum).
7.root: ز-و-ج (z-w-j) — pair, mate, spouse, to join two as a couple

8.meaning: And your kinsfolk — the wider family group, clan, or tribe to which one belongs: relatives connected by blood and lineage. The form refers to one's extended kin collectively, with the sense of those nearest and dearest by descent.

parts.en: kinsfolk / clan (with tā' marbūṭa surfacing as -t- before the suffix)

8.grammar: A noun with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and') and the attached pronoun -kum ('your', addressing a group of males or a mixed group). The noun's feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is pronounced -t- here because a suffix follows. The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or stands as the thing being named or pointed out.
8.root: ع-ش-ر (ʿ-sh-r) — close association, intimate companionship, kindred (also the number ten)

9.meaning: And wealth, possessions, property — material goods and assets owned, especially livestock, money, and movable riches. It is the plural of māl, denoting accumulated wealth in general rather than a single item.
9.grammar: A plural noun with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and'). The ending -un (nunation, marked by the doubled vowel) is the nominative case in its indefinite form, signalling 'wealth' in general (an unspecified 'some wealth') rather than a particular, definite wealth; the nominative marks it as a subject or a named thing.
9.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, the having of means

10.meaning: You have earned it / acquired it — to gain, amass, or come by something through one's own effort, often labour or enterprise. The verb iqtarafa carries the nuance of working to obtain, and can extend to 'committing' or 'perpetrating' a deed (good or bad).
10.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form VIII) in the second person masculine plural: the suffix -tum means 'you all (did)', here extended to -tumū before the attached object pronoun -hā ('it', referring to a feminine or non-human thing). So the whole conveys a completed act done by a group: 'you all earned it'.
10.root: ق-ر-ف (q-r-f) — to scrape together, earn, acquire (in Form VIII, to commit/perpetrate)

11.meaning: And trade, commerce, business — the activity of buying and selling for profit, and by extension a commercial venture or merchandise. Tijāra denotes the whole enterprise of trafficking in goods.

parts.en: trade / commerce (with tā' marbūṭa surfacing as -t- before nunation)

11.grammar: A noun with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and'). Its feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is pronounced -t- here because nunation follows. The ending -un (nunation) is the indefinite nominative case, naming 'a trade / commerce' in a general, unspecified sense and marking it as a subject or named thing.
11.root: ت-ج-ر (t-j-r) — trading, commerce, the work of a merchant

12.meaning: You fear, you are anxious about, you dread — an apprehension of harm or loss, especially a reverent or cautious fear of something turning out badly. Khashiya often blends dread with awe and wary anticipation.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second person masculine plural. The ta- prefix marks 'you', and the -na ending marks the plural, so together they mean 'you (all) fear'. The form expresses an ongoing or habitual action — fearing as a present, continuing state.
12.root: خ-ش-ي (kh-sh-y) — fear mingled with awe and reverence

13.meaning: Its becoming unsaleable / its stagnation / its slump — the state of goods not selling, lying dull and without demand, and so commerce going slack. Kasād is the failure of a market to move.
13.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hā ('its', referring to a feminine or non-human thing). The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb — the thing acted upon, feared, or sought.
13.root: ك-س-د (k-s-d) — to be slack, unsaleable, dull in trade

14.meaning: And dwellings, residences, homes — the places where people live and settle. Masākin is the plural of maskan, a place of dwelling, from the idea of coming to rest and stillness in a settled abode.
14.grammar: A plural noun with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and'). The final -u is the nominative case, marking the word as a subject or a named thing. (As a 'diptote' plural pattern, this noun does not take nunation, so the bare -u stands without an -n.)
14.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — stillness, rest, dwelling, settling down

15.meaning: You are pleased with it / you find it agreeable / you are content with it — to look on something with satisfaction and approval, to be well-pleased. Riḍā is contented acceptance and delight.
15.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second person masculine plural with an attached object pronoun -hā ('it', feminine/non-human). The ta- prefix marks 'you' and the -na marks the plural, so the verb means 'you (all) are pleased' with the thing named by -hā — expressing an ongoing or habitual state of contentment.
15.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased, satisfied, well-content

16.meaning: More beloved / dearer — held in greater love or preference. This is the comparative/superlative form ('more/most loved'), expressing that one thing is loved above another.
16.grammar: An elative (comparative/superlative) adjective on the pattern afʿal, meaning 'more/most beloved'. The leading a- is the elative prefix that conveys 'more' or 'most'. The final -a is the accusative case, the form taken when the word functions as a direct object or predicate of certain verbs. (This pattern is a 'diptote', so it takes a bare -a without nunation.)

17.meaning: To you / toward you (plural) — a preposition expressing motion or direction reaching a destination, joined with 'you all' as that destination.
17.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to, toward'), whose ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached, plus -kum ('you all'). Together they mark the end-point or recipient of an action — the direction 'toward' or 'unto' a group.

18.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
18.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
20.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
20.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

21.meaning: And striving / struggle / exertion — the wholehearted expending of effort and endurance toward a goal, including struggle in the path of Allah. Jihād is earnest, strenuous striving against difficulty.
21.grammar: A verbal noun with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and'). The ending -in (nunation) is the indefinite genitive case: the genitive typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to another noun ('… of …'), while the indefinite -in marks it as 'a striving' in general rather than a specific one.
21.root: ج-ه-د (j-h-d) — to exert effort, strive, struggle to one's utmost

22.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
22.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
22.root: — (particle)

23.meaning: "His way / His path" — the noun for a road, path, or way, here carrying the attached pronoun "His" (referring to Allah); idiomatically, the path or cause of Allah.
23.grammar: A masculine noun with the attached possessive pronoun "-hi" ("his/His"). The pronoun appears in its "-hi" form (with the "i" vowel), which is used when the noun is in the genitive — i.e., after a preposition or when linked in an "of"-type relation to a preceding word.

24.meaning: Then wait / then await / then watch and bide your time — a command to expect an outcome, holding back to see what comes. Tarabbaṣa is to wait expectantly, sometimes warily, for something to unfold.
24.grammar: A command (imperative) verb (Form V) addressed to a group of males or a mixed group, prefixed by fa- ('then/so'), which links it to what precedes as a consequence. The plural-command ending -ū means 'you all, do this!' — so it directs a group to wait. (The written alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention.)
24.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, lie in wait, watch for an outcome

25.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
25.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.
25.root: — (particle)

26.meaning: He/it comes, brings, or arrives — to come or to bring (something) about. The form points to an action not yet completed (present or future).
26.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it comes'). The ya- prefix (a single, undoubled yāʾ) marks a single male/thing subject. The final -a (in -iya) is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles meaning 'that', 'until', or 'so that', giving the sense '… that he come' or '… until he comes'.
26.root: ء-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, bring

27.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
27.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

28.meaning: With/by His command — amr means a command, order, decree, or matter/affair; with the preposition bi- ('with, by') and the pronoun 'His' it conveys 'by His command' or 'by His decree'.
28.grammar: The prefix bi- means 'with' or 'by'. The noun amr takes the genitive -i ending (required after the preposition bi-) and then the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The genitive marks the noun as governed by the preposition.
28.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order; a matter/affair

29.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
29.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
29.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

30.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
30.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

31.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
31.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
31.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

32.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
32.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
32.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

33.meaning: 'The defiantly disobedient ones'. Those described as fāsiq: people who break out of obedience to Allah, overstepping the bounds of His law and rebelling against right conduct.
33.grammar: An active participle ('one who defies/transgresses') with 'the' in front, masculine plural. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the accusative/genitive — the form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition.
33.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to forsake obedience, transgress, rebel

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: He helped, aided, supported, or gave victory to you (plural) — 'naṣr' is decisive help that brings triumph, especially in defending against an adversary.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb with an attached object pronoun. The bare three-letter form with '-a' marks a completed action by a third-person 'he'. The suffix '-kum' ('you' plural) is the object — the ones helped; its vowel is lengthened to '-kumu' to connect smoothly to the following word.
2.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support, grant victory

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: Places / locales / battlegrounds — sites where one stands, settles, or takes a position; by extension, fields of battle or theatres of action. Mawāṭin is the plural of mawṭin, a place of standing or abode.
5.grammar: A plural noun on the pattern mafāʿil. The final -a here serves as both the accusative and genitive marker because this is a 'diptote' broken-plural pattern: such nouns refuse nunation and use a single -a for both the object case and the 'of/after-preposition' case. The accusative marks it as a direct object; the same -a covers the genitive sense.
5.root: و-ط-ن (w-ṭ-n) — homeland, place of residence, where one settles

6.meaning: Many / numerous / abundant — great in number or quantity. Kathīra is the feminine form of the adjective 'much/many', describing a large amount of something.

parts.en: many / numerous (feminine; tā' marbūṭa surfaces as -t- before nunation)

6.grammar: A feminine singular adjective (the tā' marbūṭa marks feminine agreement, used also with broken plurals of non-human things); it is pronounced -t- here because nunation follows. The ending -in (nunation) is the indefinite genitive case: the genitive form follows a preposition or another noun, and the indefinite -in marks it as describing something general ('many') rather than a specific definite thing.
6.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — muchness, abundance, being numerous

7.meaning: And on the day (of) / and the day (of). The word for 'day' set as an adverb of time, joined by 'and'.
7.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the final -a, which here functions adverbially to mark a point in time ('on the day …'). The prefixed wa- means 'and'.
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a defined span of time

8.meaning: Ḥunayn — a proper name: the valley between Mecca and Ṭā'if, a site associated with a notable historical encounter. As a place-name it identifies a specific location.
8.grammar: A proper noun (a place-name). The ending -in (nunation) is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). Though a proper name, this particular word is treated as fully declinable and so carries nunation.

9.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
9.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

10.meaning: 'She pleased you / impressed you' — the verb 'to please, delight, impress' (to cause wonder or admiration), with a feminine subject acting upon a group of men.
10.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she did'), and the attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all (men)'. From form IV (aʿjaba), 'to please/impress someone' — literally to make someone wonder or admire.
10.root: ع-ج-ب (ʿ-j-b) — wonder, amazement; form IV: to please, impress

11.meaning: Your great number / your multitude / your abundance — the largeness of a group's numbers. Kathra is the noun for 'manyness', the quality of being numerous.

parts.en: multitude / large number (with tā' marbūṭa surfacing as -t- before the suffix)

11.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -kum ('your', addressing a group of males or a mixed group). Its feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is pronounced -t- here because a suffix follows. The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject of a sentence or the thing being named.
11.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — muchness, abundance, being numerous

12.meaning: A two-part device meaning 'did not …' — it combines 'and/then so' with a negating word that turns a present-tense verb into a flat statement that something did NOT happen in the past.
12.grammar: A connecting particle fa- ('and so / then') joined to the negative particle lam. Lam negates the past: it precedes a present-tense verb but flips its meaning to 'did not do', and it puts that following verb into the jussive (clipped) form.

13.meaning: It avails / it suffices / it does any good — to be of use, to satisfy a need, to spare one from want. Aghnā means to make sufficient or to free from need; in negative contexts it conveys 'to be of no avail'.

parts.en: it / you (does — Form IV prefix vowel)

13.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form IV, causative). The tu- prefix marks a third-person feminine 'it' (or a second-person 'you') as the doer. The stem ends in a bare -i (a shortened final weak letter), the form the verb takes in the jussive mood — typically after a negation meaning 'did not' or in conditions — giving the sense 'it does not avail / cannot suffice'.
13.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — sufficiency, freedom from need, richness

14.meaning: 'From you / off you' (addressing a group). The preposition 'ʿan' (denoting moving away from, or 'concerning') fused with a plural 'you'.
14.grammar: A preposition 'ʿan' with an attached pronoun object. 'ʿan' conveys moving away or off from something (and so pairs naturally with pardoning — lifting a fault away); the suffix '-kum' means a plural 'you'.

15.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
15.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
15.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

16.meaning: And it became narrow / straitened / constricted — to grow tight, cramped, or distressing. Ḍāqa describes space, or by extension the heart or circumstances, closing in and becoming oppressive.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and'). The suffix -t is the feminine singular ending, marking a third-person feminine subject ('she/it' did) — so the verb reports a completed action: 'it became narrow'.

17.meaning: 'Upon / over you (plural)' — the preposition 'on, over, upon' with an attached 'you all' pronoun, indicating something coming onto or directed at a group.
17.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -kum addresses a group ('you all'); the final -u (kumu) is a connecting helper-vowel easing the link into a following word that starts with the definite article. The preposition conveys 'on' or 'over'.

18.meaning: A noun meaning 'the earth', 'the ground', or 'the land' — the terrestrial world, the soil and land surface as opposed to the sky.
18.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The -u ending is nominative, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action). This noun is grammatically feminine.

19.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
19.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.
19.root: — (particle + relative pronoun)

20.meaning: It became wide / spacious / vast — to grow broad and roomy. Raḥuba is the opposite of constriction, describing ample, expansive space.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -t is the feminine singular ending, marking a third-person feminine subject ('she/it' did), so the verb reports a completed action: 'it grew wide / it was vast'.

21.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
21.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

22.meaning: You turned away / you turned your backs / you retreated — to wheel around and go back, to withdraw. Wallā means to turn and present one's back, often in the sense of fleeing or abandoning.
22.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form II) in the second person masculine plural. The suffix -tum means 'you all (did)', addressing a group of males or a mixed group, and reports a completed action: 'you all turned away'.
22.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to turn, to be near/adjacent, to take charge (here: to turn away)

23.meaning: Turning your backs / retreating / fleeing — those who are in the act of turning away and withdrawing. Mudbir is an active participle: one who turns his back and goes off.
23.grammar: An active participle (Form IV) — a 'doer' word formed with the mu- prefix, meaning 'one who turns his back'. The ending -īna is the masculine sound plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when such a plural is a direct object, follows a preposition, or describes the state in which someone does something ('while turning back').
23.root: د-ب-ر (d-b-r) — the back, hind part; to turn the back, to retreat

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: A past-tense verb meaning 'he sent down, he caused to descend, he revealed' — used especially of Allah sending down revelation, rain, or blessings from above.
2.grammar: A completed (past) action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the -a ending marks third-person masculine singular. The form IV (causative) pattern means 'to make something come down,' i.e., to send it down.
2.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — coming down, descending, alighting

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: His tranquillity / His calm reassurance — a settling peace and steadiness that descends upon the heart, removing fear and agitation. Sakīna is an Allah-given serenity and composure.

parts.en: tranquillity / serene calm (with tā' marbūṭa surfacing as -t- before the pronoun)

4.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hu ('his/its'). Its feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is pronounced -t- here because a suffix follows. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb — the thing that is given, sent down, or acted upon.
4.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — stillness, rest, calm, settling down

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

6.meaning: 'His Messenger' — a messenger or envoy, one sent with a message, here possessed by 'Him'.
6.grammar: A noun ('messenger') with the attached possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i ending before the pronoun is genitive, typically signalling that the word follows a preposition or is the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …'); the pronoun appears as -hi (rather than -hu) because of that preceding i vowel.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a sending, message, messenger

7.meaning: A two-part phrase: the joining word 'and' plus the preposition 'on / upon / incumbent upon,' often used to express an obligation resting on someone.
7.grammar: The connector 'wa' ('and') joined to the preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon'). Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending; a noun governed by 'ʿalā' takes the genitive.

8.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
8.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

9.meaning: 'And He sent down / caused to descend'. It denotes bringing something down from a higher place to a lower one — characteristically the sending down of revelation. Past tense, third person masculine singular.
9.grammar: 'wa-' is the connector 'and'. 'anzala' is a past-tense verb of the causative pattern (form IV) meaning 'to make descend / send down', with the third-person masculine singular subject ('he') built in; the final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending.
9.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down, send down

10.meaning: Forces / troops / hosts / armies — bodies of soldiers or assembled fighting forces. Junūd is the plural of jund, a marshalled host or army.
10.grammar: A plural noun. The ending -an (nunation, written with the alif) is the indefinite accusative case: the accusative marks it as a direct object (the thing sent or brought), and the indefinite -an signals 'forces' in a general, unspecified sense rather than particular, definite ones.
10.root: ج-ن-د (j-n-d) — a gathered host, troops, an army

11.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
11.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

12.meaning: You see it / you saw it — to perceive with the eyes, to behold. Ra'ā is the basic verb of visual sight (and, more broadly, of perceiving or considering).
12.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second person masculine plural with an attached object pronoun -hā ('it', feminine/non-human). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and (in the jussive mood, typically after a negation meaning 'did not') the plural lost its final -na, leaving the bare stem before the pronoun — giving the sense 'you (all) did not see it'.

13.meaning: And He punished / He chastised / He tormented — to inflict pain or penalty as retribution. ʿAdhdhaba (intensive form) conveys subjecting someone to suffering or punishment.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form II, intensive) with the prefixed conjunction wa- ('and'). With no subject suffix attached, it is third person masculine singular — 'he' is the doer — and the final -a is the standard past-tense ending, reporting a completed action: 'he punished'.

14.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
14.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

15.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

16.meaning: 'And that' — a connective 'and' plus the demonstrative 'that', pointing to something distant or already mentioned (masculine).
16.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'that (one)'. Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the -ka element is a particle directing attention to a distant referent.

17.meaning: 'The recompense / requital / due reward' — the fitting return given for a deed, whether reward or punishment.
17.grammar: A verbal noun, masculine singular. The -u ending is the nominative case, typical of a subject or predicate ('the recompense [is] …'). As a verbal noun it names the act of requiting and the requital itself, and it commonly heads an 'of' construction ('the recompense of …').
17.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — recompensing, requiting, repaying in kind

18.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth; the word also carries the sense of covering up or being ungrateful for what one has been given.
18.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. The stem is an active participle ('one who disbelieves/is ungrateful') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the accusative/genitive form of the sound masculine plural: it marks the word as an object of a verb or as governed by a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna.
18.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; ingratitude, disbelief

1.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
1.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

2.meaning: 'He/it turns in relenting / accepts repentance' — from tāba; of Allah it means He relents toward and accepts the return of a servant; of a person, he turns back to Allah.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix marks a masculine singular subject, 'he/it.' The final -u ending is the ordinary present-tense (indicative) marker, indicating an action that is happening or customary.
2.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

3.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
3.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

4.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
4.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

5.meaning: A noun/adverb meaning 'after' — the time or position following something; 'afterward', 'following'.
5.grammar: An adverb of time functioning as a noun, here in the genitive case marked by the final -i. The genitive ending typically appears after a preposition or as the second term of a construct ('after THE …'), linking 'after' to a following noun to specify what it comes after.
5.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — to be after, to follow, distance in place or time

6.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
6.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

7.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
7.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

8.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
8.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

9.meaning: A present-tense verb meaning 'he wills, he wishes, he chooses' — to want or intend something by one's own decision.
9.grammar: A present/ongoing action by a single masculine subject ('he'); the ya- prefix marks third-person masculine singular, and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('he wills'), as opposed to a command or a verb governed by 'that.'
9.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʾ) — willing, wishing; the root behind 'thing' (shayʾ)

10.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
10.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
10.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

11.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'much-forgiving, ever-ready to forgive, one who veils and pardons faults again and again'. The form stresses abundance, so it conveys forgiveness as a constant, far-reaching quality.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective (the ghafūr 'doer-in-abundance' pattern), used as a divine attribute of Allah. The -un ending is nunation in the nominative case: it marks the word as indefinite and in the nominative, the case typically used for the subject or for a predicate that describes the subject.
11.root: غ-ف-ر (gh-f-r) — to cover, veil, forgive

12.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
12.grammar: An intensive adjective on the form faʿīl ('abundantly/constantly merciful'). The ending -un (tanwīn) is the nominative case with indefiniteness, the form typically used for the subject of a sentence or a predicate describing it ('[He] is most merciful').

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
4.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

5.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — people who ascribe divinity, worship, or rights belonging to Allah alone to others alongside Him. From the verb meaning 'to make a partner/share,' it denotes idolaters or polytheists in general.
5.grammar: An active participle made plural: 'those who associate partners.' The definite article al- ('the') marks it as a known group. The -ūna ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — it marks the word as the doer/subject of a sentence, as opposed to the -īna form used for objects.
5.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner, associate

6.meaning: Ritual or physical impurity; filth, uncleanness. A noun naming a state of being unclean or defiling, the opposite of purity (ṭahāra).
6.grammar: A singular noun with the -un ending, which is nominative (subject case) and indefinite ('an impurity'). The doubled vowel (nunation/tanwīn) signals that the noun is indefinite — not 'the' particular thing, but 'a/some' instance of it.
6.root: ن-ج-س (n-j-s) — to be impure, unclean

7.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
7.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

8.meaning: They (should) draw near, approach, come close to something. From a verb expressing nearness in place or relation.
8.grammar: A present-tense (non-past) verb, third-person masculine plural: 'they draw near.' The ya- prefix marks third person, and the -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they'). The bare -ū form (without final -na) reflects the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after particles of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
8.root: ق-ر-ب (q-r-b) — to be near, draw close

9.meaning: A place of prostration; a mosque — the building or site where the act of bowing down in worship (sujūd) is performed.
9.grammar: A noun of place built on the pattern maf'il, naming the location where an action happens — here 'the place of prostration.' The definite article al- marks it as 'the.' The -a ending is accusative (object case): it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).

10.meaning: 'the forbidden / the sacred / the inviolable' — that which is set apart as holy and protected, so that violating it is prohibited. It applies to sacred places, months, and things whose sanctity must not be breached.
10.grammar: An adjective/noun carrying 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative; because the word already has 'the', it takes a plain -a (no 'n' sound). The accusative typically marks a direct object or describes such an object.
10.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to be forbidden, sacred, inviolable

11.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
11.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
11.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

12.meaning: Year — a span of a full year of time. The noun ʿām denotes a year, often emphasizing the cycle of seasons. Here it carries an attached pronoun marking whose year it is.
12.grammar: A noun with the possessive pronoun -him ('their') attached, so 'their year.' The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive ending: it typically links the word to a preceding preposition or makes it the second term of a possessive phrase ('… of …'). The pronoun ending -him refers to a masculine plural group ('them/their').
12.root: ع-و-م (ʿ-w-m) — a year, the turning cycle of time

13.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
13.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

14.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
14.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

15.meaning: 'You (all) feared,' 'you became afraid/apprehensive.' It states that a group experienced fear or wary concern in the past.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -tum marks the subject as second-person masculine plural, 'you all (did).' The hollow root's middle letter has dropped before the consonant ending, leaving the short stem khif- (compare khāfa, 'he feared').
15.root: خ-و-ف (kh-w-f) — to fear, be afraid, be in awe
