16.meaning: Poverty, need, destitution; the condition of having a large family or dependents to support and lacking the means. A noun naming want or financial hardship.
16.grammar: A feminine singular noun (marked by the tā' marbūṭa) with the -an ending: accusative (object case) and indefinite ('a poverty / want'). The doubled-vowel nunation (-an) shows the noun is indefinite, and the accusative case often marks it as an object or as the thing one fears or expects.
16.root: ع-ي-ل (ʿ-y-l) — to be poor, to have dependents to support

17.meaning: A two-part marker meaning 'then/so' plus 'shall/will.' It announces something forthcoming as a consequence: the particle sawfa points to the future, generally a more remote or emphatic future than the shorter prefix sa-.
17.grammar: A linking particle fa- ('then/so,' signalling result or sequence) joined to the future particle sawfa, which is placed before a present-tense verb to throw its action into the future ('will/shall …').

18.meaning: He enriches you / makes you free of need; bestows sufficiency so that one no longer depends on others. From a verb meaning to make wealthy or self-sufficient. The pronoun 'you (plural)' is attached as the one enriched.
18.grammar: A present-tense (non-past) verb in the causative (Form IV) pattern, third-person masculine singular: 'he enriches.' The yu- prefix marks 'he' and the causative shape ('to make rich'). The attached -kum(u) is the object pronoun 'you (plural)' — the ones being enriched; its vowel is lengthened to -kumu to ease pronunciation before the next word.
18.root: غ-ن-ي (gh-n-y) — to be rich, free of need, self-sufficient

19.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
19.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
19.root: — (proper divine name)

20.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
20.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

21.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
21.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
21.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

22.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
22.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

23.meaning: A past-tense verb 'he willed / he wished / he so desired'. It denotes an act of will or volition bringing something about.
23.grammar: Past-tense (perfect) verb, third person masculine singular ('he'). The bare stem with no suffix is the basic 'he did' form. Its subject and object are typically supplied by context.

24.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
24.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

25.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
25.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
25.root: — (proper name)

26.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
26.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.
26.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

27.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
27.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
27.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: Fight! / Do battle! — a command to engage in combat against an opponent. Form III implies mutual fighting (one party against another).
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb in Form III, addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you all.' Form III conveys reciprocal action — to fight against an opposing party.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

4.meaning: 'They believe / they have faith' — to affirm something as true with trusting inner conviction and to feel secure in it. The verb carries both believing and being at peace through that belief; in religious use it is to commit oneself in faith.
4.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, masculine plural. The yu-…-una frame means 'they (men, or a mixed group) do' the action now or habitually. The retained final -na marks the indicative (a plain, unqualified statement) — 'they believe' — as opposed to forms where that -na drops. The verb is Form IV (amana), used intransitively here meaning simply 'to believe / to have faith'.

5.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
5.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

6.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
6.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

7.meaning: The Day — a span of time; in religious usage it commonly points to the appointed Day (the Last Day, the Day of Resurrection and Judgment). The phrase reads 'in/by the Day.'
7.grammar: A preposition 'bi' (in/by) joined to the definite noun 'al-yawm' (the day). The noun is in the genitive case — shown by the final '-i' — because a noun following a preposition is regularly put in the genitive.
7.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day; a defined period of time

8.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the last,' 'the latter,' or 'the final' — that which comes at the end of a sequence. It is the common counterpart to 'the first,' and is often used as a name for the world or life to come (the Hereafter, the Last Day), i.e. the ultimate end of all things.
8.grammar: An active-participle-type adjective on the pattern fāʿil. It carries the definite article 'al-' ('the'). The final -i is the genitive case, signaling that the word is governed by a preceding preposition or particle, or stands as the second term of a possessive link ('… of …'). It is masculine singular.
8.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, to defer / postpone

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: They forbid / make unlawful; they declare something prohibited and sacred so that it may not be touched or done. From a verb meaning to render forbidden or inviolable.
10.grammar: A present-tense (non-past) verb in the intensive (Form II) pattern, third-person masculine plural: 'they make unlawful.' The doubled middle root letter gives the sense of actively/repeatedly declaring something forbidden. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood — the form used for a plain, ongoing statement.
10.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, make sacred/inviolable

11.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
11.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

12.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
12.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
14.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
14.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

15.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
15.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

16.meaning: They follow as a religion / hold as their way of life / render obedience and judgment by it. From a verb tied to religion, obedience, recompense, and submission to an authority or law.

parts.en: follow as religion, obey, hold as law

16.grammar: A present-tense (non-past) verb, third-person masculine plural: 'they take as religion / submit to.' The ya- prefix marks third person, and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement. The verb shares its root with the noun dīn ('religion, way, recompense').

17.meaning: Religion, way of life, creed; also the system of obedience, judgment, and recompense one lives by. A weighty term for the whole framework of belief, worship, and accountability before Allah, not merely 'a religion' in a casual sense.
17.grammar: A singular noun with the -a ending: accusative (object case), which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or the second term in certain constructions. The term itself denotes a complete way of life and the reckoning that goes with it.

18.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
18.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
18.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

19.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
19.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

20.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
20.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

21.meaning: They were given / granted — the passive past tense of the verb 'to give/bring' (form IV of ʾ-t-y), where a plural group receives something without the giver being named.
21.grammar: Passive past tense. The internal vowelling (u-...-u) marks it as passive — the subject receives the action rather than doing it. The '-ū' ending means 'they', giving 'they were given' (the giver left unmentioned).
21.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to bring or give

22.meaning: The Book, the Scripture — a written revelation; the term for a divinely revealed text.
22.grammar: A definite noun ('the Book') with attached 'al-' ('the'). The final '-a' ending is the accusative case, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb.
22.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write; a writing, book

23.meaning: 'Until / up to the point that; so that' — a particle marking a limit or goal. It expresses the end-point reached ('until') or the purpose aimed at ('so that, in order that').
23.grammar: A particle indicating a goal or limit. When followed by a present-tense verb it places that verb in the subjunctive mood (clipping its ending to -a), conveying 'until / so that' something comes about. Ḥattā itself is invariable.

24.meaning: They give, hand over, pay or render something to someone. From a verb meaning to bestow or deliver.
24.grammar: A present-tense (non-past) verb in the Form IV pattern, third-person masculine plural: 'they give / pay.' The yu- prefix marks 'they' (he-class), and the -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject. The bare -ū (without final -na) reflects the subjunctive/jussive mood, used after particles of purpose, condition, or negation.
24.root: ع-ط-و (ʿ-ṭ-w) — to give, grant, hand over

25.meaning: The jizya — a tribute or protection tax levied on non-Muslims living under Muslim rule, in exchange for protection and exemption from military service. A specific fiscal-legal term.
25.grammar: A feminine singular noun (marked by the tā' marbūṭa) with the definite article al- ('the') and the -a ending: accusative (object case), which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb — the thing being given or paid. The term is connected by root to the idea of compensation or what suffices in return.
25.root: ج-ز-ي (j-z-y) — to recompense, repay, suffice in return

26.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

26.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

27.meaning: Hand; also figuratively power, capacity, or direct personal agency. The noun yad literally means a hand, and by extension a means, control, or readiness.
27.grammar: A singular noun with the -in ending: genitive case and indefinite ('a hand'). The doubled-vowel nunation (-in) marks the noun as indefinite, and the genitive case typically follows a preposition or links the word to a preceding noun ('… of …'). The word's own stem is simply yad (one yā'); any doubling of the yā' heard in connected recitation is extrinsic — it results from a following word assimilating this word's tanwīn (idghām) and is not part of the noun's intrinsic form.
27.root: ي-د-ي (y-d-y) — hand; by extension power, means

28.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
28.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.

29.meaning: Those who are lowly, humbled, brought low; people in a state of submission and smallness. From a verb meaning to be small, low, or humbled.
29.grammar: An active participle made plural: 'those who are humbled / brought low.' The -ūna ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — it marks the word as the subject or as describing the state of the subject, rather than the -īna form used for objects.
29.root: ص-غ-ر (ṣ-gh-r) — to be small, low, humbled

1.meaning: And she said / and … said; the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense 'said' in the feminine form — reporting that a feminine (or grammatically feminine) subject spoke or stated something.

parts.en: she (feminine past marker), here read with -i

1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') + a past-tense verb 'said.' The -t is the feminine marker showing the subject is grammatically feminine ('she said'). This -t would normally be silent (-at), but here it is voiced as -ti to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting (un-pronounced) alif.

2.meaning: The Jews; the religious community of the Children of Israel known as the Yahūd — the people of Judaism, traditionally linked to Judah (Yahūdā) or to the idea of 'turning (back) (to Allah).'
2.grammar: A noun made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The -u ending is the nominative case, typically used when the noun is the subject of a sentence (the one doing the action) or what something is equated with.
2.root: ه-و-د (h-w-d) — to turn back, return, repent (the Yahūd, 'those who turned')

3.meaning: ʿUzayr — a proper name (commonly identified with Ezra), the name of a person. As a name it carries no lexical meaning, though its form is a diminutive shape.
3.grammar: A proper name with the -un ending, which is nominative (subject case) — marking it as the subject or topic of a statement. The doubled-vowel nunation appears because the name takes regular case endings; the diminutive pattern (fuʿayl) lends a sense of endearment or smallness inherent in the name itself.

4.meaning: 'Son' — a male child or descendant. It expresses the relationship of being the son of someone.
4.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or for a noun in apposition (a word that renames or further identifies another). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, normally elided after a preceding word, so it is read as 'bnu'. It is typically followed by the name of the father or parent ('son OF …').
4.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w/y) — son; to build (offspring as that which is built up)

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: And she said / and … said; the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense 'said' in the feminine form — reporting that a feminine (or grammatically feminine) subject spoke or stated something.

parts.en: she (feminine past marker), here read with -i

6.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') + a past-tense verb 'said.' The -t is the feminine marker showing the subject is grammatically feminine ('she said'). This -t would normally be silent (-at), but here it is voiced as -ti to ease pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting (un-pronounced) alif.
6.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

7.meaning: The Christians; the followers of Jesus (the Naṣārā). A plural noun used as the standard term for Christians as a community.
7.grammar: A plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'), assimilated in pronunciation to an-naṣārā because the n-sound absorbs the 'l.' Its ending is a fixed long -ā (an invariable plural pattern), so it does not take the usual short case vowels; the word stays the same whether subject or object.
7.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — to help, support (the name is linked to this root)

8.meaning: Al-Masīḥ, 'the Messiah / the Anointed One' — a title of the Prophet ʿĪsā (Jesus). It signifies one who is anointed or wiped over, traditionally linked to blessing and to his role of healing by touch.
8.grammar: A definite noun used as a title. The al- prefix means 'the', making it specific. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject of a sentence or for a noun identifying who or what something is. Masīḥ has the form of a passive participle ('one who is anointed/wiped').
8.root: م-س-ح (m-s-ḥ) — to wipe, anoint, stroke over

9.meaning: 'Son' — a male child or descendant. It expresses the relationship of being the son of someone.
9.grammar: A noun. The -u ending is nominative, the case used for the subject or for a noun in apposition (a word that renames or further identifies another). The initial alif is a connecting hamza, normally elided after a preceding word, so it is read as 'bnu'. It is typically followed by the name of the father or parent ('son OF …').
9.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w/y) — son; to build (offspring as that which is built up)

10.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
10.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

11.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
11.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

12.meaning: Their saying, statement, or word; what they say. The verbal noun qawl means an utterance or speech-act, here marked as belonging to a group.
12.grammar: A verbal noun ('saying / speech') with the possessive pronoun -hum ('their') attached, so 'their saying.' The -u vowel before the pronoun is the nominative ending: it typically marks the word as the subject or topic of a sentence. The pronoun -hum refers to a masculine plural group ('them/their').

13.meaning: With their mouths — by means of what they utter or speak aloud (often contrasted with what their hearts truly hold).
13.grammar: A noun preceded by 'bi-' ('with/by') with an attached possessive pronoun. 'Afwāh' is the broken (irregular) plural 'mouths.' The '-i' ending is genitive after the preposition 'bi-'; the suffix '-him' means 'their,' so the whole reads 'with their mouths.'

14.meaning: They liken / resemble / imitate; they make their speech or conduct resemble that of others. From a verb meaning to compare, match, or copy.
14.grammar: A present-tense (non-past) verb in the Form III pattern (which often carries the sense of doing something toward or matching another), third-person masculine plural: 'they imitate / resemble.' The yu- prefix marks 'they' (he-class), and the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject in the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement.
14.root: ض-ه-ي / ض-ه-أ (ḍ-h-y/ḍ-h-ʾ) — to resemble, imitate, compare

15.meaning: The saying, statement, or utterance — speech that is spoken; a word, remark, or what someone says.
15.grammar: A noun, 'saying/speech.' The final -a ending is the accusative case, which commonly marks the noun as the direct object — the thing the verb acts upon (e.g., what is heard, said, or known). This form names the act or product of speaking.
15.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak; an utterance

16.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
16.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

17.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
17.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
17.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
19.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
19.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

20.meaning: He fought against them / opposed them in battle; idiomatically used as an imprecation, 'may Allah destroy/curse them.' From a verb meaning to fight or wage war against. The pronoun 'them' is attached as the object.
20.grammar: A past-tense verb in the Form III pattern (mutual/directed action — 'to fight against'), third-person masculine singular: 'he fought against.' The final -a on the stem marks the simple past, 'he (did).' The attached -hum(u) is the object pronoun 'them' (masculine plural); its vowel is lengthened to -humu to ease pronunciation before the following word.
20.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, fight, wage war

21.meaning: Allah — the proper name of the One God: the sole, eternal Creator and Sustainer, unique and without partner, the object of all worship.
21.grammar: The unique proper name of the Deity (al-lāh, 'the God'). The final '-u' is the nominative case, the form typically used when the name is the subject of a sentence — the one performing the action.
21.root: — (a proper name; no triliteral root)

22.meaning: A particle/adverb meaning 'in whatever manner,' 'from wherever,' or 'whenever' — it asks or denotes the how, where, or when of an action in an open-ended way.
22.grammar: An invariable interrogative/conditional adverb; it has no case ending and never changes form. It introduces the manner, place, or time of an action in a general, open sense ('in what way / from where / when').
22.root: — (particle)

23.meaning: They are turned away / deluded — a passive verb meaning that people are diverted away from truth toward falsehood, made to deviate from what is right.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb in the passive voice — the u- prefix vowel with an a-vowel on the stem signals 'are being [acted upon]', so the subjects are the ones turned away, not the ones turning. The -ūna ending marks a 3rd-person masculine plural subject ('they') and the indicative mood (a plain statement). The sense is being led astray or deluded away from the truth.
23.root: ا-ف-ك (ʾ-f-k) — turning away, deviation, falsehood and deception

1.meaning: They took for themselves, adopted, acquired, or chose something. From a verb meaning to take or seize. The reflexive Form VIII shape adds the sense of taking for one's own benefit or making something into something.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb in the reflexive (Form VIII) pattern, third-person masculine plural: 'they took for themselves / adopted.' The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the past tense. The initial helping vowel i- and the doubled t belong to the Form VIII shape, which often gives the verb a self-directed sense ('to take for oneself').

2.meaning: Their rabbis / learned religious scholars; the recognized scholars and authorities, especially Jewish religious learned men. The plural of ḥabr/ḥibr, a scholar or doctor of religion. Marked here as belonging to a group.
2.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun, 'scholars/rabbis,' with the possessive pronoun -hum ('their') attached, so 'their scholars.' The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending: it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb — the ones being acted upon. The pronoun -hum refers to a masculine plural group.
2.root: ح-ب-ر (ḥ-b-r) — learning, scholarship; a learned man, ink

3.meaning: And their monks; devout religious ascetics who withdraw for worship (especially Christian monks). The plural of rāhib, one who lives in fear/awe of Allah and devotes himself to worship. Joined by 'and' and marked as belonging to a group.
3.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a plural noun, 'monks,' with the possessive pronoun -hum ('their') attached: 'and their monks.' The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as a direct object — the ones being acted upon. The pronoun -hum refers to a masculine plural group.
3.root: ر-ه-ب (r-h-b) — to fear, stand in awe; (hence) a monk/ascetic

4.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'lords' or 'masters' — those who own, command, sustain, and are obeyed; the plural of rabb. Used of beings wrongly set up as objects of obedience and devotion.
4.grammar: A plural noun. The final -an ending (written with the extra alif) is the indefinite accusative: the 'n' sound (tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('lords', not 'the lords'), and the accusative case typically marks a direct object of a verb or the second object of verbs like 'to take (X as Y)'.
4.root: ر-ب-ب (r-b-b) — to nurture, own, master; lordship

5.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
5.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

6.meaning: A noun used to mean 'besides', 'other than', 'apart from', or 'short of'. It points to something or someone set apart from, or lower/lesser than, a named party. Often used in the phrase 'besides Allah'.
6.grammar: 'dūn' functions as an adverb-like noun of place/relation. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, which appears because it follows a preposition (such as 'min', 'from') and because it links to a following noun ('other than …'). It commonly heads the construction 'besides/other than [someone]'.
6.root: د-و-ن (d-w-n) — to be low/beneath, to fall short; hence 'below, other than, besides'

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: And the Messiah; the Anointed One, a title of Jesus (al-Masīḥ). From a root meaning to wipe or anoint. Joined here by 'and.'
8.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') joined to a noun with the definite article al- ('the'): 'and the Messiah.' The -a ending is accusative (object case), which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb — the one being acted upon. The title is built on a pattern (fa'īl) often used for one upon whom an action is done, i.e. 'the anointed.'

9.meaning: "son" — a male child or descendant.
9.grammar: A noun beginning with a helping (elidable) vowel. The -a ending is accusative, which marks the word as the object of a verb or as an appositive describing a preceding accusative noun. When placed between two names, it functions as "son of …"

10.meaning: "Maryam" — the personal name Mary, the mother of the prophet Jesus.
10.grammar: A proper name (feminine, foreign origin). It is diptote: it takes no -n (nunation), and in the genitive and accusative it ends in -a rather than -i, so the -a ending shown serves for both object and "of" positions.

11.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
11.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
11.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

12.meaning: they were commanded / they were ordered — to be instructed or directed to do something. This is the passive: the doers received an order, with the commander left unnamed.
12.grammar: A past-tense passive Form I verb: the vowel pattern u–i ('umirū') shows it is passive ('were commanded'), so the subject is the one receiving the order. The suffix -ū is the masculine-plural subject ending ('they'), and the trailing alif is silent (alif al-wiqāyah).

13.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
13.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

14.meaning: So that they may worship / serve; to the end that they devote worship and obedience. From the verb 'to worship, serve, submit,' here prefixed with 'so that' to express purpose.
14.grammar: The purpose particle li- ('so that / in order to') attached to a present-tense verb, third-person masculine plural: 'so that they may worship.' The li- forces the subjunctive mood, which is why the ending is the bare -ū ('they') without final -na. The ya- prefix marks third person and the -ū marks a masculine plural subject.
14.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, submit as a devoted servant

15.meaning: 'A god / a deity, an object of worship' — the word in its indefinite form, naming a single divine being without specifying which.
15.grammar: A singular indefinite noun. The -an ending combines two things: the accusative case (the form for a verb's object or, often, a noun described by a following adjective) and nunation, the -n sound that signals 'a/an,' i.e. indefiniteness.
15.root: ء-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, that which is worshipped

16.meaning: 'And one / and single, sole' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the cardinal number one. The number 'one' stresses uniqueness and oneness, often attached to a preceding noun as a description. The opening waw carries a shadda because the conjunction 'wa' has merged with the initial w- of 'wāḥid.'
16.grammar: Conjunction 'wa' (and) prefixed to an adjective/number in the active-participle pattern; the doubled (shadda) waw represents 'wa' contracted onto the word's own initial w-. The -an ending is accusative plus nunation: it marks indefiniteness ('a/an' / 'one') and the accusative case, the form an adjective takes to agree with a noun it describes that is itself in the accusative.

17.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
17.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

18.meaning: God / object of worship — a deity that is worshipped. The bare noun names the concept of a worshipped god.
18.grammar: A singular noun carrying an -a ending. This short -a typically marks the accusative (object) case; it is also the form a noun takes immediately after the absolute-negation particle 'lā' to mean 'no … (at all).'
18.root: أ-ل-ه (ʾ-l-h) — godhood, worship, being a deity

19.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
19.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
19.root: — (particle)

20.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
20.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

21.meaning: An exclamation of glorification meaning 'far removed and utterly above all imperfection is He.' The verbal noun 'subḥān' declares that the One referred to is exalted beyond any deficiency, partner, or fault, and the attached 'Him' directs that declaration to a single masculine being.
21.grammar: A verbal noun used as an absolute exclamation, fixed in the accusative ending -a (an emphatic declaration, roughly 'I declare His utter transcendence'). The attached -hu is the possessive/object pronoun 'Him', referring to one masculine person.
21.root: س-ب-ح (s-b-ḥ) — to swim/glide away, hence to declare Allah free of all imperfection

22.meaning: 'About what' / 'of that which' — the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning, away from') merged with 'mā' ('what, that which').
22.grammar: A fusion of the preposition 'ʿan' ('about, concerning') with the relative/interrogative 'mā' ('what'); the 'n' of 'ʿan' assimilates into 'mā' to give 'ʿammā'. It introduces the thing being spoken about.

23.meaning: 'They associate (partners with Him)' — an ongoing/present verb. From the root for partnership, this form (causative, Form IV) means to make something a partner or associate, especially to set up partners alongside Allah in worship or divinity (the act underlying shirk).
23.grammar: A present/ongoing action. The yu- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a masculine plural 'they' doing the action now or habitually. The yu- prefix is the marker of Form IV (causative): 'to make (something) a partner.' The full -ūna ending signals the verb is in its ordinary (indicative) state, not cut short by a governing particle.
23.root: ش-ر-ك (sh-r-k) — to share, partner; (causative) to associate partners

1.meaning: they want / they intend — to will, desire, or purpose something. The verb conveys an active, ongoing intention or wish on the part of a group.
1.grammar: A present-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The yu- prefix marks a third-person subject, and the ending -ūna marks masculine plural plus the indicative mood (a plain statement: 'they want'). The -na would drop under a particle that changes the mood.

2.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
2.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
2.root: — (particle; no root)

3.meaning: To extinguish, put out, or quench a fire or light. The form expresses an action done by a plural subject ('they') to a source of light or flame.
3.grammar: A present/future-tense verb (causative Form IV) for a masculine plural subject, 'they extinguish' or 'they would extinguish.' The yu- prefix marks the third-person doer and the causative pattern (to cause to go out); the doubling (shaddah) on the prefix reflects assimilation of a preceding particle's final consonant into the verb. The -ū ending marks a masculine plural subject. The dropped final nūn signals the verb is governed by a particle of intent or negation ('that they may…' / 'they will not…').
3.root: ط-ف-أ (ṭ-f-ʾ) — extinguishing, putting out a fire or light

4.meaning: Light — radiance, illumination, brightness; the visible glow that dispels darkness, and by extension guidance and spiritual enlightenment.
4.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -a (accusative) ending typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb ('… the light') or shows it standing as the first term of a possessive phrase ('light OF …'), where the following owner takes the genitive.

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: With their mouths — by means of what they utter or speak aloud (often contrasted with what their hearts truly hold).
6.grammar: A noun preceded by 'bi-' ('with/by') with an attached possessive pronoun. 'Afwāh' is the broken (irregular) plural 'mouths.' The '-i' ending is genitive after the preposition 'bi-'; the suffix '-him' means 'their,' so the whole reads 'with their mouths.'
6.root: ف-و-ه (f-w-h) — mouth, opening; utterance

7.meaning: To refuse, decline, or be unwilling; to reject something and hold back from accepting or allowing it.
7.grammar: The wa- prefix is a connective ('and' or, in contrast, 'but'). What follows is a present/future-tense verb for a third-person masculine singular subject, 'he refuses' or 'he is unwilling.' The ya- prefix marks the 'he' doer; the verb ends in a long -ā (a defective root whose final weak letter appears as ālif), the standard present-tense shape of this verb.
7.root: أ-ب-ي (ʾ-b-y) — refusing, declining, being unwilling

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
10.root: — (particle; no root)

11.meaning: That he completes / brings to fullness — to carry something through to its end, perfecting and finishing it.
11.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'), on the causative pattern (form IV) — 'to bring to completion'. The yu- prefix marks 'he'; the final -a marks the subjunctive mood, used after particles like 'that' or 'so that'.
11.root: ت-م-م (t-m-m) — completion, fullness, perfection

12.meaning: His light — light or radiance belonging to a single male owner; brightness, illumination, and by extension guidance attributed to him.
12.grammar: A masculine singular noun, 'light,' with the attached pronoun -hu ('his/its') marking a single male possessor. The -a vowel on the noun (accusative) typically marks it as the direct object of a verb ('… his light'); the suffix -hu shows ownership.

13.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
13.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

14.meaning: He disliked, was averse to, or detested something — felt repugnance or unwillingness toward it.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I) on the pattern of verbs expressing an inner state. With no prefix and the bare '-a' ending, it carries its default meaning: a completed action by a single 'he' — 'he disliked / was averse.'

15.meaning: Definite plural noun/participle: 'the disbelievers, those who reject faith' — those who cover over and deny the truth. The pattern names a whole group defined by this attribute.
15.grammar: A definite active participle ('the rejecters'). The '-ūna' ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — the form a word takes when it is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence ('the disbelievers [are/do]…').
15.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover over, reject, disbelieve

1.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
1.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

2.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

3.meaning: To send, dispatch, or send forth — to commission someone or something and set it on its way toward a destination or purpose.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb (causative Form IV) for a third-person masculine singular subject: 'he sent' or 'he dispatched.' The a- prefix and the pattern give the causative sense (to cause to go / send off); the final -a is the standard 'he (did it)' past-tense ending.
3.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching, commissioning a messenger

4.meaning: His messenger — an envoy, emissary, or apostle belonging to a single male sender; one sent to deliver a message on his behalf.
4.grammar: A masculine singular noun, 'messenger,' with the attached pronoun -hu ('his') marking a single male owner/sender. The -a vowel (accusative) typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb ('… his messenger').
4.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending; a messenger is 'one who is sent'

5.meaning: A two-part expression meaning 'with/through the guidance'. It combines the preposition 'with/by means of' and the noun hudā — right guidance, the clear showing of the correct way and being led upon it.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to the definite noun al-hudā ('the guidance'). Because hudā ends in a fixed long vowel (a 'frozen' ending), its case does not visibly change after the preposition, though it stands in the genitive that bi- requires.
5.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — to guide, lead rightly, show the way

6.meaning: And religion — a way of life, system of belief, worship, and obedience owed to a higher authority; also recompense or the binding code one lives by. Dīn carries the sense of a complete path one is accountable to, not merely private belief.
6.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and,' joining this to what precedes. The noun 'religion' carries the -i (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the religion OF …') or follows a preposition or possessive construction.
6.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, way of life; obedience, recompense

7.meaning: 'The truth', 'the right', 'what is rightfully due' — that which is real, correct, and justly owed; the opposite of falsehood and wrongdoing.
7.grammar: A definite masculine noun (the al- prefix means 'the'). The -i ending is genitive, the case typically taken after a preposition or when the word links to a preceding noun ('… of the truth / by right').
7.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, rightness, that which is established and due

8.meaning: So that he may make it prevail, manifest it, or cause it to triumph and become dominant over all else.
8.grammar: The li- prefix means 'so that' or 'in order to,' expressing purpose. The verb is present-tense (causative Form IV) for a 'he' subject — to cause to appear, make manifest, or make victorious — and the purpose particle forces the special -a ending (subjunctive) heard as 'yuẓhira.' The attached -hu ('it/him') is the object being made to prevail.
8.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — appearing, becoming manifest; prevailing, gaining the upper hand

9.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
9.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
9.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

10.meaning: A term for 'the religion, the faith, the way of life and obedience owed to Allah'. It covers belief, worship, law, and the system of accountability and recompense — broader than the English word 'religion'.
10.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion'); the al- prefix means 'the'. The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …').
10.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, judgment, requital, obedience, debt

11.meaning: 'All of it / the whole of it' — a word denoting entirety or totality, here joined to a pronoun meaning 'it', giving 'the whole of it, every part of it'.
11.grammar: A noun meaning 'all/the totality', used in apposition for emphasis. It is in the genitive (the -i before the pronoun), the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link. The attached -hi is the pronoun 'it/his' ('all of it').
11.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — wholeness, totality, the sum of parts

12.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
12.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

13.meaning: He disliked, was averse to, or detested something — felt repugnance or unwillingness toward it.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb (Form I) on the pattern of verbs expressing an inner state. With no prefix and the bare '-a' ending, it carries its default meaning: a completed action by a single 'he' — 'he disliked / was averse.'

14.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — people who ascribe divinity, worship, or rights belonging to Allah alone to others alongside Him. From the verb meaning 'to make a partner/share,' it denotes idolaters or polytheists in general.
14.grammar: An active participle made plural: 'those who associate partners.' The definite article al- ('the') marks it as a known group. The -ūna ending is the masculine sound plural in the nominative (subject) case — it marks the word as the doer/subject of a sentence, as opposed to the -īna form used for objects.

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
4.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

5.meaning: An adjective/noun meaning 'many', 'much', or 'numerous' — a large quantity or great number of something.
5.grammar: Adjective/noun in the indefinite accusative, marked by the final -an (nunation with fatḥa). The accusative typically marks a verb's object or an indefinite quantity, and the doubled-n sound shows the word is indefinite ('many').
5.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be much, many, abundant

6.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
6.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

7.meaning: The learned scholars — religious authorities and teachers of scripture; the plural refers to a body of such learned men (often rendered 'rabbis' or scriptural scholars).
7.grammar: A masculine plural noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i (genitive) ending typically marks the word as following a preposition or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the scholars').
7.root: ح-ب-ر (ḥ-b-r) — a learned scholar; ink/learning, scholarship

8.meaning: And the monks — men devoted to ascetic religious life, withdrawn for worship and renunciation; the plural denotes such a class of devotees.
8.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and.' The definite article al- ('the') here assimilates into the following r-sound (heard as ar-ru). The -i (genitive) ending typically marks the noun as following a preposition or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the monks').
8.root: ر-ه-ب (r-h-b) — fear, awe, reverence; monastic devotion

9.meaning: They surely consume — they eat up, devour, or use up; with an emphatic 'surely/indeed' affirming that they certainly do so. Often extended to consuming wealth wrongfully.
9.grammar: The la- prefix is an emphatic 'surely, indeed,' stressing the truth of the statement. The verb is present/future-tense for a masculine plural subject, 'they eat/consume.' The ya- prefix marks the third-person doer; the -ūna ending marks an ongoing action by 'they' (masculine plural) in a complete, unrestricted clause.

10.meaning: Properties, possessions, wealth — the goods and assets a person owns. It is the plural of māl (money/property), denoting riches and material holdings in general.
10.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of māl, on the afʿāl pattern. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb. It lacks tanwīn here because it is the muḍāf — the first term of a possessive construction (iḍāfa) — and the first term of such a construction never carries tanwīn.
10.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, to have means

11.meaning: Humankind, people, mankind — the collective of human beings.
11.grammar: A collective noun ('people, mankind') carrying the definite article al- ('the'); the 'l' of the article assimilates into the following 'n', doubling it (al-nās → an-nās). The genitive ending -i marks the word as governed by a preposition or as the second term of a possessive.
11.root: ء-ن-س (ʾ-n-s) — humankind, sociability, familiarity; the word for 'people' is most commonly traced to this root (related to insān, 'human being')

12.meaning: With / by falsehood — 'the false, the vain, the baseless' joined to a preposition and 'the'.
12.grammar: The preposition bi- joined to the definite noun 'the falsehood' (an active participle meaning 'that which is null/vain'). The -i ending is the genitive, required because the noun follows the preposition.
12.root: ب-ط-ل (b-ṭ-l) — to be void, false, vain, of no effect

13.meaning: And they bar / turn (others) away — a present-tense verb of a group obstructing, hindering, or diverting people from a path or course.
13.grammar: A plain (form I) present-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they') and the -ūna specifically signals the indicative mood — a real, ongoing or habitual action ('they hinder / keep turning away').

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

14.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

15.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
15.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
15.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

16.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
16.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

17.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
17.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

18.meaning: They hoard, amass, and store up — to pile up and treasure wealth, keeping it withheld rather than putting it to use.
18.grammar: A present/future-tense verb for a masculine plural subject, 'they hoard' or 'they store up.' The ya- prefix marks the third-person doer; the -ūna ending marks an ongoing action by 'they' (masculine plural) in a complete, unrestricted clause.
18.root: ك-ن-ز (k-n-z) — hoarding, amassing and storing up treasure

19.meaning: Gold — the precious yellow metal, a measure of wealth and treasure.
19.grammar: A masculine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'); the article's l-sound assimilates into the following dh-sound (heard as adh-dhahab). The final -a (accusative) ending typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb ('… the gold').
19.root: ذ-ه-ب (dh-h-b) — gold; also going/departing

20.meaning: And silver — the precious white metal, a store of wealth and treasure alongside gold.
20.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and.' The noun 'silver' carries the definite article al- ('the'). The final -a (accusative) ending typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb ('… the silver').

21.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
21.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

22.meaning: They spend it — they pay it out, expend or disburse it; the action of giving wealth out, with 'it' referring to a feminine or collective thing spent.
22.grammar: A present/future-tense verb (causative Form IV) for a masculine plural subject, 'they spend.' The yu- prefix marks the third-person doer and causative pattern; the -ūna ending marks ongoing action by 'they' (masculine plural). The attached -hā ('it/them') is the feminine or collective object being spent.
22.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — spending, expending, disbursing wealth

23.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
23.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

24.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
24.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
24.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

25.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
25.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

26.meaning: Then give them glad tidings / then announce to them: a command to one person to bring news to a group, joined by 'then/so'. The verb's core sense is announcing news that visibly moves the hearer — usually good news, but the form can carry news of any kind.
26.grammar: A command (imperative) verb of the intensive pattern (Form II), addressed to a single person: 'announce / give tidings!'. The prefixed 'fa-' means 'then/so'. The attached -hum is the object pronoun 'them'.
26.root: ب-ش-ر (b-sh-r) — glad tidings; (the skin's) glow of joy

27.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
27.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

28.meaning: Painful / agonizing: causing intense pain; said of something that grieves and torments deeply. An intensive adjective, so 'sorely painful'. Indefinite ('a painful …').
28.grammar: An indefinite adjective on an intensive pattern (conveying 'deeply/sorely painful'). The ending -in shows both indefiniteness (the final -n, nunation: 'a painful one') and the genitive case (the -i vowel), the case that an adjective takes to match a genitive noun it describes or that follows a preposition.

1.meaning: Day — a span of time; frequently used to denote a momentous appointed Day, especially the Day of Resurrection and Judgment.
1.grammar: A noun ending in the accusative vowel -a. On a time-word like this the accusative commonly works adverbially to mean 'on the day (when…)' or 'on a day', setting the time-frame for an action.

2.meaning: It is heated — made hot, brought to a fierce, scorching heat; the form describes something being subjected to intense heating.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense passive verb for a third-person masculine singular subject, 'it is heated' or 'it is made hot.' The yu- prefix with the passive vowel pattern shows the subject receives the action rather than doing it; the long final -ā reflects the weak final root letter standing as ālif.
2.root: ح-م-ي (ḥ-m-y) — heat, becoming hot; protecting

3.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
3.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: Fire — blaze, flame; the burning element, and by extension the Fire of punishment.
5.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -i (genitive) ending typically marks the word as following a preposition (e.g. 'in / from the fire') or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the fire').
5.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — blazing, giving off light and heat; the source of fire and flame

6.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
6.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
6.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

7.meaning: Then they are branded — and so are seared or cauterized with it; the action of burning a mark onto flesh, presented as a consequence ('then…').
7.grammar: The fa- prefix means 'then' or 'so,' marking a result or sequence. The verb is present/future-tense passive for a feminine singular (or non-human plural) subject, 'it/they is/are branded' — the subject receives the searing. The tu- prefix with the passive vowel pattern marks the passive; the long final -ā reflects the weak final root letter standing as ālif.
7.root: ك-و-ي (k-w-y) — branding, searing, cauterizing with heat

8.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
8.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.

9.meaning: Their foreheads — the brows or fronts of the heads belonging to a group of males.
9.grammar: A plural noun, 'foreheads,' with the attached pronoun -hum ('their') for a masculine plural group of owners. The -u vowel on the noun (nominative) typically marks it as the subject or doer of its clause ('their foreheads [are…]').
9.root: ج-ب-ه (j-b-h) — forehead, brow; the front of something

10.meaning: And their sides — the flanks or lateral parts of the bodies belonging to a group of males.
10.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and.' The plural noun 'sides/flanks' carries the attached pronoun -hum ('their') for a masculine plural group. The -u vowel on the noun (nominative) typically marks it as the subject or doer of its clause.
10.root: ج-ن-ب (j-n-b) — side, flank; being adjacent, setting aside

11.meaning: And their backs — the rear parts or spines of the bodies belonging to a group of males.
11.grammar: The wa- prefix means 'and.' The plural noun 'backs' carries the attached pronoun -hum ('their') for a masculine plural group. The -u vowel on the noun (nominative) typically marks it as the subject or doer of its clause.
11.root: ظ-ه-ر (ẓ-h-r) — back, spine; appearing, being outward

12.meaning: 'This' — a pointing word (demonstrative) used for something near, masculine singular: 'this one (here).' It singles out a specific, present thing.
12.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun, masculine singular, for something near at hand ('this'). It is fixed in form and does not change for case. It points out a particular thing and can stand alone ('this') or precede a noun ('this X').

13.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
13.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

14.meaning: You hoarded — you amassed and stored up treasure; a completed act of piling up wealth done by a group being addressed ('you all').
14.grammar: A past-tense verb with the ending -tum, which marks the doer as 'you' — a masculine plural group being addressed: 'you (all) hoarded.' The suffix both identifies the subject and shows the action is completed.
14.root: ك-ن-ز (k-n-z) — hoarding, amassing and storing up treasure

15.meaning: For yourselves / for your own selves — the preposition li- ('for, to') with the plural noun anfus ('selves, souls') and the pronoun 'your', conveying benefit accruing to one's own persons.
15.grammar: The preposition li- ('for/to') governs the noun anfus, which therefore takes the genitive -i ending; the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', plural) is attached. The genitive is required because the noun follows the preposition li-.
15.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath, inner being

16.meaning: So taste! — a command to a group to 'taste' or experience something, often used figuratively of undergoing a consequence or punishment.
16.grammar: A command (imperative). The fa- prefix means 'so' or 'then', linking it to what precedes. The -ū ending directs the order to a masculine plural addressee ('you all'): 'so taste!'. The final silent alif is a spelling convention after this plural ending.

17.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
17.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

18.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
18.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
18.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

19.meaning: You hoard, amass, and store up — to pile up and treasure wealth, keeping it withheld; addressed to a group ('you all').
19.grammar: A present/future-tense verb for a masculine plural addressee, 'you (all) hoard.' The ta- prefix marks the second-person 'you' doer; the -ūna ending marks ongoing action by a masculine plural subject in a complete, unrestricted clause.
19.root: ك-ن-ز (k-n-z) — hoarding, amassing and storing up treasure

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: Number, count, or tally — the reckoned quantity or total of something; also a fixed reckoning or appointed amount.
2.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -a (accusative) ending typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or shows it standing as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the number OF …'), where the following noun takes the genitive.
2.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, numbering, reckoning a quantity
