3.meaning: "the months" — the plural of shahr (lunar month), made definite by the article so it refers to the months as a known, complete category.
3.grammar: A definite plural noun. The final -i is the genitive case: it typically marks the word as linked to a preceding noun ('… OF the months') or as following a preposition or oath particle. The article al- (assimilated as ash- before the sun-letter sh) makes it 'the months'.
3.root: ش-ه-ر (sh-h-r) — month, lunar/visible cycle; to make well-known

4.meaning: 'With / in the presence of / near' — an adverb of place and relation meaning at, by, in the sight or estimation of someone. It indicates nearness, possession, or what holds in someone's view (as in 'with Allah' = in His sight).
4.grammar: An adverb of place that is always followed by a noun it relates to. It carries a fixed -a ending; this accusative-type vowel is characteristic of such adverbs of place and shows the word is functioning to locate something ('at, near, in the presence of').

5.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
5.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

6.meaning: "two" — the first element of the compound number 'twelve' (ithnā ʿashar). On its own ithnā is the dual form meaning 'two', used as the base before 'ten' is added.
6.grammar: A dual noun ('two'). The -ā ending is the dual marker in the nominative (subject) state, the form used when 'two' functions as the subject or stands free. It pairs with a following 'ten' to express the number twelve.
6.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — two, doubling, to fold/double over

7.meaning: 'Ten' — the number ten; used as the second part of the compound number 'twelve' (literally 'two and ten').
7.grammar: The number 'ten' as it appears within a compound teen-number. In such compounds it stays in a fixed form with an unchanging -a ending regardless of grammatical role.
7.root: ع-ش-ر (ʿ-sh-r) — ten; relating to the number ten

8.meaning: "a month" — a single lunar month, in the indefinite singular. The accusative form here is the one used to specify the unit being counted after a number ('… months').
8.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case and the lack of 'the'; after numbers it functions as the counted noun ('… as months'), and more generally the accusative can mark an object or a specifying complement.
8.root: ش-ه-ر (sh-h-r) — month, lunar/visible cycle; to make well-known

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: A scripture or book; in particular a written revelation. The word denotes something written down and consigned to record — a 'Book' in the sense of a divinely sent, recorded scripture, also carrying the broader sense of a binding decree or anything set down in writing.
10.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The final -i ending is genitive (the 'of' case): it typically marks the word as linked to a following noun ('… OF …'), or as governed by a preceding preposition or oath particle.
10.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — writing, inscribing, recording

11.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
11.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

12.meaning: The noun 'day' — a span of time, often used for a momentous Day or appointed time; in the accusative it frequently functions as 'on the day (when…)', marking the time at which something occurs.
12.grammar: A masculine noun bearing the -a (accusative) ending. As an adverb of time this ending typically gives the sense 'on the day…', fixing the moment of an event.
12.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — day, a period of time

13.meaning: 'He created' — to bring into being, to originate and shape something that did not exist before, from the root denoting creation and the fashioning of things from nothing.
13.grammar: Past tense, third-person masculine singular ('he'), completed action ('he created'). This is a form I verb of the CaCaCa pattern. The masculine singular 'he' here is the unmarked (zero-suffix) form — there is no separate person ending; the final -a is the inherent stem vowel of the base pattern, not a person or tense suffix.

14.meaning: The heavens / the skies — the plural of 'heaven', referring to the skies above and the celestial realms; the elevated expanse over the earth.
14.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun with the prefix 'al-' ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF the heavens') or follows a preposition. In the sound feminine plural, this -i form also covers what would be an object role.

15.meaning: 'and the earth' — the ground, land, or the planet earth; the world we stand upon, often paired with the heavens to mean all of creation.
15.grammar: A feminine noun, prefixed with 'and' and 'the.' The -a ending is accusative, the case typically marking the object of a verb (the thing acted upon) or a noun governed by certain particles.
15.root: ا-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

16.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
16.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

17.meaning: "four" — the cardinal number four, in its feminine indefinite form.
17.grammar: An indefinite number-noun. The -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending marks the nominative case and the lack of 'the'; the nominative is the case used when a word serves as a subject or as the thing being asserted about. The -a (tā' marbūṭa) is the feminine form of the numeral.

18.meaning: 'in a state of ritual consecration' (plural) — describes pilgrims who have entered iḥrām, the sanctified condition during pilgrimage in which certain otherwise-lawful acts (like hunting) become forbidden. It can also describe the sacred precinct or sacred months in which such prohibitions hold.
18.grammar: A plural noun/adjective. The -un ending is nominative (the subject/predicate form) and the final 'n' sound (nunation) marks it as indefinite — 'consecrated ones' rather than 'the consecrated ones'.
18.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to be forbidden, sacred, inviolable

19.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
19.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

20.meaning: A noun, 'the dīn.' Dīn spans religion, faith, the way of life one follows in obedience, and also judgement, reckoning, and recompense — the system of accountability and devotion one lives by and answers to.
20.grammar: A definite noun marked by al- ('the'). The final -u is the nominative ending, which typically marks the word as the subject or main topic of a sentence (the one doing or being something).

21.meaning: "the upright/straight" — that which is firmly established, correct, and self-sustaining; an adjective describing something as true, standing, and properly ordered.
21.grammar: A definite adjective on the fayʿil (فَيْعِل) pattern from a hollow (wāw-medial) root: the wāw shifts to yā' and is inserted after the first radical, giving qayyim (compare sayyid from s-w-d) and conveying steadfast uprightness. The final -u is the nominative case, used for a subject or for a word describing a nominative noun. The article al- makes it definite ('the upright').
21.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, be upright; to establish/maintain

22.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
22.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

23.meaning: "you (plural) wrong / do injustice" — to put something out of its rightful place, to act unjustly or harm wrongfully. The bare stem expresses the act of committing injustice.
23.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd-person masculine plural. The ta- prefix signals 'you', and the -ū ending makes the subject plural ('you all'). The dropped final nūn (taẓlimū rather than taẓlimūna) shows the verb is in the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form taken after certain particles such as those of negation, prohibition, or purpose.
23.root: ظ-ل-م (ẓ-l-m) — injustice, wrongdoing, darkness; to put out of place

24.meaning: A small unit: the preposition 'in / within / during' joined to the attached pronoun 'them' referring to a group of feminine things.
24.grammar: 'fī' is the preposition 'in/within/during'. The attached -hinna is the object pronoun 'them' for a group of feminine items, so the whole means 'in/among them'. Pronouns attached to a preposition like this always take the genitive form.
24.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

25.meaning: 'Yourselves' — your own selves, persons, or souls. The base noun 'nafs' means the self, soul, or inner person.
25.grammar: A plural noun, 'selves,' with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('your,' addressed to a group). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative case, marking the word as the direct object — the thing being acted upon.
25.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, breath

26.meaning: And fight / do battle. A command to engage in combat. The verb is the mutual third-pattern form, implying fighting against an opposing party.
26.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to a second-person masculine plural ('you all'). It is the third (mutual/reciprocal) verb pattern, which conveys fighting against an adversary. The -ū ending marks the masculine-plural addressee; wa means 'and.'
26.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill; in this pattern, to fight, do battle

27.meaning: Those who associate partners with Allah — idolaters / polytheists who set up others alongside the one God in worship or devotion.
27.grammar: An active participle used as a noun, with 'the', in the masculine sound plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the genitive/accusative case — the form used after a preposition or as the object of a verb.

28.meaning: "all together, entirely, as a whole" — a term stressing totality and completeness: the whole group acting or being addressed without exception.
28.grammar: An indefinite noun used adverbially (a ḥāl/circumstantial). The -an ending (here written on the tā' marbūṭa as -tan) is the accusative, which is the case used for adverbs of manner describing how something is done — 'all together / in full'.
28.root: ك-ف-ف (k-f-f) — to restrain, hold back; (in this form) totality, all-encompassing

29.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
29.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

30.meaning: They fight you / they wage war against you. A present-tense verb of mutual combat with an object pronoun 'you (plural).'
30.grammar: A present-tense verb in the third (mutual) pattern, third-person masculine plural ('they…'). The yu- prefix (vowelled with a ḍamma, as the third pattern requires) signals a 'they' subject, and the -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the indicative (a stated, ongoing action). The attached -kum is the object pronoun 'you all.'
30.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill; in this pattern, to fight, do battle

31.meaning: "all together, entirely, as a whole" — a term stressing totality and completeness: the whole group acting or being addressed without exception.
31.grammar: An indefinite noun used adverbially (a ḥāl/circumstantial). The -an ending (here written on the tā' marbūṭa as -tan) is the accusative, which is the case used for adverbs of manner describing how something is done — 'all together / in full'.
31.root: ك-ف-ف (k-f-f) — to restrain, hold back; (in this form) totality, all-encompassing

32.meaning: And know! — the connector 'and' joined to a command to know, realize, or be aware of something. A direct summons to a group to take firm notice.
32.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a group. The ending -ū marks the masculine plural addressee ('you all, know!'). Prefixed with wa- ('and').

33.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
33.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

34.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
34.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

35.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
35.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

36.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

36.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: "the postponing / deferment" — the act of putting something off or shifting it to a later time; a delaying or intercalating. The verbal noun names the deed of delaying itself.
2.grammar: A definite verbal noun (the name of an action) on the faʿīl pattern. The final -u is the nominative case, the case used when the word is a subject or the thing being asserted. The article al- (assimilated as an- before the sun-letter n) makes it 'the postponing'.
2.root: ن-س-أ (n-s-') — to postpone, defer, delay

3.meaning: "an increase / addition" — an adding-on, an excess or augmentation beyond the original amount.
3.grammar: An indefinite verbal noun (the name of the act of increasing). The -un (tanwīn ḍamm) ending marks the nominative case and the absence of 'the'; the nominative is used for a subject or for the thing being asserted about. The -a (tā' marbūṭa) is a feminine/abstract-noun ending.
3.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, add, grow, exceed

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'disbelief' or 'rejection of faith' — the deliberate covering over or denial of truth and of Allah; from a root whose core sense is to cover or conceal.
5.grammar: A definite verbal noun ('the disbelief') with the definite article 'al-' and the genitive '-i' ending. The genitive case typically follows a preposition or links this noun to a preceding noun in an 'of/in' relationship. The original root sense is 'to cover', since disbelief covers or hides the truth.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to deny, disbelieve, be ungrateful

6.meaning: "he/it is led astray / is caused to err" — to be made to wander from the right path by an outside agent. The sense is passive: someone is led into error rather than straying on their own.
6.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, 3rd-person masculine singular. It is the passive of the transitive Form IV aḍalla ('to lead someone astray'), not of the intransitive Form I ḍalla ('to stray oneself'); the active yuḍillu ('he leads astray') becomes the passive yuḍallu ('he is led astray') through the yu-…-a- vowelling of the passive. The final -u indicates the indicative mood — the plain statement form used for an ongoing or general fact. The doubled lām reflects the geminate root.
6.root: ض-ل-ل (ḍ-l-l) — to stray, go astray, lose the way; error

7.meaning: By it, with it, through it; the preposition 'bi' (with/by means of) joined to a pronoun referring to something previously mentioned.
7.grammar: A preposition plus an attached third-person masculine singular pronoun ('it / him'). 'Bi' conveys instrument or means ('by means of it'); the pronoun takes the -i vowel because words governed by 'bi' stand in the genitive.
7.root: — (preposition with pronoun; no root)

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

10.meaning: "they make it lawful / permitted" — to treat something as ḥalāl, declaring or rendering it allowed. The verb is the causative 'to make permissible', with an object 'it' attached.
10.grammar: A present-tense causative verb (form IV), 3rd-person masculine plural, with an attached object pronoun. The -ūna ending means 'they (men)' and shows the indicative mood (the plain statement form, with its nūn intact). The suffix -hu means 'it / him' as the thing acted upon. The yu- prefix plus doubled lām belongs to the 'make/declare' (iḥlāl) pattern.
10.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful/loosed, to untie; permissibility

11.meaning: "a year" — a single year, in the indefinite singular. The accusative form is typically used to mark a span of time ('for a year / in a year').
11.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case and the lack of 'the'; for nouns of time the accusative commonly functions as an adverb of duration ('for a year'), and more generally it can mark a direct object.
11.root: ع-و-م (ʿ-w-m) — year; cycle (often linked to swimming/floating through a cycle of time)

12.meaning: "and they make it unlawful / forbidden" — and to treat something as ḥarām, declaring or rendering it prohibited. The verb is the intensive 'to forbid', with 'it' as its object and a joining 'and'.
12.grammar: A present-tense intensive verb (form II), 3rd-person masculine plural, with a prefixed 'and' and an attached object pronoun. The wa- means 'and'. The -ūna ending means 'they (men)' and marks the indicative mood (the plain statement form, nūn intact). The suffix -hu means 'it / him'. The doubled middle root letter (ḥarrim) gives the causative/intensive 'to render forbidden'.
12.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — to forbid, make sacred/inviolable; prohibition

13.meaning: "a year" — a single year, in the indefinite singular. The accusative form is typically used to mark a span of time ('for a year / in a year').
13.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The -an (tanwīn fatḥ) ending marks the accusative case and the lack of 'the'; for nouns of time the accusative commonly functions as an adverb of duration ('for a year'), and more generally it can mark a direct object.
13.root: ع-و-م (ʿ-w-m) — year; cycle (often linked to swimming/floating through a cycle of time)

14.meaning: "so that they may match / make (a number) tally" — to bring two things into correspondence or agreement, to make one figure align with another. The verb is the form III 'to bring into accord'.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb (form III, of mutual correspondence), 3rd-person masculine plural, preceded by the purpose particle li- ('so that, in order to'). Because of that particle the verb is subjunctive, so its final nūn drops and the ending is just -ū ('they, men'). The yu- prefix with the ā-after-first-radical pattern marks the form III sense of making one thing match another.
14.root: و-ط-أ (w-ṭ-') — to tread, set foot; (form III) to make level with, bring into correspondence

15.meaning: Number, count, or tally — the reckoned quantity or total of something; also a fixed reckoning or appointed amount.
15.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -a (accusative) ending typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb, or shows it standing as the first term of a possessive phrase ('the number OF …'), where the following noun takes the genitive.
15.root: ع-د-د (ʿ-d-d) — counting, numbering, reckoning a quantity

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
17.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'

18.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
18.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

19.meaning: "so they make lawful / so they permit" — and as a result to render something ḥalāl. The verb is the causative 'to make permissible', here following a connecting 'so/then'.
19.grammar: A present-tense causative verb (form IV), 3rd-person masculine plural, with a prefixed fa- ('so, then', marking a consequence). The verb is in the subjunctive (carrying over from a preceding purpose particle), so the final nūn is dropped, leaving -ū ('they, men'). The yu- prefix plus doubled lām belongs to the 'make/declare lawful' pattern.
19.root: ح-ل-ل (ḥ-l-l) — to be lawful/loosed, to untie; permissibility

20.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
20.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

21.meaning: 'He forbade / made unlawful / declared sacredly off-limits.' To prohibit something firmly, to render it ḥarām — barred and inviolable, set outside what is permitted.
21.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) Form II verb, third-person masculine singular: 'he [did it],' a completed past action. The doubled middle root letter (Form II) gives an intensive/causative force — 'to make something forbidden/inviolable.'
21.root: ح-ر-م (ḥ-r-m) — prohibition, sacredness, inviolability

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
22.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
22.root: — (proper divine name)

23.meaning: It was made beautiful / adorned / made alluring; the act of decorating something or making it appear attractive and appealing.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice on an intensive (form II) pattern, so the action is done to the subject and stresses thorough adorning ("was made beautiful/alluring"). The -u-…-i- vowel pattern marks the passive, and the final -a ending marks a third-person masculine singular subject ("it/he").

24.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
24.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

25.meaning: "evil / badness of" — that which is bad, harmful, or offensive; the wrongness or foulness of a thing. In the construct form it means 'the evil of …'.
25.grammar: A noun meaning 'evil/badness'. The final -u is the nominative case, the case used for a subject or for the thing being asserted. The bare (non-tanwīn) ending shows it is in a construct (possessive) chain, leaning on a following noun: 'the evil OF …'.
25.root: س-و-أ (s-w-') — to be bad, to harm, to do evil; that which displeases

26.meaning: "their deeds / their works" — the actions and doings of a group; the plural of ʿamal (deed) joined to the pronoun 'their'.
26.grammar: A broken-plural noun with an attached possessive pronoun. The -i ending is genitive, the case used when a noun is possessed (in a construct chain) or follows a preposition. The suffix -him means 'their' (referring to a group of males or mixed group); its vowel is i to harmonize with the preceding genitive -i.
26.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deed

27.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
27.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
27.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

28.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
28.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

29.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
29.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
29.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

30.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
30.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
30.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

31.meaning: 'The disbelievers / those who reject faith' — also 'those who cover up or are ungrateful.' It names people characterized by rejecting the truth and concealing or denying it, in contrast to those who believe.
31.grammar: A definite plural noun: the prefix al- means 'the,' and the -īna ending marks a masculine 'sound' plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state — the form used when the word is an object of a verb or follows a preposition, as opposed to the subject form -ūna. It denotes many male persons (or a mixed group) of this description.
31.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to disbelieve, reject, be ungrateful

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
5.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

6.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
6.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.
6.root: — (a time particle; no triliteral root)

7.meaning: 'It was said' — speech was uttered or a statement was made. The passive form: the saying is reported without naming who spoke.

parts.en: was said (passive verb stem of the root q-w-l)
he/it (default short vowel of the 3rd masc. sg. past)

7.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice (pattern qīla) from the hollow root ق-و-ل. The passive is formed by internal vowel change: the middle radical (wāw) is replaced by a long 'ī', which marks the verb as passive (the doer is left unnamed). The lām is the third root letter, not an ending; the final -a is simply the default short vowel of the third-person masculine singular past, here used impersonally as 'it was said'.
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — saying, speech, utterance

8.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something is done or given.
8.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). Such prepositions assign a benefit, purpose, or recipient. The pronoun's vowel appears as '-u' (kumu) to ease pronunciation when a word follows.

9.meaning: 'Go forth!', 'march out!', 'mobilize!' — a command to a group to set out and advance, especially rushing out for an undertaking such as battle.
9.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending addresses a plural masculine 'you' (more than one person). The initial 'i-' is a helping vowel that allows the word to be pronounced. Force: 'all of you, march out!'
9.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — going forth, rushing out, mobilizing

10.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
10.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
10.root: — (particle)

11.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
11.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.
11.root: س-ب-ل (s-b-l) — way, path, road

12.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
12.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

13.meaning: "you (plural) became weighed down / sluggish, you clung heavily to the ground" — to feel heavy and reluctant, sinking down rather than setting out. The verb conveys a self-induced heaviness or holding back.
13.grammar: A past-tense reflexive verb (form VI, with its initial prosthetic alif and assimilated tā', originally tathāqala). The -tum suffix marks the subject as 2nd-person masculine plural ('you all') and the past tense (a completed action). The form VI pattern gives the sense of becoming or making oneself heavy/sluggish.
13.root: ث-ق-ل (th-q-l) — to be heavy, weighty; burden

14.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
14.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

15.meaning: The earth; the land, ground, or soil. The world we walk upon, as opposed to the sky.
15.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the definite article al- ('the'). The -i ending marks the genitive case, which typically links the word to a preceding noun ('... of the earth') or follows a preposition (as after 'in / on the earth').
15.root: أ-ر-ض (ʾ-r-ḍ) — earth, land, ground

16.meaning: "are you (plural) content / well-pleased?" — to be satisfied and willingly accepting of something. The opening alif turns it into a question: 'have you become pleased?'.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb, 2nd-person masculine plural, prefixed with the interrogative hamza a- ('…?'). The -tum suffix marks 'you all' and the past tense (a completed state of being pleased). The leading a- is the question particle, equivalent to turning the statement into 'Are you …?'.
16.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w/y) — to be pleased, satisfied, content; good pleasure

17.meaning: "with / by the life" — the noun ḥayāh (life, living existence) made definite and governed by the preposition 'with/in'.
17.grammar: A definite noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/in/by'). Because a preposition precedes it, the noun is in the genitive case, shown by the -i ending (here -ti on the tā' marbūṭa). The article al- makes it 'the life', and bi- links it as 'with the life'.
17.root: ح-ي-ي / ح-ي-و (ḥ-y-y/w) — to live, be alive; life

18.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
18.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
18.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

19.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
19.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

20.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
20.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
20.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

21.meaning: A two-part expression: 'so/then' joined to a negating word 'not.' The first piece links to what precedes (drawing a result or sequence), and the second negates the statement that follows. Together roughly: 'so… not / and so it did not…'
21.grammar: A connective particle fa- ('so, then,' showing result or sequence) plus the negating particle mā. When mā precedes a past-tense verb, it denies that the action happened ('did not…').

22.meaning: Provision, enjoyment, or the goods of life — something one is given to use and take comfort in for a time; often implies a temporary benefit or worldly furnishing rather than a lasting possession.
22.grammar: A masculine noun, indefinite. The final -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for a word standing as the predicate ('it is …'). The absence of nunation (-un) here reflects that it is bound to a following noun in a possessive ('… of …') construction.
22.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — enjoyment, benefit, provision

23.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
23.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.

24.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
24.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
24.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

25.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
25.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
25.root: — (particle)

26.meaning: The Hereafter — the final, lasting life that comes after death and the present world; literally 'the last/latter (abode or life)', as opposed to the first, nearer life.
26.grammar: A feminine adjective used as a noun, with 'the'. The -i ending is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… OF …'), or follows a preposition or oath particle.
26.root: ء-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — to be last, to come after, end

27.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
27.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

28.meaning: 'Few', 'little', 'a small amount/number'. Describes something scant in quantity — a small group of people or a small portion of a thing.
28.grammar: A descriptive adjective (or noun). The '-un' ending is the nominative case with nunation ('tanwīn'), marking it as indefinite ('a few', not 'the few'); the nominative typically marks the subject or a predicate.

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: "you (plural) march out / set forth" — to go out and mobilize, to advance for a purpose (often a campaign or expedition). The verb expresses moving out together.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb, 2nd-person masculine plural. The ta- prefix signals 'you', and the -ū ending makes the subject plural ('you all'). The dropped final nūn (tanfirū rather than tanfirūna) shows the subjunctive/jussive mood — the form taken after particles of negation, prohibition, condition, or purpose.
2.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to flee, startle, rush forth; to mobilize for a march

3.meaning: "he/He will punish you (plural)" — to inflict chastisement or torment. The verb is the intensive 'to punish severely', with 'you all' attached as its object.
3.grammar: A present-tense intensive verb (form II), 3rd-person masculine singular, with an attached object pronoun. The yu- prefix means 'he'. The verb stem ends in a vowelless (sukūn) state, the mark of the jussive mood — the clipped form used after conditional or commanding particles. The suffix -kum means 'you all' as the ones acted upon. The doubled middle root letter gives the intensive 'to punish'.

4.meaning: 'A punishment / torment.' A noun naming chastisement or painful suffering inflicted as a penalty.
4.grammar: A masculine noun. The -an ending marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the object of a verb or as the thing being described/quantified.

5.meaning: 'Painful / agonizing' — causing intense pain; an adjective describing something that hurts severely, e.g. a grievous, tormenting affliction.
5.grammar: An adjective of the intensive faʿīl pattern ('intensely painful'). The ending -an is accusative and indefinite, the case typically marking a verb's object or a describing word that agrees with such a noun; the final -n (tanwīn) marks indefiniteness.
5.root: أ-ل-م (ʾ-l-m) — pain, to ache, to hurt

6.meaning: "and he/He will substitute / exchange" — and to put one thing in place of another. The verb is the form X 'to replace', here joined by 'and'.
6.grammar: A present-tense verb (form X, the 'seeking/effecting' pattern with its ista- core), 3rd-person masculine singular, prefixed with 'and'. The wa- means 'and' and ya- means 'he'. The stem ends in a vowelless (sukūn) state, marking the jussive mood — the clipped form used after conditional or commanding particles. Form X here carries the sense of bringing about a replacement.
6.root: ب-د-ل (b-d-l) — to change, exchange, substitute; a replacement

7.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
7.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

8.meaning: "other than you / a people other than you" — ghayr expresses 'other-than, different from, not'; with 'you all' attached it means 'others besides you'.
8.grammar: The noun ghayr ('other-than'), used to negate or exclude, with an attached pronoun. The -a ending is the accusative case, used for a direct object or a similar complement. The suffix -kum means 'you all', so the whole means 'other-than-you / others besides you'.

9.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
9.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

10.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) harm/damage/injure Him,' with an attached object pronoun referring to a singular male (Allah). It conveys the act of inflicting hurt or detriment upon someone.
10.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, 2nd person masculine plural, in the indicative mood. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks 'you all (men)' as the doer. The final nūn of the indicative ending (-ūna in 'taḍurrūna') drops here purely because an object pronoun is attached directly to the verb — an obligatory morphophonological rule, not a change of mood. The final -hu is an attached object pronoun, 'him/Him.'
10.root: ض-ر-ر (ḍ-r-r) — harm, damage, detriment

11.meaning: A thing; something or anything. With a negation it commonly amounts to 'nothing at all.'
11.grammar: A singular masculine noun, indefinite ('a thing'). The -an ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative, often used here as an object or an adverbial 'in any respect / at all.'
11.root: ش-ي-أ (sh-y-ʾ) — thing, to will

12.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
12.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
12.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

13.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
13.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

14.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
14.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

15.meaning: 'a thing' — anything that exists or can be conceived, an entity or matter in the most general sense. It is the broadest Arabic word for 'something,' covering objects, affairs, and abstractions alike.
15.grammar: An indefinite singular noun. The '-in' ending (tanwīn al-kasr) signals two things at once: indefiniteness ('a thing,' not 'the thing') and the genitive case, marking it as following a preposition or completing a possessive link to a preceding noun.
15.root: ش-ي-ء (sh-y-ʼ) — to will, to be a thing/existent

16.meaning: All-powerful, fully able, ever-capable — possessing complete and effective power to do whatever is willed; one whose ability never falls short.
16.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, which stresses a deep, abiding quality ('thoroughly able'). The final -un is the indefinite nominative (nunation) — the doubled-n shows no 'the', and the -u base vowel marks the nominative case, used when the word is a subject or a predicate ('… is all-powerful').

1.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
1.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'you (plural) help/aid/support/grant victory to him.' It denotes coming to someone's assistance, especially backing them against an adversary.
2.grammar: An imperfect (present/future) verb, 2nd person masculine plural, in the indicative mood. The ta- prefix with the -ū ending marks 'you all (men)' as the doer. The final nūn of the indicative ending (-ūna in 'tanṣurūna') drops here purely because an object pronoun is attached directly to the verb — an obligatory morphophonological rule, not a change of mood. The final -hu is an attached object pronoun, 'him.'
2.root: ن-ص-ر (n-ṣ-r) — help, victory, support

3.meaning: A two-part connector: fa- means 'so', 'then', or 'and so', linking what follows as a result or consequence; qad before a past-tense verb intensifies it, conveying 'certainly', 'indeed', or 'already' — stressing that the action has truly and definitely occurred.
3.grammar: fa- is a connecting particle meaning 'so' or 'then', often marking a result. qad is a particle of emphasis; placed before a completed (past-tense) verb it affirms that the action has definitely or already happened. Neither part takes a case ending.

4.meaning: A verb meaning 'He helped him / granted him victory,' a completed act of one party (singular male) aiding another against an opponent.
4.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb, 3rd person masculine singular: the bare stem with the final -a marks 'he' as the doer of a completed action. The attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him,' so the form means 'he helped him.'

5.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
5.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
5.root: — (proper divine name)

6.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

7.meaning: A verb meaning 'he drove him out / expelled him / caused him to come out,' the act of forcing or bringing someone (singular male) to leave a place.
7.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern 'akhraja,' 3rd person masculine singular. The a- prefix turns the root sense 'to go out' into 'to make/bring out.' The final -a marks 'he' as the doer of a completed action, and the attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him': 'he brought/drove him out.'
7.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — going out, exit, emergence

8.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
8.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

9.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

10.meaning: An active participle/noun meaning 'second' or 'one of two / the second of two.' In the construct 'thānī ithnayn' it describes someone who is the second member of a pair.
10.grammar: An active participle from the root for 'two,' functioning as a noun/adjective ('second, one of a pair'). The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks a word as a direct object, or as a circumstantial description ('being the second of...'), or after certain particles.
10.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — two, doubling, repeating

11.meaning: Two; the cardinal number 2 (in its masculine dual form), denoting a matched pair.
11.grammar: The number 'two' in dual form. The '-ayni' ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive case — the shape used when the word is an object or follows a preposition. The initial 'i' is a helping vowel (a 'connecting hamza') that smooths pronunciation.
11.root: ث-ن-ي (th-n-y) — twoness, doubling, a second of a pair

12.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
12.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

13.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'they two / both of them' — the dual third-person pronoun referring to exactly two persons or things.
13.grammar: A detached (independent) personal pronoun, 3rd person dual. The -mā ending specifically marks duality (exactly two). It can stand alone as a subject ('they two') or attach to nouns, verbs, or prepositions to mean 'their (two)' or 'them two.'

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: A noun meaning 'the cave' — a hollow or cavern in a mountain or rock, a sheltered recess.
15.grammar: A definite singular noun ('the cave'); al- is the definite article 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or oath particle, or as being possessed by a preceding noun ('... of ...').
15.root: غ-و-ر (gh-w-r) — hollow, depression, sinking in

16.meaning: A particle meaning 'when' or 'at the time that', used to point back to a past moment or event and introduce a recollection of something that occurred.
16.grammar: An indeclinable particle (it has no case ending and never changes form). It signals a point in past time, typically introducing a clause that recalls 'the time when' something happened.

17.meaning: 'He says' or 'he is saying' — the act of speaking or uttering words. The imperfect tense conveys an ongoing, habitual, or present/future action.
17.grammar: Imperfect (present/future) verb, third person masculine singular. The ya- prefix marks 'he', the stem qūl carries the meaning 'say', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling a plain factual statement (as opposed to a subjunctive -a or jussive sukūn used after certain particles).

18.meaning: A phrase meaning 'to his companion / for his companion,' where the companion is one who accompanies, befriends, or keeps company with someone (singular male owner).
18.grammar: A noun with a prefixed preposition and an attached possessive pronoun. The prefix li- means 'to/for.' 'Ṣāḥib' is an active participle used as a noun, 'companion.' The -i ending is genitive, required because the word follows the preposition li-. The attached -hi means 'his,' so the whole means 'to/for his companion.'

19.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
19.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

20.meaning: A verb meaning 'do not grieve / feel no sorrow' — to be saddened, anxious, or sorrowful. In a prohibition it tells someone (singular male) not to be distressed.
20.grammar: An imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, in the jussive mood (shown by the silent/sukūn ending on the final consonant rather than a vowel). This jussive form is the one used after the prohibitive particle 'lā' to express 'do not...,' i.e., a command not to grieve. The ta- prefix marks 'you (one man)' as the addressee.

21.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
21.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

22.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
22.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
22.root: — (proper name)

23.meaning: A phrase meaning '(is) with us' — expressing accompaniment, presence alongside, or support of a group ('us').
23.grammar: An adverb/particle of accompaniment 'maʿa' ('with, together with') with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'). The -nā suffix is the 1st person plural object/possessive pronoun. Together it states togetherness or presence: 'with us.'

24.meaning: A verb meaning 'and/then he sent down / caused to descend,' the act of bringing something down from a higher place (often used of revelation, rain, or aid descending from Allah).
24.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb of the causative (Form IV) pattern 'anzala,' 3rd person masculine singular, prefixed with the connector fa- ('so/then'). The a- prefix turns 'to descend' into 'to send/bring down.' The final -a marks 'he' as the doer of a completed action: 'so He sent down.'
24.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — descending, coming down, alighting

25.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
25.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
25.root: — (proper divine name)

26.meaning: His tranquillity / His calm reassurance — a settling peace and steadiness that descends upon the heart, removing fear and agitation. Sakīna is an Allah-given serenity and composure.

parts.en: tranquillity / serene calm (with tā' marbūṭa surfacing as -t- before the pronoun)

26.grammar: A noun with the attached pronoun -hu ('his/its'). Its feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is pronounced -t- here because a suffix follows. The -a vowel before the pronoun is the accusative case, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb — the thing that is given, sent down, or acted upon.
26.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — stillness, rest, calm, settling down

27.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
27.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

28.meaning: A verb meaning 'and he strengthened/supported/reinforced him,' the act of backing someone (singular male) and bolstering them with strength or aid.
28.grammar: A perfect (past-tense) verb of the intensive (Form II) pattern 'ayyada,' 3rd person masculine singular, with the connector wa- ('and'). The doubled middle consonant gives the sense of firmly strengthening or reinforcing. The final -a marks 'he' as the doer; the attached -hu is the object pronoun 'him': 'and He strengthened him.'

29.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with troops / forces / armies' — 'junūd' is the plural of 'soldiers,' denoting military hosts or massed forces.
29.grammar: A plural noun with the prefixed preposition bi- ('with, by means of'). 'Junūd' is the broken plural of 'jund' (a body of soldiers). The ending -in is genitive case with tanwīn (nunation): the genitive is required after bi-, and the tanwīn marks the noun as indefinite ('some forces / forces').

30.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
30.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

31.meaning: You see it / you saw it — to perceive with the eyes, to behold. Ra'ā is the basic verb of visual sight (and, more broadly, of perceiving or considering).
31.grammar: A present-tense verb in the second person masculine plural with an attached object pronoun -hā ('it', feminine/non-human). The ta- prefix marks 'you', and (in the jussive mood, typically after a negation meaning 'did not') the plural lost its final -na, leaving the bare stem before the pronoun — giving the sense 'you (all) did not see it'.

32.meaning: 'And he made / appointed / rendered' — the connector 'and' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to make something into something, to fashion or appoint it. It can mean to create, to assign, or to cause a thing to become a certain way.
32.grammar: The connective wa- ('and') prefixed to a past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare verb with its final -a vowel denotes a completed act by a third-person masculine singular subject ('he made/did').
32.root: ج-ع-ل (j-ʿ-l) — to make, render, appoint, place

33.meaning: A noun meaning 'word, utterance, statement,' or by extension a 'cause,' 'message,' or 'decree' expressed in words.
33.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final -a is the accusative case ending, which typically marks the word as a direct object of a verb, or as otherwise grammatically governed into the accusative. The 't' of the feminine ending (tā' marbūṭa) is pronounced here because a case vowel follows it.

34.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
34.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

35.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
35.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
35.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

36.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the lowest / lowermost,' the feminine form denoting that which is beneath or inferior in rank or position.
36.grammar: A definite feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the lowest'), on the 'fuʿlā' pattern that pairs with the masculine 'asfal.' The only internal boundary is al- (the definite article 'the') plus the inseparable stem 'suflā'; 'suf' and 'lā' are not separate morphemes. The word ends in a fixed 'alif maqṣūra' (-ā), an unchanging ending typical of feminine superlatives, so it does not take the usual short case vowels.
36.root: س-ف-ل (s-f-l) — lowness, being beneath, the bottom

37.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and the word / and the utterance,' joining a noun meaning 'word, statement, decree' to what precedes.
37.grammar: A feminine singular noun with the connector wa- ('and'). The final -u is the nominative case ending, which typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the topic about which something is stated. The feminine 't' is voiced here because a case vowel follows it.

38.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
38.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

39.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
39.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

40.meaning: An adjective meaning 'the highest / uppermost / supreme,' the feminine form denoting that which is above or superior in rank or position.
40.grammar: A definite feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the highest'), on the 'fuʿlā' pattern that pairs with the masculine 'aʿlā.' al- is the definite article 'the,' attached to the inseparable stem 'ʿulyā.' The word ends in a fixed 'alif maqṣūra' (-ā), an unchanging ending typical of feminine superlatives, so it does not take the usual short case vowels.

41.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
41.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
41.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

42.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
42.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").

43.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
43.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
43.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: A command verb meaning 'go forth! / march out! / set out (to fight or on an expedition)!' — to mobilize and move out, especially for a campaign.
1.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a masculine plural group, 'you all.' The -ū ending marks the plural addressees (the silent alif after it is merely a spelling convention). It directs a group to mobilize and march out.
1.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — going forth, mobilizing, rushing out

2.meaning: An adjective meaning 'light (in weight or burden), unencumbered, lightly equipped,' the plural describing people who are nimble, free of heavy load, or easily able to move.
2.grammar: A plural adjective (broken plural of 'khafīf,' 'light'). The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (nunation). The accusative here typically marks a circumstantial state — describing the manner or condition in which people act ('being light / lightly equipped') — and the tanwīn shows it is indefinite.
2.root: خ-ف-ف (kh-f-f) — lightness, being light in weight

3.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and/or heavy ones' — an adjective for that which is heavy, weighty, or burdened, the plural describing people who are heavily laden or weighed down.
3.grammar: A plural adjective (broken plural of 'thaqīl,' 'heavy') with the connector wa- ('and/or'). The ending -an is the accusative case with tanwīn (nunation). The accusative here typically marks a circumstantial state ('being heavy / heavily laden'), paired as a contrast with 'light'; the tanwīn shows it is indefinite.

4.meaning: A command verb meaning 'and strive! / struggle! / exert yourselves to the utmost (including in fighting for a cause)!' — to expend maximum effort against an obstacle or enemy.
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb of the mutual-effort (Form III) pattern 'jāhada,' addressed to a masculine plural group, with the connector wa- ('and'). The Form III pattern conveys exerting oneself strenuously against something. The -ū ending marks the plural addressees 'you all' (the trailing alif is a spelling convention).

5.meaning: A phrase meaning 'with your wealth/property.' It combines 'with/by means of,' the plural noun for goods and possessions, and a 'your' (plural) possessor.
5.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with, by means of') governs the noun, which therefore takes the genitive case-vowel -i (the ending always required after a preposition). The noun is a 'broken' plural of māl ('wealth'). The suffix -kum means 'your' for a group of males or a mixed group.
5.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, possessions

6.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and your selves / your own persons / your lives' — 'anfus' is the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person), here belonging to 'you' (plural).
6.grammar: A plural noun with the connector wa- ('and') and an attached possessive pronoun. 'Anfus' is the broken plural of 'nafs' (self/soul). The -i ending is genitive case; the attached -kum ('your,' for a group of men) is a possessor pronoun, and a noun owned by such a pronoun stands in the genitive: 'and your selves/lives.'
6.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person, breath

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
8.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

9.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
9.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

10.meaning: A demonstrative meaning 'that' addressed to a group of people (plural 'you'). It points to something at a distance — whether physical, or to a previously mentioned matter — and is directed at multiple listeners.
10.grammar: A demonstrative pronoun for something distant. The base 'dhā' carries the sense 'that', the 'li' is an element of distance, and the ending '-kum' tells you the speaker is addressing a plural 'you' — it specifies the audience, not the thing pointed at. It does not change for case.

11.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
