3.meaning: You (plural) wait and watch expectantly, biding your time to see how a matter will turn out — often with the sense of lying in wait for an outcome to befall someone.

parts.en: wait / lie in wait (form V stem)

3.grammar: A present-tense form V verb for a plural 'you'. Form V verbs (the tafaʻʻala pattern) carry an inherent ta- inside the stem itself (tarabbaṣ), so the second-person plural is marked jointly by the outer ta- prefix together with the -ū suffix — not by ta- alone. The -ū marks a masculine plural subject and the final -na is the indicative marker, signalling an ongoing or habitual action (a plain statement, not a command or a negated/subjunctive form). The doubled middle consonant of form V adds a sense of deliberate, sustained waiting.
3.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, watch, lie in wait for an outcome

4.meaning: A particle 'with/for/by' joined to the word 'us'. It signals accompaniment, means, or that something concerns or befalls 'us'.
4.grammar: The preposition bi- always attaches to the front of a noun or pronoun and puts it in the genitive. Here it is fused with the attached pronoun -nā ('us'), the first-person plural object. The bi- can convey 'with', 'by means of', or that an event happens 'to/concerning' the people named.

5.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
5.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: One (feminine) of two, a single one out of a pair or group. The feminine counterpart used when counting or singling out one item among others.
6.grammar: The feminine form of the number 'one', used to single out one female/feminine item from a set. It is invariable in shape here (its ending does not change for case) and characteristically precedes the group it selects from ('one OF …').
6.root: و-ح-د (w-ḥ-d) — oneness, unity, singularity; being one.

7.meaning: The two best things — a dual form naming a pair of most-excellent or finest outcomes, the superlative 'best' counted as two.
7.grammar: A definite dual noun. The al- means 'the'. The base ḥusnā is the feminine superlative 'best/finest'; its final ā contracts to -ay- before the dual suffix, and the oblique dual ending -ayni (here -yayni after that stem) marks exactly two and is the form used when the word is an object or follows a preposition (the oblique dual case). So the whole word means 'the two best (outcomes)'.
7.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — beauty, goodness, excellence

8.meaning: 'And we' — the standalone pronoun 'we' (a group including the speaker), prefixed with the connector 'and'; often used to set up a contrast ('while we…').
8.grammar: A detached subject pronoun meaning 'we,' here introduced by wa- ('and' / 'while'). As an independent pronoun it stands on its own (not attached to a verb) and is invariable — it is fixed in form and takes no case ending that changes.

9.meaning: We wait expectantly, watching for an outcome to unfold — keeping vigil over how a matter will resolve.

parts.en: wait / lie in wait (form V stem)

9.grammar: A present-tense form V verb with the na- prefix meaning 'we'. The final -u is the indicative ending, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement of what 'we' do (as opposed to a wish or a negated form, which would change that vowel). The doubled middle consonant of form V conveys deliberate, sustained waiting.
9.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, watch, lie in wait for an outcome

10.meaning: A preposition 'bi' ('with / by / in / for') joined to the attached pronoun 'you all', yielding 'with you' or 'for you (plural)'. The exact shade — attachment, instrument, or benefit — depends on the verb it accompanies.
10.grammar: A preposition plus an attached pronoun. 'bi' is a versatile preposition (with, by, in, for), and -kum is the genitive/object pronoun 'you all' (masculine plural). Pronouns following a preposition always take this attached (genitive) form.
10.root: — (preposition; no root)

11.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
11.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
11.root: — (particle; no root)

12.meaning: He strikes/afflicts you (plural) — to hit a target, reach someone, or have something (good or ill) befall them.
12.grammar: A present-tense verb with the yu- prefix for 'he/it' (form IV, 'to cause to hit/afflict'). The stem-vowel ending is -a (subjunctive), the mood used after certain particles meaning 'that', 'so that', or 'lest' — it points to an action as intended, expected, or contingent rather than a flat fact. Attached -kum(u) is the plural object 'you'; its vowel is lengthened to -kumu to ease into the next word.
12.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — to hit the mark, be right, befall

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: With/of a punishment: 'with' joined to a word for a chastisement, torment, or penalty inflicted as recompense; indefinite ('a punishment').
14.grammar: An indefinite noun with the prefixed preposition 'bi-' ('with / of'). The ending -in does two things: the final -n (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a punishment'), and the -i vowel is the genitive case required after the preposition 'bi-'.

15.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
15.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

16.meaning: His presence, His keeping, that which is 'with' Him or proceeds from Him. 'ʿind' denotes being at, near, or in the possession of someone; with the 'His' pronoun it points to what lies in Allah's own keeping or comes from Him.
16.grammar: An adverb of place ('with, in the presence of') joined to the possessive pronoun -hi ('his/him'). The -i vowel before the pronoun reflects the genitive state — the form this word takes after a preposition or when bound to what precedes it; -hi names the one in whose presence something is.
16.root: ع-ن-د (ʿ-n-d) — being at, near, or in the keeping of

17.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
17.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

18.meaning: A particle 'with/by' joined to 'our hands' — denoting agency or means, literally 'by our hands'.
18.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attaches to a noun and makes it genitive. The noun aydī is the broken (irregular) plural 'hands'; its long final -ī is the genitive form a plural like this takes after a preposition. The attached -nā is the possessive 'our'. Together: 'by our hands', expressing the means or doer of an act.

19.meaning: Then wait / then await / then watch and bide your time — a command to expect an outcome, holding back to see what comes. Tarabbaṣa is to wait expectantly, sometimes warily, for something to unfold.
19.grammar: A command (imperative) verb (Form V) addressed to a group of males or a mixed group, prefixed by fa- ('then/so'), which links it to what precedes as a consequence. The plural-command ending -ū means 'you all, do this!' — so it directs a group to wait. (The written alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention.)
19.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, lie in wait, watch for an outcome

20.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
20.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

21.meaning: An expression meaning 'with you' — combining the word for accompaniment, togetherness, or presence-alongside with the attached pronoun 'you' (a group). It signals being in the company of, or on the side of, the addressed people.
21.grammar: An adverb of accompaniment (maʿa, 'with/in the company of') carrying the attached pronoun -kum ('you,' for a group of males). It expresses togetherness or being alongside the people addressed.

22.meaning: Ones who wait and watch — people in the act of biding their time, lying in wait to see how something turns out.
22.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) of form V, built with the mu- prefix and the -i- vowel before the last consonant, meaning 'ones who wait/watch'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural subject in the nominative — the case used when such a word is the doer or the thing being described. It names the people as habitual waiters, not a one-time act.
22.root: ر-ب-ص (r-b-ṣ) — to wait, watch, lie in wait for an outcome

1.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
1.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

2.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'spend!' — give out or expend wealth, resources, or provisions. The verb often carries the nuance of charitable or purposeful giving, releasing what one has for a cause or for others.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb. The -ū ending marks a masculine-plural addressee: 'you all, do this.' Built on Form IV (the af'ala pattern), which here gives the sense of expending or paying out from one's wealth.
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out (of wealth)

3.meaning: 'Willingly, obediently, of one's own accord' — acting out of voluntary compliance and submission rather than compulsion.
3.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The -an ending (with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) is the accusative, here describing the manner of an action — 'willingly, in a state of compliance.'

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: A noun used adverbially meaning 'by force, against one's will, under compulsion / with reluctance,' i.e., something done unwillingly or imposed.
5.grammar: A verbal noun. The final -an (tanwīn fatḥa) is the indefinite accusative; on a noun like this it functions adverbially, describing the manner or circumstance of an action ('forcibly,' 'reluctantly').
5.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — disliking, aversion, compulsion

6.meaning: A particle of strong negation directed at the future: 'never; will not at all.' It emphatically denies that something will ever happen and puts the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive.
6.grammar: A negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb, denying it for the future and forcing that verb into the subjunctive mood (so the verb takes a final '-a' instead of '-u'). It has no ending of its own.

7.meaning: It is accepted / received favorably — passive of 'to accept', as when an offering, deed, or plea is graciously received and approved.
7.grammar: A present-tense passive verb (form V) with the yu- prefix; the vowel pattern marks it as 'is being accepted' rather than 'accepts'. The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after particles like 'that' or 'so that' — presenting the acceptance as intended or hoped-for rather than as a bare fact. Form V here adds the nuance of graciously, willingly receiving.
7.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, face toward

8.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
8.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
8.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

9.meaning: 'Indeed you (plural)' — the emphatic particle inna ('truly, indeed, surely'), which strongly affirms and stresses the statement that follows, fused with the attached pronoun 'you (all)'. Inna has no single English word; it functions to underline certainty.
9.grammar: Inna is an emphasising particle that introduces and strengthens a sentence; grammatically it places the following noun or pronoun in the accusative-like role of its 'subject'. The attached -kum is the masculine plural object/possessive pronoun 'you (all)'. Together: 'indeed you (all)…'.

10.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
10.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
10.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

11.meaning: 'A people, a folk, a community' — a group of human beings bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared standing.
11.grammar: An indefinite collective noun. The -an ending (accusative with tanwīn, the 'n' sound) marks it as the object of an action.
11.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group, people

12.meaning: Ones who break out of obedience — those who deviate from the right path and rebel against what is due to Allah; morally corrupt, defiantly disobedient people.

parts.en: rebel against obedience / morally corrupt one

12.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) naming people characterized by fisq — willfully stepping outside obedience to Allah. The -īna ending marks a masculine plural in the oblique case (the form used as an object or after a preposition). The picture is of those who knowingly break free from the bounds of right conduct.
12.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to break away from obedience, deviate, act corruptly

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He prevented/withheld them — to bar, deny, hold back, or stop someone from something.
2.grammar: A simple past-tense verb. The form manaʻa is the complete past verb for 'he/it', a finished act — its final -a is the verb's own third-person-masculine-singular vowel, not a detachable suffix. The attached -hum is the masculine plural object pronoun, 'them'. The verb conveys denying access or holding something back from the people named.
2.root: م-ن-ع (m-n-ʻ) — to prevent, withhold, deny, protect

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'It is/will be accepted; it is received favourably' — said of something taken in, approved, and granted acceptance (often used of deeds, repentance, or offerings being accepted by Allah).

parts.en: she/it (3rd person feminine singular present prefix)

4.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, 3rd person feminine singular ('it/she is accepted'). The 'tu-' prefix simply marks a 3rd person feminine present subject and is shared by active and passive alike; what makes the verb passive is the internal vowel pattern (ḍamma on the first radical, fatḥa on the one before last), giving 'is accepted' rather than 'accepts'. The final '-a' is the subjunctive ending, which appears when the verb follows certain particles (such as a future-negation or purpose particle).
4.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to accept, receive, turn toward

5.meaning: From them / among them — the preposition min ('from, out of, part of') joined to the pronoun 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group).
5.grammar: The preposition min ('from / among / part of') with the attached third-person masculine plural pronoun -hum ('them'). Pronouns after a preposition are in the genitive; the combination expresses origin, partition ('some of them'), or belonging to that group.
5.root: — (preposition with pronoun, no root)

6.meaning: Their expenditures/contributions — the sums or things one spends or gives out, here marked as belonging to them.
6.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt marks plural) meaning 'amounts spent / contributions', with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The short -u before the pronoun is the nominative case, the form a noun takes when it is the subject or doer of a sentence. The root sense is wealth that is paid out or disbursed.
6.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, disburse

7.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
7.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
8.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

9.meaning: 'They disbelieved / rejected faith' — from a root meaning to cover over or conceal. To disbelieve in this sense is to cover up and refuse the truth, and also to be ungrateful, hiding or denying favours received.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb in the third person masculine plural: 'they disbelieved'. The completed action is built into the stem kafara ('he disbelieved'), and the -ū suffix (written وا) marks the doer as 'they' (masculine plural). The silent alif written after the -ū is a spelling convention with no sound.
9.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to reject faith, be ungrateful

10.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
10.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
10.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

11.meaning: 'And in/by His Messenger' — the conjunction 'and', plus a particle 'in/by', plus the noun 'messenger' carrying the possessive 'His'. A messenger is one sent with a commission to convey something.
11.grammar: Several pieces joined: wa- ('and') links it to what precedes; bi- ('in/by') is a preposition that puts its noun in the genitive. The noun rasūl ('messenger, one sent') therefore takes the -i genitive ending, and the attached -hi is the possessive 'His'. A rasūl is specifically an envoy entrusted with a message to deliver.
11.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message, one who is sent

12.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
12.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

13.meaning: They come / they approach — to arrive at or come to a place or person; also figuratively to do or bring about a thing.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb for a masculine plural 'they'. The ya- prefix marks third-person, the long -ū carries the plural subject 'they', and the final -na is the indicative marker showing a plain ongoing or habitual action (not a command or a negated form). Core sense: to come, arrive, or bring something about.

14.meaning: The ritual prayer (ṣalāh): the prescribed formal worship of standing, bowing, and prostrating before Allah at appointed times. As a verbal noun it also carries the underlying sense of calling upon, supplicating, and blessing.
14.grammar: A definite feminine noun. The -a ending is accusative: it generally marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing being acted upon, e.g. that which is established or performed), or the object of certain particles.

15.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
15.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
15.root: — (particle)

16.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
16.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

17.meaning: Sluggish, lazy, listless — describing people who are heavy and reluctant, dragging themselves to an action without energy or eagerness.
17.grammar: A plural adjective (the broken-plural pattern fuʿālā) meaning 'lazy / sluggish ones,' describing a group. It ends in a fixed long -ā (alif maqṣūra) and does not take the usual changing case-vowels — its form stays the same whether subject, object, or possessive. It typically functions as a state-descriptor: 'while sluggish / lazily.'

18.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
18.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

19.meaning: 'They spend/give out': to expend wealth or provision, especially by giving it away in charity and in good causes. The word centers on disbursing what one has rather than hoarding it.
19.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form IV (anfaqa, 'to spend, expend'). The imperfect prefix is only yu-; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ف-ق), not part of the prefix. The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default 'plain' form used for ongoing or repeated action.
19.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out

20.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
20.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

21.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
21.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

22.meaning: An active participle (a doer-noun) meaning 'ones who dislike / are averse / find something hateful' — people who feel reluctance or aversion toward something.
22.grammar: An active participle in the masculine plural, naming those who carry out the action: 'those who dislike'. The -ūna ending marks the masculine plural in the nominative case, which is typically used for the subject or for a predicate describing the subject.
22.root: ك-ر-ه (k-r-h) — to dislike, be averse, find hateful

1.meaning: A two-part word: the connective particle 'fa-' meaning 'so', 'then', or 'therefore' (drawing a consequence from what precedes), joined to 'lā', the particle of negation/prohibition. Together they convey 'so do not …' or 'so there is no …'.
1.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that links a clause to what came before and often signals a result or consequence. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a present-tense verb it commonly forms a prohibition ('do not …') or a simple negation ('not'). It carries no ending of its own.

2.meaning: It pleases/impresses you (singular) — to delight, dazzle, or fill someone with admiration and wonder.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb (form IV, 'to cause wonder/delight') with the tu- prefix agreeing with a feminine 'it/she'. The stem ends with no vowel (jussive form), which is what happens after certain conditional or negating particles. The attached -ka is the singular masculine object 'you'. It describes something striking the onlooker with admiration.
2.root: ع-ج-ب (ʻ-j-b) — to wonder, marvel; to amaze, please

3.meaning: Their wealth / their possessions. The base noun amwāl is the plural of māl, meaning property, wealth, goods, or money — anything owned of value. With the attached pronoun it means 'their wealth'.
3.grammar: A plural noun with the -u (nominative) ending, which generally marks it as the subject of a sentence or a predicate. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group, grammatically masculine plural) when joined to a noun.
3.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property, to be wealthy

4.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
4.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

5.meaning: Their children / their offspring. The base noun awlād is the plural of walad, meaning a child or offspring (son or, broadly, descendant). With the attached pronoun it means 'their children'.
5.grammar: A plural noun with the -u (nominative) ending, generally marking it as a subject or predicate. The attached pronoun -hum means 'their' (a group, grammatically masculine plural) when joined to a noun.
5.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth, beget; hence child, offspring

6.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
6.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

7.meaning: He/it wills, wants, intends, desires — to seek or aim at something purposefully.
7.grammar: A present-tense (form IV) verb, third-person masculine singular ('he wills/wants'). The ya- prefix marks 'he', and the final -u is the indicative ending, signalling an ongoing or habitual action ('does / is doing').
7.root: ر-و-د (r-w-d) — to seek, to want; (form IV) to will/intend

8.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
8.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

9.meaning: So that He may punish them / chastise them. A purpose construction built on a verb meaning to inflict severe, deliberate punishment or torment, intensified to convey repeated or thorough chastisement.
9.grammar: The prefix li- ('so that') puts the present-tense verb into the subjunctive, shown by the final -a on yuʿadhdhiba; it expresses purpose ('in order that…'). The yu- prefix marks third-person masculine singular ('He'), and the doubled middle letter marks the intensive form. The attached -hum means 'them' (masculine plural object).

10.meaning: with it / by it — a preposition meaning 'with' or 'by means of' joined to a pronoun referring to a single feminine (or grammatically feminine) thing.
10.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition meaning 'with', 'by', or 'by means of'. The attached -hā is an object pronoun meaning 'it' or 'her', referring to something feminine in gender. Together they mean 'with it' or 'by means of it'.
10.root: — (preposition with pronoun)

11.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
11.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
11.root: — (particle)

12.meaning: 'The life' — living existence, the state of being alive.
12.grammar: The definite article al- with the feminine noun ḥayāt ('life'); the waw belongs to the stem and the tā' marbūṭa is its feminine suffix. The final -i is the genitive case vowel, which typically marks the word as following a preposition or standing in an 'of' relationship to a following noun.

13.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
13.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
13.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

14.meaning: 'And it departs/perishes' — the conjunction 'and' with a verb meaning a soul or life goes out, slips away, and is destroyed.
14.grammar: The wa- ('and') links this to what precedes. The verb is present-tense with the ta- prefix agreeing with a feminine 'it/she' (fitting a 'soul', which is feminine). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, used after particles like 'so that' or 'until' — framing the departing as a purpose or expected result rather than a plain fact. The sense is a life-breath going out and being extinguished.
14.root: ز-ه-ق (z-h-q) — to depart, vanish, perish; (of a soul) to expire

15.meaning: Their own selves / their souls — the plural of "self" (the inner person, soul, or very being) joined to "their." It points to people's own selves, their lives, or their inner beings.
15.grammar: Plural noun "selves/souls" with the -u ending, which is nominative, typically marking the word as the subject or doer in a sentence. The attached -hum means "their," so the whole is "their selves."
15.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — soul, self, breath; the inner self and life-essence of a person

16.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
16.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

17.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers: those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle names people characterized by ungrateful rejection of what should be acknowledged.
17.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate (as opposed to -īna for object/genitive).
17.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: 'And they swear' — the conjunction 'and' with a verb meaning to take an oath, to vow solemnly that something is true.
1.grammar: The wa- means 'and'. The verb is present-tense: the ya- prefix marks third-person, the long -ū carries the masculine plural subject 'they', and the final -na is the indicative marker for a plain ongoing or habitual action. The verb means to bind oneself by a solemn oath.
1.root: ح-ل-ف (ḥ-l-f) — to swear, take an oath

2.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
2.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
2.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

3.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
3.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

4.meaning: An emphatic 'surely/indeed' joined to 'from you (plural)' — affirming strongly that someone belongs to or comes from a group ('truly of you').
4.grammar: Three pieces: the prefixed la- is an emphasizing particle that stresses the truth of a statement ('surely, indeed'). The preposition min means 'from / of / among' and governs a genitive. The attached -kum is the plural 'you'. Together it strongly affirms membership: 'truly among/of you'.

5.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
5.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.
5.root: — (relative pronoun / particle)

6.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
6.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

7.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
7.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.
7.root: — (preposition with pronoun; no root)

8.meaning: 'But/however they…' — a contrastive particle that corrects or sets against what was just said, here joined to the conjunction 'and' and the pronoun 'they'.
8.grammar: The wa- ('and') joins this to the previous clause. Lākinna is a contrastive particle meaning 'but/however', used to overturn or qualify a preceding statement; it ends in its own inherent -a (fatḥa). Like its sister inna, it grammatically takes a following noun or pronoun as its 'ism' in the accusative. The attached -hum ('they/them') is that accusative ism — the semantic subject of the clause, though formally in the accusative. The whole conveys 'but they (in fact)…'.

9.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.
9.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
9.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

10.meaning: They are afraid / they dread — to feel fear and anxiety, to be alarmed and shrink back.
10.grammar: A present-tense verb for a masculine plural 'they'. The ya- prefix marks third-person, the long -ū carries the plural subject, and the final -na is the indicative marker signaling a plain ongoing or habitual state. In this verb pattern the sense is being gripped by fear and dread.
10.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — primarily to separate, divide, distinguish; in this derived sense, to be afraid, dread

1.meaning: A conditional particle introducing a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact supposition: 'if (it were the case that…)'. It typically presents a condition that is unfulfilled or merely imagined, often implying the result did not or would not happen.
1.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case ending). It signals a hypothetical 'if': it sets up a supposed condition whose consequence is then stated, frequently with the sense 'if X were so, then Y would be so' — often where X is contrary to fact.

2.meaning: 'they find' — to come upon, obtain, or encounter something; to perceive a thing to be present or available.
2.grammar: A present/future verb, 3rd-person masculine plural ('they …'). The ending -ūna combines the plural 'they' (-ū) with the indicative marker -na, signalling a simple ongoing or future statement (not negated or subjunctive). The ya- prefix marks the third person.
2.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, obtain

3.meaning: A place of refuge — a shelter or sanctuary one resorts to for protection and escape.
3.grammar: A 'place' noun (the ma- prefix forms a noun of place) meaning 'a place to take shelter, a refuge'; the final hamza is the third root letter. The closing -an is the indefinite accusative ending ('a refuge'), the form a noun takes when it is, for example, the object of a verb. The root idea is a haven one flees to.
3.root: ل-ج-أ (l-j-ʾ) — to take refuge, resort to for protection

4.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
4.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

5.meaning: Caves — natural hollows or caverns in a mountain or rock used as shelter (plural).
5.grammar: A feminine plural noun (the -āt marks plural) meaning 'caves'. The final -in (written with the two-stroke tanwīn) is the indefinite genitive ending — the form used after a preposition or in a possessive link, here unspecified 'caves'. The root sense is a hollow or recess in rock that one enters.
5.root: غ-و-ر (gh-w-r) — to sink in, be hollow; a cave, hollow place

6.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
6.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

7.meaning: A place to enter / a tunnel or burrow — a spot one can go into, slip inside, or take cover within.

parts.en: place to enter / passage one slips into

7.grammar: A passive 'place' noun (form VIII, with the mu- prefix and an assimilated t) meaning 'a place that is entered, a passage one slips into'. The final -an is the indefinite accusative ending ('a place to enter'), the form taken, for example, as the object of a verb. The form adds a nuance of pushing or working one's way inside.
7.root: د-خ-ل (d-kh-l) — to enter, go in

8.meaning: 'They would surely turn away' — an emphatic 'surely' joined to a past-tense verb meaning to turn one's back and go off, to turn aside.
8.grammar: The prefixed la- is an emphasizing particle ('surely, certainly'), often the answer to an 'if' clause. The verb (form II, an intensive) means 'to turn away / turn one's back'; its final long vowel with silent alif marks a completed act done by a masculine plural 'they'. So: 'they would certainly turn away'.
8.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to turn, turn toward/away; to be near, to be in charge

9.meaning: 'To Him' or 'toward Him' — the preposition expressing direction or endpoint ('to / toward') combined with a pronoun referring to a single masculine person, indicating motion or attention directed at him.
9.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The base 'ilā shifts to 'ilay- when a pronoun is added. The suffix -hi is the third-person masculine singular object of a preposition, 'him'; its -i vowel is the form the pronoun takes after the 'ay' sound.

10.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
10.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

11.meaning: They race headlong / bolt uncontrollably — to rush off recklessly and unrestrained, like a runaway horse that cannot be held back.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb for a masculine plural 'they'. The ya- prefix marks third-person, the long -ū carries the plural subject, and the final -na is the indicative marker for a plain ongoing or habitual action. The root pictures a horse bolting beyond its rider's control, hence rushing headlong and unrestrained.
11.root: ج-م-ح (j-m-ḥ) — to bolt, run away uncontrollably (as an unruly horse)

1.meaning: 'And among them / and some of them' — a connective 'and' plus a preposition meaning 'from / among / part of,' joined to the pronoun 'them'; often introduces a subgroup ('among them are …').
1.grammar: A connective wa- ('and') with the preposition min ('from / among'), which always governs a following word in the genitive. Here that word is the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), giving 'and among them / and from them.' Particles like these do not themselves carry case or tense.

2.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
2.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

3.meaning: He finds fault with you, criticizes you, or taunts you with disparaging remarks — to single someone out for blame, often privately or sneeringly.

parts.en: he (present-tense marker, with assimilated preceding consonant)

3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The shaddah (doubling) on the yā shows that the final consonant of a preceding word — typically a short particle — has assimilated into it, fusing the two into one geminated sound. The -u vowel on the stem marks the indicative mood (a plain, ongoing statement of fact). The attached -ka is the direct object 'you' (a single male).
3.root: ل-م-ز (l-m-z) — to find fault, defame, taunt

4.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
4.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

5.meaning: Acts of charity, alms, voluntary or obligatory gifts given for the sake of Allah — the giving that flows from sincere faith (the word is linked to the notion of truthfulness/ṣidq, as such giving confirms the genuineness of one's faith).
5.grammar: A definite feminine plural noun (with 'the'). The sound-feminine plural ending -āt takes the vowel -i, which serves for both the genitive and the accusative in this plural pattern — marking the word either as object of a preposition / linked to a preceding noun, or as a direct object.
5.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — to be truthful, sincere; charity

6.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'fa-' ('then', 'so', 'but') drawing a consequence, joined to the conditional particle 'in' ('if'). Together: 'then if …', 'but if …'.
6.grammar: 'fa-' is a connector that signals a result or transition ('then/so'). 'in' is the conditional particle 'if', introducing a supposed condition. Both are indeclinable particles with no case ending.

7.meaning: They were given or granted (something) — a passive verb describing people who receive a portion or gift handed to them.
7.grammar: A past-tense passive verb. The vowelling (u- on the prefix) signals the passive voice: the subject is the receiver, not the giver. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they').
7.root: ع-ط-و (ʿ-ṭ-w) — to give, grant, bestow

8.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
8.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

9.meaning: They became content, satisfied, or pleased — to be well-pleased with what one has, to accept it gladly.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). It states a completed action: they came to be pleased.
9.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased, satisfied, content

10.meaning: A two-part word: the connective 'wa-' ('and'), joined to 'in', the conditional particle meaning 'if'. Together: 'and if …'.
10.grammar: 'wa-' is a connecting particle ('and'). 'in' is a particle introducing a hypothetical condition ('if …'), typically setting up a result clause that follows. Neither carries a case ending.

11.meaning: The particle 'lam', a negating word used to push a verb into the past: it means 'did not' / 'has not'. Though it sits before a present-tense verb form, it negates the action as something that did not happen.
11.grammar: 'lam' is a negating particle that governs a following present-tense verb but gives it past meaning ('did not …'). It also puts that verb into the shortened (jussive) form. 'lam' itself carries no ending.

12.meaning: They are (not) given or granted — a passive verb in a non-final mood, describing people who do not receive what is handed out.
12.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The yu- prefix with the -a- stem vowel marks the passive voice ('are given'). The dropped final nūn (ending in -aw rather than -awna) shows the subjunctive/jussive mood, the form used after certain particles such as 'if' or 'not'.

13.meaning: A two-part word: the preposition 'min' ('from / out of / some of') joined to the pronoun 'it' (feminine). Together: 'from it / out of it / of it,' indicating a source or a portion taken from a feminine thing.
13.grammar: A preposition 'min' with the attached pronoun '-hā' ('it/her'), referring to a feminine noun. 'Min' indicates origin, source, or a part taken from a whole; the attached pronoun is in the object form required after a preposition.

14.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
14.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

15.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
15.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

16.meaning: They are enraged, indignant, or filled with resentment — to seethe with anger and displeasure.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix plus the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending (with the nūn intact) signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing state.
16.root: س-خ-ط (s-kh-ṭ) — to be angry, displeased, indignant

1.meaning: 'and if' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the particle 'if'. This particular 'if' (law) introduces a hypothetical or contrary-to-fact condition: 'if (such-and-such had been the case)…', often implying it was not.
1.grammar: A conjunction plus a conditional particle. wa- means 'and'. law is a non-changing particle (no case ending) that sets up a supposition, typically answered by a clause beginning with la- ('… then certainly …').

2.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
2.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

3.meaning: They became content, satisfied, or pleased — to be well-pleased with what one has, to accept it gladly.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). It states a completed action: they came to be pleased.
3.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased, satisfied, content

4.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

5.meaning: He gave / granted / bestowed upon them — to bring, hand over, or confer (a gift or favour) to someone.
5.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb in Form IV ('to give/bestow'). With no subject suffix, it is third-person masculine singular ('he did'). The attached object pronoun 'them' (here voweled '-humu' to connect to the next word) gives 'he bestowed upon them.'
5.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (Form IV) to bring, give, bestow

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
6.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
6.root: — (proper divine name)

7.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
7.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
7.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

8.meaning: And they said — to utter or declare in speech, with the action presented as completed by a group.
8.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. 'qāla' is the past-tense verb 'to say'; the '-ū' suffix marks a completed action done by 'they' (a masculine or mixed group). The stem shown here ('qālu') carries only the stem vowel before the suffix, with the plural '-ū' supplied by the separate ending. Past tense, so the speaking is presented as already finished.

9.meaning: Means 'enough for us / our sufficiency'. The base word 'ḥasb' denotes that which suffices and satisfies — a sufficiency that makes anything more unnecessary; with the attached pronoun, 'sufficient for us / all we need'.
9.grammar: A noun functioning as a predicate ('[is] enough'), carrying the nominative -u ending typical of the thing being asserted. The attached -nā means 'us / for us / our', so the phrase reads 'our sufficiency' or 'enough for us'.
9.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count; to suffice, be enough

10.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
10.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
10.root: — (proper divine name)

11.meaning: He will soon give us — combining the near-future sense 'soon/shortly' with the act of giving, bringing, or bestowing upon us.
11.grammar: A present-tense verb turned into the future by the prefix sa- ('will, shortly'). The ya-…-ī shape marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The attached -nā is the object pronoun 'us'.
11.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come; (form IV) to give, bring

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
12.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

13.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
13.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

14.meaning: 'His bounty / grace / favor' — faḍl is overflowing generosity, an extra goodness given beyond what is owed; with the attached pronoun it means the bounty belonging to Him (Allah).
14.grammar: A noun with an attached possessive pronoun '-hi' ('his/His'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, which typically appears after a preposition or links the noun to what follows in an 'of' relationship; here it carries through to the possessor.
14.root: ف-ض-ل (f-ḍ-l) — excess, surplus; hence bounty, grace, superiority

15.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
15.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
15.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

16.meaning: A two-part expression: an emphatic particle that strongly affirms and confirms a statement ('truly, indeed, certainly'), fused with the attached pronoun 'we.' Together: 'truly we…' / 'indeed we…'
16.grammar: The particle inna gives strong emphasis and certainty to the clause it opens. The attached -ā is the pronoun 'we,' serving as the subject being emphasized: 'truly we…'

17.meaning: 'To / toward / up to' — a preposition marking the endpoint, goal, or limit of an action or motion: the direction something moves toward or the boundary at which it stops.
17.grammar: An invariable preposition. It has no case ending of its own but puts the noun that follows it into the genitive ('of / to' state). It indicates direction toward, or the terminal limit of, something.

18.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
18.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

19.meaning: Ones who earnestly desire, yearn, or set their hopes (toward something) — eager, longing seekers.
19.grammar: An active participle (a doer-noun, 'ones who desire') in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending marks the plural in the nominative case — the form a noun takes as the subject or as a predicate describing 'they'.
19.root: ر-غ-ب (r-gh-b) — to desire, long for, aspire to

1.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
1.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

2.meaning: The acts of charity, alms, or obligatory almsgiving — voluntary or prescribed giving for the sake of Allah and the needy.
2.grammar: A feminine plural noun with the definite article 'the'. The sound feminine plural is built with the suffix -āt- (the -ā belongs to this derivational suffix, part of the stem pattern). The case ending itself is solely the final -u, marking the nominative — the form used when the noun is the subject of a sentence.
2.root: ص-د-ق (ṣ-d-q) — truthfulness; charity given sincerely

3.meaning: For the poor / to the needy — a preposition 'for' joined to 'the poor,' the destitute who lack sufficient means; the plural of one in a state of poverty and need.
3.grammar: The preposition li- ('for') merged with the definite article al- (here written 'lil-'), on the plural noun 'the poor.' The preposition forces the genitive case, shown by the final -i; the genitive is the case taken after a preposition. The noun is a broken (irregular) plural meaning 'poor/needy people.'
3.root: ف-ق-ر (f-q-r) — poverty, need, to be poor

4.meaning: The poor and needy — those in straitened circumstances who lack sufficient means and are humbled by want.
4.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural noun meaning 'the needy', with prefixes wa- 'and' and al- 'the'. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to a noun before it ('… of …').
4.root: س-ك-ن (s-k-n) — to be still, to be subdued; one humbled by poverty

5.meaning: And those who work at or administer (something) — workers, agents, or officials engaged in a task, here especially those employed to collect and manage alms.
5.grammar: An active participle ('workers, those who do') in the masculine plural, with 'and' plus the article 'the'. The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive case — the form a noun takes as an object or after a preposition.
5.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to work, do, act

6.meaning: 'On it / upon it / over it' — the preposition 'alā ('on, upon, against') joined to the pronoun 'it/her', referring to a single feminine or grammatically feminine thing.
6.grammar: 'ʿalā' is a preposition meaning 'on/upon/over'; its ending shifts to -ay when a pronoun is attached. The suffix -hā is the object pronoun for a single feminine (or feminine-gender) thing. Together they mean 'on it'. Words after a preposition stand in the genitive, though attached pronouns like -hā do not visibly change form.

7.meaning: And the ones whose hearts are reconciled or won over — those whose affection and inclination toward the faith is being cultivated and made firm.
7.grammar: A passive participle ('ones who are reconciled / brought together') with 'and' plus the article 'the'. The -ati ending marks the genitive case — the form used after a preposition or when the word is linked to a following noun ('… of …').
7.root: ا-ل-ف (ʾ-l-f) — to join, unite, reconcile, make familiar

8.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
8.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
8.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

9.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
9.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

10.meaning: 'The necks' — the plural of 'neck', commonly used as a figure for slaves or captives (so 'freeing necks' = freeing slaves). The neck stands for the whole person held in bondage.
10.grammar: A definite broken plural of raqaba ('neck'), on the fiʿāl pattern. The final -i is the genitive case, taken after a preposition or as the second term of a possessive construction.
10.root: ر-ق-ب (r-q-b) — neck; watching over, guarding

11.meaning: And those burdened with debt — people weighed down by financial obligations they owe to others.
11.grammar: An active participle ('debtors, those who owe') in the masculine plural, with 'and' plus the article 'the'. The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive case — the form used as an object or after a preposition.
11.root: غ-ر-م (gh-r-m) — to be liable, owe a debt, suffer loss

12.meaning: 'And in' — the connector 'and' joined to the preposition 'in / within / during.'
12.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the preposition fī ('in'). Fī governs the following noun, putting it into the genitive case. Neither particle changes form.

13.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
13.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: Son of — used in the construction 'son of the road' (ibn al-sabīl), an idiom for the traveller or wayfarer.
15.grammar: A masculine noun, 'son', with the prefix wa- 'and'. The initial alif carries a connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl): its helping vowel is not pronounced here because the preceding wa- runs straight into the word, so it reads 'wab-' in connected speech. The final -i is the genitive ending, which typically links the word to a preceding preposition or to the following noun in a possessive chain ('son OF …').
15.root: ب-ن-و / ب-ن-ي (b-n-w / b-n-y) — to build; son, offspring

16.meaning: The way, road, or path — a route one travels; very often used figuratively for a course of life, conduct, or the path of religion. The attached article makes it definite: 'the way'.
16.grammar: al- is the definite article 'the' (its 'l' assimilates to the following 's', heard as 'as-sabīl'). The final -i is the genitive ending, marking the word as joined to a preceding noun ('… OF the way') or governed by a preposition.

17.meaning: A noun meaning 'an ordained obligation, a fixed and binding portion,' and specifically a stipulated bridal gift (dower) that is set and due as a duty.
17.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The -an ending is the accusative indefinite (tanwīn): it commonly marks the noun as a direct object of a verb, or expresses 'as a(n) …' / a specified amount, and lacks the definite article ('the').
17.root: ف-ر-ض (f-r-ḍ) — to appoint, ordain, make obligatory, fix a portion

18.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
18.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

19.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
19.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

20.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
20.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
20.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

21.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
21.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.
21.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

22.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
22.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
22.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: And among them / and some of them — singling out a subset from within a larger group of people.
1.grammar: A combination of 'and' + the preposition 'from/among' + the attached pronoun 'them' (masculine plural). The pronoun's base form -hum takes a connecting -u (humu) to ease pronunciation before a following word.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: They harm, hurt, or cause injury — to inflict pain or annoyance on someone, whether by word or deed.
3.grammar: A present-tense verb. The yu- prefix plus -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending (nūn intact) signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing action.
3.root: ا-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, annoy

4.meaning: 'The prophet' — a person to whom Allah sends revelation and inspired tidings to convey to people.
4.grammar: A noun made definite by the prefix al- ('the'). The final -a is the accusative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the direct object of a verb or otherwise governed into that state. It denotes a recipient and bearer of prophetic revelation.
4.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — momentous news, tidings (hence 'prophet,' bearer of revealed news)

5.meaning: A verb meaning 'and they say / and they keep saying' — to utter or assert in speech. The structure presents an ongoing or repeated act of speaking by a group.
5.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb joined by wa- ('and'). The ya-…-ūna frame marks the 3rd-person masculine plural ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the inseparable indicative-plural suffix, showing the verb is in its base (indicative) form and expressing an ongoing or habitual action.
5.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

6.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
6.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

7.meaning: An ear — the organ of hearing; figuratively, one who listens to and believes everything he is told.
7.grammar: A singular noun. The final -un ending marks the nominative case together with indefiniteness ('an ear') — the doubled n-sound (tanwīn) shows the noun is unspecified and functions as a subject or predicate.
7.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear; to listen, give ear, permit

8.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
8.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

9.meaning: An ear of / a listener to — the organ of hearing, here in the construct form that links it to a following word ('an ear for/of …').
9.grammar: A singular noun in the nominative case, ending in plain -u with no tanwīn. The absence of the doubled n-sound shows it is in construct (joined to a following noun), giving the sense 'an ear of …'.
9.root: ا-ذ-ن (ʾ-dh-n) — ear; to listen, give ear, permit

10.meaning: Good / goodness; also 'better' or 'best'. A word for what is good, beneficial, or excellent — and, by its pattern, often 'better than'.
10.grammar: An indefinite noun/adjective ('good' or 'better'). The final -in (nunation with -i) marks it as indefinite ('some good / any good') and in the genitive case, typically after a preposition or in a possessive link.
10.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, what is better

11.meaning: 'for you,' 'to you,' 'for your benefit' — the preposition 'for/to' joined to 'you (plural).' It marks the party for whose sake, benefit, or possession something exists or is given.
11.grammar: A preposition ('for/to') with the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). It assigns a benefit, purpose, or recipient — 'for you (all).' The suffix '-kum' is the plural 'you,' showing the recipients are a group.

12.meaning: He believes; he has faith. The verb denotes giving heartfelt trust and assent, especially affirming faith in Allah and what He has revealed; the form also carries the sense of granting security.
12.grammar: A present/future verb, third-person masculine singular ('he'). The yu- prefix marks 'he' for this verb pattern (form IV), and the final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain ongoing or habitual statement.

13.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
13.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
13.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

14.meaning: And he believes, has faith, or trusts — to affirm and rely upon something as true, especially faith in Allah.
14.grammar: 'And' joined to a present-tense verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing action. This verb commonly takes 'in' (bi-) before its object: 'believes in …'.
14.root: ا-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure; (form IV) to believe, have faith

15.meaning: A combination meaning 'for the believers' — 'to/for' + 'the' + 'those who have faith': people characterized by belief, trust, and security in faith.
15.grammar: The prefix li- is the preposition 'for/to'; 'al-' ('the') follows, its alif elided after li-. 'mu'minīn' is the active participle 'believers' (the mu- prefix forms the doer: 'those who have faith'). The -īna ending is the masculine plural in the genitive/accusative state (versus -ūna for the subject case), here governed by the preposition 'for'.
15.root: أ-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security; faith, trust

16.meaning: 'And a mercy' — raḥma is tender compassion that actively moves one to kindness, relief, and care. The wa- prefix adds 'and'. It is the same quality central to the divine names ar-Raḥmān and ar-Raḥīm.
16.grammar: The wa- prefix is 'and'. The word ends in a tāʾ marbūṭa (ة), the feminine ending: read in full it carries the -un here as -tun, while at a pause it is softened to -h. The final -un marks the noun as indefinite ('a mercy') and nominative, the subject form.

17.meaning: 'For/to those who …' — a preposition 'for / to / belonging to' joined to the masculine plural relative pronoun 'those who,' which introduces a description of a group by something they do.
17.grammar: The preposition li- ('for / to / belonging to') fused with the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). Relative pronouns like this do not change for case; they point ahead to a clause that describes the group ('those who …').

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
18.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

19.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
19.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural).
