Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
19.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

20.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
20.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

21.meaning: They harm, hurt, or cause injury — to inflict pain or annoyance on someone, whether by word or deed.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb. The yu- prefix plus -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending (nūn intact) signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing action.
21.root: ا-ذ-ي (ʾ-dh-y) — to harm, hurt, injure, annoy

22.meaning: 'Messenger / envoy' — one who is sent with a message. In religious usage it denotes a prophet entrusted by Allah to convey His revelation to people.
22.grammar: A noun. The final -a is the accusative case, the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb, or — as often with this word — standing in apposition (an explanatory restatement) to another accusative noun before it.
22.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; hence a messenger/envoy

23.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
23.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

24.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
24.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

25.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
25.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.
25.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

26.meaning: Painful, agonizing, deeply hurtful. An intensive adjective describing something that inflicts severe, grievous pain.
26.grammar: A masculine singular adjective on the intensive pattern faʿīl, conveying a strong, abiding quality ('truly painful'). The -un ending (tanwīn ḍamm) marks the nominative case (the case of a subject or of a noun's basic naming form), and the nunation shows it is indefinite.
26.root: أ-ل-م (ʾ-l-m) — pain, ache, suffering

1.meaning: They swear, take an oath, or vow — to make a solemn declaration, often invoking Allah's name as a pledge.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix plus -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The full -ūna ending (nūn intact) signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of ongoing action.
1.root: ح-ل-ف (ḥ-l-f) — to swear, take an oath

2.meaning: A phrase 'in Allah / by Allah', combining the preposition 'with/in/by' and the divine name Allah, the proper name of the One God.
2.grammar: The preposition bi- ('in, with, by means of') prefixed to the divine name Allah. A preposition always forces the following noun into the genitive case, which is why Allah here ends in -i. With verbs of believing, bi- conveys the object of faith — to believe IN.
2.root: — (Allah is the proper name of God and is not derived from a triliteral root in the usual sense)

3.meaning: 'For you' or 'to you' — the preposition of benefit or attribution ('for / belonging to') combined with a plural 'you', marking the people for whose benefit or possession something is done.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached pronoun. The prefix la- (the preposition li- 'for', here vowelled 'la' before a pronoun) conveys benefit, purpose, or belonging. The suffix -kum is the second-person masculine plural object, 'you all'.

4.meaning: So that they may please you / to gain your approval — the act of seeking to make someone satisfied and content.
4.grammar: A present-tense verb opened by li- ('so that, in order to'), which gives a purpose and puts the verb in the subjunctive mood. The dropped final nūn (-ū instead of -ūna) is the mark of that subjunctive. The yu-…-ū shape marks a third-person plural subject ('they'); attached -kum is the object 'you' (plural).
4.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased; (form IV) to please, satisfy

5.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
5.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
5.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

6.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
6.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

7.meaning: An adjective meaning 'more entitled, having a better/greater right, more deserving' of something.
7.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern, meaning 'more/most entitled'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word serves as the subject or as a predicate describing the subject.
7.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, just claim, what is due

8.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
8.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

9.meaning: That they should please Him / for them to satisfy Him — the act of seeking to make someone (here, Allah) well-pleased.

parts.en: they (present-tense marker, with assimilated preceding consonant)

9.grammar: A present-tense verb in the subjunctive mood: the dropped final nūn (-ū rather than -ūna) shows it follows a particle such as 'that' or 'so that'. The shaddah (doubling) on the yā shows that the final consonant of the preceding particle has assimilated into it, fusing into one geminated sound. The yu-…-ū shape marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); attached -hu is the object 'him/it'.
9.root: ر-ض-و (r-ḍ-w) — to be pleased; (form IV) to please, satisfy

10.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
10.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

11.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
11.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
11.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

12.meaning: Believers, those who have faith — who trust, affirm, and find security in what they believe; the active participle of believing, in the plural.
12.grammar: An active participle (Form IV, 'one who believes/gives faith'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (oblique) case; with no preposition governing it, the form here is accusative, marking it as a direct object.

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: That they (should) know, realize, or come to be aware — to possess or arrive at knowledge of something.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb in the subjunctive/jussive mood: the dropped final nūn (-ū instead of -ūna) shows it follows a particle such as 'that', 'so that', or 'did not'. The ya-…-ū shape marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they').
2.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, be aware, learn

3.meaning: 'That He …' — an emphatic particle meaning 'that / indeed' joined to the pronoun 'he'; it introduces and affirms a clause reporting something about a single masculine subject (most often Allah).
3.grammar: The emphatic particle 'anna' ('that, indeed') with the attached pronoun '-hu' ('he/it') as its subject. 'Anna' introduces a subordinate clause ('… that He …') and gives it certainty; '-hu' identifies a single masculine subject. (The pronoun is pronounced '-hu' here following the 'a' vowel.)

4.meaning: A pronoun meaning 'who / whoever / the one who', used for people; it points to a person or persons without naming them and usually introduces a description of them.
4.grammar: An indeclinable pronoun (it never changes its ending) referring to a person or persons — 'who' or 'whoever'. It can ask a question ('who?') or, as a relative pronoun, link to a following clause that describes the person(s) it stands for.

5.meaning: He opposes, defies, or sets himself in hostile opposition (to Allah and His Messenger) — to take a contrary, antagonistic stand.

parts.en: he (present-tense marker, with assimilated preceding consonant)

5.grammar: A present-tense verb (form III, conveying mutual or directed action) with the yu- prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The shaddah (doubling) on the yā shows that the final consonant of a preceding particle has assimilated into it, fusing into one geminated sound. The verb stands in the jussive mood — the form used after 'whoever' or a conditional 'if' — whose base form would end in a bare consonant (yuḥādid). The final -i (kasra) is inserted to break up the prohibited meeting of two unvowelled consonants (the verb's final consonant and the first consonant of the following word).
5.root: ح-د-د (ḥ-d-d) — boundary, limit; to oppose, set oneself against

6.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
6.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
6.root: — (proper name)

7.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
7.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.
7.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching a messenger

8.meaning: Then that, so that — a connector introducing a fact or clause. It joins the particle 'anna' ('that', which presents a firm statement) to a preceding 'fa' ('then/so'), linking what follows as a consequence or specification.
8.grammar: Two particles joined. The prefixed fa- signals sequence or result ('then/so'). 'anna' means 'that' and introduces a noun-clause stating something as established fact; it characteristically puts the following noun into the accusative. Neither is a verb; together they head a 'so that…' statement.

9.meaning: For him / to him / belonging to him. A small preposition meaning 'to/for' joined to the pronoun 'him', expressing possession, benefit, or direction toward him.
9.grammar: A preposition 'li-' ('to/for') fused with the attached pronoun 'him'. The pronoun 'him' stays the same; it is the preposition that changes, its vowel shifting from -i (li-) to -a (la-) when an attached pronoun follows it directly. The whole unit commonly conveys possession or that something is for someone's benefit.

10.meaning: Fire — the blaze; very often the Fire of Hell as a place of punishment.
10.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -a marks the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb, or after certain particles.
10.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — light, fire

11.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
11.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
11.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

12.meaning: 'Abiding (forever)' / 'remaining permanently' — an active participle describing one who stays and endures in a place without leaving; lasting, perpetual.
12.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun, 'one who abides') on the fāʿil pattern. The -an ending (nunation) is the accusative with indefiniteness, a form commonly used to describe the state or circumstance of someone ('… while abiding').
12.root: خ-ل-د (kh-l-d) — to abide, remain forever, endure

13.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
13.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

14.meaning: A demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that' — pointing to something regarded as distant or elevated, as opposed to 'this' (hadha) for what is near. It singles out a masculine singular thing and lends it a sense of distinction or loftiness.
14.grammar: A demonstrative for a masculine singular referent at a distance. The -ka ending is an address particle directed at a single male listener; it does not change for case. The whole word stays fixed in form regardless of its grammatical position.

15.meaning: The disgrace, humiliation, or ignominy — a state of public shame and abasement.
15.grammar: A singular noun with the definite article 'the'. The final -u marks the nominative case — the form a noun takes as the subject of a sentence or as a predicate.
15.root: خ-ز-ي (kh-z-y) — to be disgraced, humiliated, put to shame

16.meaning: 'the Most Great / the Immense' — vast, mighty, and tremendous in greatness and grandeur. As a divine name it conveys overwhelming magnificence and majesty.
16.grammar: A definite adjective/noun in an intensive pattern ('the Magnificent'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for an appositive descriptive title attached to such a subject.
16.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: He is wary, cautious, or on guard — to take heed and beware of a danger or consequence.
1.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). The final -u marks the indicative mood — a plain statement of an ongoing state or action.
1.root: ح-ذ-ر (ḥ-dh-r) — to be cautious, wary, take heed

2.meaning: 'The hypocrites' — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief or treachery; the term pictures someone who has a hidden 'tunnel' or back-exit out of their professed commitment.
2.grammar: A definite plural noun (an active participle, 'the ones who dissemble'). The al- prefix means 'the'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the nominative case, the form typically used when the noun is the doer/subject.
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to tunnel through, dissemble; hypocrisy

3.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
3.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

4.meaning: 'It is/was sent down, revealed (in stages)' — caused to descend; used especially of revelation being brought down. The intensive form suggests a gradual or repeated sending-down.

parts.en: she/it (3rd person feminine singular present prefix)
be sent down (passive-vowelled Form II stem)

4.grammar: A present-tense passive verb, 3rd person feminine singular ('it is sent down'). It is a Form II (fa''ala) verb, a pattern that often adds intensity or gradualness ('to send down bit by bit'). The 'tu-' prefix marks a 3rd person feminine present subject and is shared by active and passive; what makes this verb passive is the internal vowel pattern (ḍamma on the prefix, fatḥa on the one before last). The final '-a' is the subjunctive ending, appearing when the verb follows a subjunctive particle.
4.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to descend, come down; (Form II) to send down

5.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
5.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
5.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

6.meaning: A chapter or section of revelation — a discrete, named unit of the Qur'an, complete in itself. The word denotes an enclosed division of the sacred text, like a wall or row that bounds a distinct portion. Being indefinite, it means 'a chapter / some chapter' rather than a specific one.

parts.en: chapter (of the Qur'an); the stem already ends in the feminine tā' marbūṭa (ة)

6.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final nunation (the -un sound, written as the two-ḍamma sign) marks it as indefinite ('a chapter / some chapter'), and that nunation is built on the ḍamma vowel, which is the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being named/described. The tā' marbūṭa (ة) that gives the word its feminine form belongs to the stem itself, not to this ending.
6.root: س-و-ر (s-w-r) — to enclose, wall round; a row or tier (hence a bounded section)

7.meaning: To inform, notify, or tell someone of weighty, consequential news — to give a report or announcement that matters. The doubled middle letter intensifies the plain verb 'to bring news,' so it conveys conveying serious tidings; with the attached object it means 'it/she informs them.'
7.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb of the intensive form. The tu- prefix marks a third-person feminine singular ('she/it') or second-person masculine singular ('you') subject; the -u on the stem is the indicative mood, used for an ongoing or factual action. The suffix -hum is the direct object 'them.'
7.root: ن-ب-أ (n-b-ʾ) — news, tidings, weighty report

8.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
8.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
9.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

10.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
10.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
10.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

11.meaning: 'Say!' — a command to utter or declare something aloud, addressed to a single male.
11.grammar: A command (imperative) verb addressed to one male: 'say!'. Its natural form ends in a silent consonant (qul), but here a short -i vowel is added simply to smooth pronunciation before a following word that begins with a connecting sound; it carries no case meaning of its own.
11.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, to speak

12.meaning: A command 'mock! / scoff! / ridicule!' addressed to a group — to treat something with derision and make a jest of it. The form carries the sense of deliberately seeking to deride, and the plural command tells more than one person to do so.
12.grammar: A command (imperative) verb of the seeking/'requesting' form, addressed to a masculine plural 'you all.' The -ū ending is the plural marker telling a group to perform the act; the silent alif after it is merely a spelling convention.

13.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
13.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: 'One who brings out / brings forth / produces.' The doer that draws something out from a hidden or enclosed state into the open — a bringer-forth or revealer.
15.grammar: An active participle ('one who brings forth') built on the causative pattern 'to cause to come out'. The -un ending is the indefinite nominative case, which typically marks the word as a subject or as the predicate that describes the subject ('is one who brings forth').
15.root: خ-ر-ج (kh-r-j) — to go out, come forth; (causative) to bring out

16.meaning: A short, highly versatile particle 'mā.' It can mean 'what' or 'that which,' can negate ('not'), and can serve as an intensifier attached to another word. Its precise force depends on what it accompanies, but its core is to point to a thing or to add emphasis.
16.grammar: A multifunctional particle. It does not take case endings. Depending on usage it can be a relative ('that which'), an interrogative ('what?'), a negator ('not'), or — when joined to another particle — an emphasizer. It is uninflected and indeclinable.

17.meaning: To be wary, on guard, or cautious — to take heed and beware of something feared or dangerous, keeping oneself protected from it. It blends fear with vigilance: not mere dread but careful self-guarding. With the plural ending it means 'you all are wary / take heed.'
17.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The ta-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the full -ūna ending shows the indicative mood, used for a real, ongoing action (as opposed to the shortened -ū used after certain particles).
17.root: ح-ذ-ر (ḥ-dh-r) — caution, wariness, taking heed against danger

1.meaning: A combination meaning 'and surely if' — introducing a hypothetical condition ('if…') sworn by an implied oath, so that the outcome is strongly anticipated; roughly 'and by all means, if…'.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a noun or verb, so it takes no case ending: wa- 'and', the lam al-qasam (the 'lam of swearing') that marks the following condition as sworn by an implied oath, and in 'if' which sets up the condition. This oath-lam construction correlates with a later response clause that itself carries emphasis (an emphatic lam plus the 'nūn of emphasis' on its verb), giving the sense 'and [I swear] if … they would surely …'.

2.meaning: To ask, question, or request — to put a query to someone or seek something from them. With the endings attached it means 'you asked them,' a completed act of questioning directed at a group.
2.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -ta marks the doer as second-person masculine singular ('you'); the further suffix -hum is the direct object 'them.'
2.root: س-أ-ل (s-ʾ-l) — to ask, question, request

3.meaning: An emphatic assertion 'they will surely say / they will certainly say.' The word fuses an oath-like emphasis with a future statement of speaking, leaving no doubt that the utterance will occur. The heavy doubled ending drives home the certainty.
3.grammar: A present/future verb made doubly emphatic. The opening la- means 'surely'; the ya- prefix marks a third-person masculine subject; and the heavy -nna suffix (the 'energetic' ending) intensifies it to 'they will most certainly say.' Together la-…-nna is a fixed pattern of strong affirmation about something yet to happen.

4.meaning: 'Only / nothing but' — a restrictive particle that limits and emphasizes, asserting that the matter is exclusively so and no other ('it is only...'). It combines the emphatic 'inna' with the restricting 'mā'.
4.grammar: A compound particle formed from the emphatic inna ('indeed') and mā, which together work as a tool of restriction meaning 'only / nothing but'. It both stresses and confines the statement that follows to a single truth, excluding all alternatives.

5.meaning: 'We were' — the past tense of the verb 'to be,' establishing a past state or condition for a group including the speaker. It is the basic verb of existence and of 'being something.'
5.grammar: The past tense of 'to be' in the first-person plural ('we were'). The subject suffix is -nā ('we'); its nūn is written with a shadda (نَّ) because it merges with the final nūn of the verb stem kun-, and the alif spells the long -ā. A hollow verb, its middle weak letter drops in this form. It sets up a past state, and what follows describes how 'we' were.
5.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to come into being, existence

6.meaning: To wade or plunge into something — literally to step into water, and by extension to immerse oneself in idle, rambling, or frivolous talk and to engage in vain discourse. With the 'we' prefix it means 'we were wading/engaging (in talk).'
6.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb. The na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'); the -u ending is the indicative mood, signalling a real, ongoing action.
6.root: خ-و-ض (kh-w-ḍ) — to wade into water; to plunge into idle/vain talk

7.meaning: To play, sport, or amuse oneself — to engage in jest and diversion rather than serious purpose. Prefixed with 'and we,' it means 'and we play / and we were jesting,' the act of passing time in frivolity.
7.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and.' The verb is present-tense (imperfect): the na- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'), and the -u ending is the indicative mood, used for a real, ongoing action.
7.root: ل-ع-ب (l-ʿ-b) — to play, sport, amuse oneself

8.meaning: Say! — a command to speak or declare; the singular imperative addressed to one person.
8.grammar: Imperative (command) verb addressed to a single male/person: 'Say!'. From a hollow root, the middle weak letter drops in the command, leaving the short form 'qul'. The bare ending (no vowel) is characteristic of this singular imperative.

9.meaning: A pointed question 'Is it Allah…?' — the interrogative particle joined to the name of Allah by the preposition 'with/in/by.' It opens a challenge or rebuke about whether Allah is the object of some act named afterward.
9.grammar: Three elements fused together. The opening a- is the question particle ('is it…?'). The preposition bi- ('with/in/by') then governs the divine name, which is why it carries the -i (genitive) ending — the case regularly taken by a noun after a preposition.
9.root: — (the proper name Allah has no derivational root; the particles likewise have none)

10.meaning: 'And His signs / His verses' — the plural of 'sign,' meaning tokens, proofs, or marks that point to a greater reality, and also the verses of revelation. The attached 'His' refers the signs to Allah, and the leading 'and' connects them to what precedes.
10.grammar: A sound feminine plural noun. The -i ending on the plural marks the genitive case, used when a noun is possessed ('… OF …'), follows a preposition, or (as here) carries an attached possessor. The suffix -hi means 'his,' and its vowel is i to harmonize with the preceding genitive. The opening wa- means 'and.'
10.root: أ-ي-ي (ʾ-y-y) — a sign, token, mark, or evidence

11.meaning: A phrase meaning 'and His Messenger' — referring to one who is sent, an envoy or apostle bearing a message, joined by 'and' and possessed by 'His.'
11.grammar: 'Messenger' joined by wa- ('and') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i vowel before the pronoun is the genitive case, here because the word is linked in possession ('Messenger OF Him'); the pronoun takes the -hi form (with i-vowel) when it follows an i-sound.
11.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — sending, dispatching; a message or one who is sent

12.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
12.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
12.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

13.meaning: To mock, deride, or scoff — to treat something as a laughingstock and ridicule it. The form conveys deliberately engaging in derision. With the 'you all' frame it means 'you (all) mock / are mocking.'
13.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb of the seeking/'requesting' form. The ta-…-ūna frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'); the full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, used for a real, ongoing action.

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: To offer an excuse, apologize, or plead a justification — to put forward reasons in one's own defense. The form conveys actively seeking to excuse oneself. Addressed to a group it means '(do not) make excuses.'

parts.en: make an excuse, apologize, plead a justification

2.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb of the reflexive form. The ta-…-ū frame marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all'). The ending is the shortened -ū (not -ūna), the form a verb takes after a negating, prohibiting, or other governing particle; the silent alif after it is only a spelling convention.
2.root: ع-ذ-ر (ʿ-dh-r) — excuse, apology, justification

3.meaning: A short particle placed before a verb to emphasize or affirm it. Before a past-tense verb it means 'indeed / certainly / has already (happened)'; before a present-tense verb it can mean 'sometimes / may'. It sharpens and confirms the verb that follows.
3.grammar: An indeclinable particle (its form never changes). It does not take case or tense endings; its job is to color the following verb — affirming and intensifying a past action ('has indeed done') or signaling occasional possibility with a present verb.

4.meaning: To disbelieve, reject faith, or be ungrateful — to cover over and deny the truth, refusing to acknowledge Allah or His favor. The root sense is 'to cover/conceal,' so disbelief is pictured as veiling what one knows to be true. With the ending it means 'you (all) disbelieved.'

parts.en: you all (masculine plural) — past-tense subject ending

4.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action. The suffix -tum marks the doer as second-person masculine plural ('you all'), so the whole word means 'you all disbelieved.'
4.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to deny/reject (disbelief, ingratitude)

5.meaning: After; following in time or order — the point or moment subsequent to something.
5.grammar: An adverb of time functioning much like a preposition ('after'). It is fixed in the accusative form ending in -a, and is normally followed by a noun in the 'of' relationship, giving 'after (the) …'.
5.root: ب-ع-د (b-ʿ-d) — afterness, that which comes later; distance/remoteness

6.meaning: Your faith / your believing — the inward belief and trust of a group of people. It joins the noun 'faith' (īmān) to an attached pronoun 'your (plural)'.
6.grammar: The noun īmān ('faith') carries the genitive -i ending and then the possessive pronoun -kum ('your', plural). The genitive shows the noun is governed by a preposition or joined to a preceding word; -kum makes it 'your faith' (belonging to a group).
6.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — to be secure, to trust, to believe

7.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
7.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

8.meaning: To pardon, forgive, or let pass — to wipe away an offense and excuse it without penalty. The root carries the idea of effacement, of something being erased or passed over. With the 'we' prefix it means 'we pardon / we forgive.'
8.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb whose root ends in a weak letter. The n- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The bare final -u (with no added consonant) is the jussive/conditional form — the shape this kind of verb takes after a governing particle such as 'if' — where the original final weak letter has dropped away.
8.root: ع-ف-و (ʿ-f-w) — to efface, pardon, forgive, let pass

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'on behalf of,' 'for,' 'about,' or 'away from.' It often conveys removing a burden from someone or acting in their place.

parts.en: on behalf of / for / away from

9.grammar: A preposition (a linking particle). It governs the noun that follows it, putting that noun into the genitive case. It does not change form.

10.meaning: A group, party, or band of people — a portion or faction of a larger whole, a contingent that stands apart as a section. Being indefinite, it means 'a group / some party.'

parts.en: group, party, band (a portion of people)

10.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The -in (nunation) marks it indefinite ('a group / some party'), and the -i vowel under the nunation is the genitive case, used after a preposition or to link the noun to a preceding one ('… of …').
10.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go round, circle; a band that moves about, a portion

11.meaning: 'From you / among you (plural)' — indicating a part taken out of, or belonging to, a group of people being addressed.
11.grammar: The preposition min ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun -kum ('you all,' masculine plural). Together they express partition or origin: a part drawn 'from / among' the addressed group.
11.root: — (preposition with pronoun; no root)

12.meaning: To punish, chastise, or inflict torment — to make someone suffer a penalty for wrongdoing. The doubled middle letter intensifies it to severe or repeated chastisement. With the 'we' prefix it means 'we punish / we chastise.'
12.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb of the intensive form. The nu- prefix marks a first-person plural subject ('we'). The final consonant carries no vowel (sukūn) — the jussive/conditional form a verb takes after a particle such as 'if,' as opposed to the indicative which would end in -u.

13.meaning: A group, party, or band of people — a portion or section of a larger company. It denotes a subset of people set apart from the whole.
13.grammar: An indefinite feminine noun with the -an (tanwīn) ending, which is accusative. This ending typically marks the noun as a direct object or as the subject of certain emphatic/existential constructions. The base noun ends in the feminine tā' marbūṭa (the -t of ṭāifat), sounded before the case-vowel.
13.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle; a ṭāʾifa is a group that 'goes about' together, a faction or party

14.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
14.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

15.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
15.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

16.meaning: Those who commit crimes — wrongdoers, sinners, the guilty who cut themselves off from righteousness. The root sense is to 'sever' or 'cut off,' picturing the criminal as one who breaks away into guilt. This is the plural, 'criminals / guilty ones.'
16.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun) in the sound masculine plural. The -īna ending marks the plural in the accusative/genitive case — the form used for a direct object, after a preposition, or when linked to a preceding noun (as opposed to -ūna, which would be the subject form).
16.root: ج-ر-م (j-r-m) — to cut off, sever; hence to commit a crime or sin

1.meaning: The hypocrites (men) — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief, presenting one face in public and hiding another within. The form names people who 'enter through a tunnel,' i.e. slip in deceptively. This is the definite masculine plural, 'the hypocrites.'
1.grammar: A definite active participle (a 'doer' noun) in the sound masculine plural. The al- prefix means 'the.' The -ūna ending marks the plural in the nominative case — the form used for the subject of a sentence (as opposed to -īna, the object/oblique form).
1.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — a tunnel or burrow with two exits; hence hypocrisy (a hidden second way out)

2.meaning: 'And the hypocrites (women)' — the feminine counterpart to the male hypocrites: women who outwardly show faith while concealing disbelief. The leading 'and' joins them to what precedes; this is the definite feminine plural in the subject form.
2.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun, with wa- ('and') and al- ('the') prefixed. The -āt is the feminine plural marker, and the final -u is the nominative case, used for the subject of a sentence. (A sound feminine plural shows nominative with -u and the object/oblique case with -i.)
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — a tunnel with two exits; hence hypocrisy (a hidden second way out)

3.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
3.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
3.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
5.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
5.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

6.meaning: They command / they enjoin: a group ordering, commanding, or urging that something be done, as an ongoing or habitual action.
6.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb (Form I) meaning 'to command' or 'to enjoin'. The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'), and the full -ūna ending shows the plain, unrestricted present tense, expressing ongoing or habitual action.
6.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, to order; a matter/affair

7.meaning: The wrong, the disapproved, the abhorrent — that which is recognized as evil, unacceptable, and rejected by sound nature and revelation. The root sense is 'unknown / unrecognized,' so the munkar is what right conscience refuses to acknowledge as good. Joined here with 'with/by.'
7.grammar: A passive participle ('that which is disapproved'), made definite with al- ('the') and preceded by the preposition bi- ('with/by'). The final -i is the genitive case, the ending a noun regularly takes after a preposition.
7.root: ن-ك-ر (n-k-r) — to be unknown/unrecognized; hence the disapproved, the abhorrent

8.meaning: And they forbid, prohibit, or restrain — the act of holding others back from something, the natural counterpart to commanding.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The wa- prefix means 'and'. The ya- prefix marks third person ('he/they'). The root ends in a weak letter (-y), which surfaces as a wāw within the stem (yanhaw-); the masculine plural present subject is then marked by the ending -na ('they'), in the present/ongoing tense: 'they forbid'.

9.meaning: About / concerning; a particle marking the topic of inquiry or the thing one moves away from.
9.grammar: A preposition meaning 'about, concerning, away from'. Its base form is ʿan; the final -i here is a helping vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a connecting 'al-'. It governs the genitive case on whatever noun follows.

10.meaning: The right, the recognized good, the fitting — that which is known and acknowledged by sound nature and revelation to be proper and beneficial. The root sense is 'known / recognized,' so the maʿrūf is conduct that conscience and law affirm as good and customary.

parts.en: the right, the recognized good, what is fitting

10.grammar: A passive participle ('that which is known/recognized'), made definite with al- ('the'). The final -i marks the genitive case, used when the noun follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun ('… of …').
10.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognize; hence the recognized good, the fitting and customary

11.meaning: 'And they hold back / withhold / close up' — to draw in, grasp tightly, or clench (as a hand is closed), and by extension to be tight-fisted and withhold. The leading 'and' connects it to what precedes; with the 'they' frame it means 'and they withhold/clench.'
11.grammar: A present-tense (imperfect) verb, with wa- ('and') prefixed. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the full -ūna ending is the indicative mood, used for a real, ongoing action.
11.root: ق-ب-ض (q-b-ḍ) — to grasp, clench, contract, draw in (hence to withhold)

12.meaning: Their hands — the physical hands; often figuratively the means by which one acts, strikes, or exerts force (plural of 'hand').
12.grammar: A plural noun (aydī, plural of yad, 'hand') with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a vowel before the pronoun marks the accusative case, which typically signals that the word is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon).

13.meaning: A verb meaning 'they forgot' or 'they neglected/abandoned.' The root spans both genuine forgetfulness and the willful neglect of something one chooses to put out of mind.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb. The ending -ū marks a completed action by 'they' (masculine plural). The silent 'alif' written after the -ū is a spelling convention and is not pronounced.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: 'So He has forgotten them' — to let slip from memory, to neglect, leave out, or pass over. Of Allah it is used figuratively for deliberate disregard, treating someone as though forgotten. The leading 'so/then' draws a consequence; the ending 'them' is the object.
15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb describing a completed action, with fa- ('so/then') prefixed to mark a result. The bare stem with final -a is the default third-person masculine singular ('he'); the suffix -hum is the direct object 'them.'
15.root: ن-س-ي (n-s-y) — to forget, neglect, leave behind

16.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
16.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

17.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
17.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
17.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

18.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
18.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

19.meaning: Those who defiantly disobey — the active participle 'fāsiq' (one who breaks away from obedience, transgressing moral and religious limits) in its sound masculine plural, with the definite article.
19.grammar: Definite ('al-') sound masculine plural active participle. The '-ūna' ending is the nominative (subject) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the doer of an action or the subject of a sentence.
19.root: ف-س-ق (f-s-q) — to break away, depart from obedience; to act immorally

1.meaning: 'He promised / pledged' — a completed act of giving one's word that something will come about, whether a reward or a consequence.
1.grammar: A past-tense verb with no attached pronoun, so the doer is 'he' (third-person masculine singular) and the action is complete. The final -a is the standard past-tense vowel.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
2.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.
2.root: — (proper divine name)

3.meaning: the hypocrites — those who outwardly profess faith while inwardly concealing disbelief; people who present one face publicly and hide another within. From a root evoking a tunnel with two openings, suggesting a hidden way out.
3.grammar: A definite noun: al- means 'the'. 'Munāfiq' is an active participle of Form III ('one who behaves hypocritically'). The ending -īna marks the masculine sound plural in the oblique case (the form used for objects of verbs and after prepositions, i.e. accusative/genitive, as opposed to nominative -ūna).
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — tunnel/burrow with a hidden exit; hence hypocrisy

4.meaning: 'And the hypocrites (women)' — the feminine plural counterpart of the male hypocrites: women who outwardly profess faith while concealing disbelief. The leading 'and' joins them to what precedes; this is the definite feminine plural in the object/oblique form.
4.grammar: A definite sound feminine plural noun, with wa- ('and') and al- ('the') prefixed. The -āt is the feminine plural marker, and the final -i is the accusative/genitive case — the form used for a direct object, after a preposition, or linked to a preceding noun. (In a sound feminine plural this same -i serves both the object and the genitive, contrasting with -u for the subject.)
4.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — a tunnel with two exits; hence hypocrisy (a hidden second way out)

5.meaning: "And the disbelievers / the staunch deniers," "kuffār" being an intensive plural for those who persistently reject faith and cover over the truth — often connoting obstinate or ungrateful denial.
5.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and" and "al-" is the definite article "the." The base "kuffār" is an intensive/broken plural (fuʿʿāl pattern) stressing the depth or persistence of the trait. The final "-a" ending is the accusative case, the form taken as a direct object or other sentence complement.
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; hence to deny or be ungrateful for truth

6.meaning: Fire — the blaze; very often the Fire of Hell as a place of punishment.
6.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final -a marks the accusative case — the form a noun takes as the direct object of a verb, or after certain particles.
6.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — light, fire

7.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
7.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
7.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

8.meaning: Ones who abide / remain forever — those who dwell perpetually and permanently in a state or place, without end. The word denotes lasting, undying permanence.
8.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' word: 'ones abiding'). The -īna ending is the sound masculine plural in its accusative/genitive form, used when the word is an object or governed by a preceding element. It describes people characterized by perpetual abiding.

9.meaning: 'In it / therein.' A preposition with an attached pronoun: 'in' plus a feminine singular 'it,' meaning 'inside it / within it,' referring back to some feminine or grammatically feminine thing (such as a place).
9.grammar: A prepositional phrase: fī ('in, within') with the attached object pronoun -hā ('it,' feminine singular). The pronoun is the object of the preposition and points back to a previously mentioned feminine noun.

10.meaning: A standalone pronoun meaning 'she' or 'it' (feminine). Arabic has no neuter, so 'it' for a feminine noun is expressed with this word. Used independently for emphasis or to stand as the subject of a sentence.
10.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person feminine singular. It stands on its own (not attached to another word) and most often functions as the subject of a nominal sentence ('she/it is …'). Its form is fixed and does not take case endings.

11.meaning: It/he is enough for them; it suffices them and meets their need so nothing more is required. From a noun meaning 'sufficiency, reckoning, what is enough,' carrying the sense that a thing is fully adequate as a reckoning or accounting for someone.
11.grammar: A noun in the subject (nominative) form with the -u ending, marking it as the thing being spoken about (the 'topic' or doer of being-sufficient). The attached -hum means 'them' (a group of males or mixed) and shows for whom it suffices.
11.root: ح-س-ب (ḥ-s-b) — to reckon, count, account; sufficiency

12.meaning: And he cursed them — i.e. expelled them from mercy and consigned them to being far from good and from divine favour. The verb denotes a curse: a pronouncement of removal from mercy and exclusion from blessing.
12.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'he' form (3rd-person masculine singular): the action is completed and done by a single male subject. The attached -humu means 'them' (a group) as the object receiving the curse; its final -u is a connecting vowel that smooths into the next word.
12.root: ل-ع-ن (l-ʿ-n) — to curse, to remove/banish from mercy

13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
13.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

14.meaning: 'And for them / and they have.' A combination expressing possession or entitlement belonging to a group of males: 'and to/for them (belongs).' The particle li- conveys 'for' or 'belonging to,' and the attached pronoun refers to 'them.'
14.grammar: A possessive/benefactive phrase: the preposition li- ('for, belonging to') with the attached object pronoun -hum ('them,' masculine plural). Such 'for X' phrases commonly express that something belongs to or is owed to that party.

15.meaning: Painful punishment, torment, or chastisement — suffering imposed as a penalty.
15.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The ending -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite ('a punishment') and in the nominative case, typically used for the subject or for the thing said to exist.
15.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

16.meaning: "lasting, enduring, permanent, abiding" — an active participle describing something that stays in place, persists, or is established and ongoing.
16.grammar: An active participle (form IV) functioning as an adjective/noun ("one that stays, abiding"). The "mu-" prefix marks the doer/agent of the action. The final "-un" (tanwīn ḍamma) is the indefinite nominative ending, marking the word as indefinite ("a lasting one") and as a subject or predicate rather than an object.
16.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, remain, establish

1.meaning: Like those who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, meaning 'similar to the ones who…' and pointing to a group defined by what follows.
1.grammar: A compound of the preposition ka- ('like, as'), expressing resemblance, and the masculine plural relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'). The relative pronoun is fixed in form and introduces a description; it does not change for case.

2.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
2.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
2.root: — (preposition)

3.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
3.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'

4.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
4.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
4.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

5.meaning: More intense, stronger, more severe or vehement; the comparative/superlative form denoting a higher degree of strength or intensity ('more / most intense').
5.grammar: A comparative/elative adjective on the pattern afʿal ('more / most …'). The final -a here is an accusative ending — note that elative adjectives are often diptotes (taking -a even in the genitive and not taking nunation). It conveys 'more intense / stronger' and is commonly followed by a noun specifying in what respect.
5.root: ش-د-د (sh-d-d) — to be strong, intense, firm, severe

6.meaning: A combination meaning 'from among you' or 'of you' — singling out a part or some individuals out of a larger group being addressed.
6.grammar: The preposition min ('from, among, some of') with the attached pronoun -kum, which means 'you' for a group of two or more (grammatically masculine plural). Because the pronoun follows a preposition, it is in the object form; the whole expression partitions or draws out individuals from the addressed group.
6.root: — (min is a particle/preposition; -kum is a pronoun)

7.meaning: Strength, power, force, might — physical or military vigour, robustness, and the capacity to exert force or prevail. Also used for firmness and resolve.
7.grammar: A feminine noun carrying the -an ending (the 'tanwīn' or 'n' of indefiniteness), so 'a strength / some power' with no 'the.' The accusative -an form is commonly used to specify in what respect something is meant ('in terms of strength') or as the object of a verb.
7.root: ق-و-ي (q-w-y) — to be strong; strength, power

8.meaning: And greater in number, more numerous, more abundant — the comparative 'more' formed from the idea of plentifulness and multitude.
8.grammar: A comparative/elative adjective ('more …') on the pattern afʿal. Words of this pattern are 'diptote' (they refuse the indefinite -n and take only two endings instead of three): they use -u as the subject form and a single -a for BOTH the object and the after-preposition/linked positions. So the -a seen here is not strictly 'accusative' — for a diptote the same -a covers what would otherwise be the object and the linked (genitive) endings, and no 'tanwīn' (-n) is ever added. Comparatives of this pattern also stay the same for masculine and feminine.
8.root: ك-ث-ر (k-th-r) — to be many; abundance, multitude

9.meaning: Wealth, possessions, goods, property — the plural of 'māl' (money/property), denoting riches and material assets of every kind.
9.grammar: A plural noun with the indefinite -an ending ('wealth' / 'some possessions,' no 'the'). The accusative -an form frequently specifies the respect in which something is meant ('in terms of wealth') or serves as a verb's object.

10.meaning: And children, offspring, sons — the plural of 'walad' (child/son), covering one's progeny and descendants.
10.grammar: A plural noun with the indefinite -an ending ('children,' no 'the'). The accusative -an form commonly marks it as the object of a verb or as a complement specifying respect ('in terms of children').
10.root: و-ل-د (w-l-d) — to give birth; child, offspring

11.meaning: So they sought enjoyment / took their fill of pleasure — they availed themselves of and indulged in worldly goods and gratification. The form adds the sense of 'seeking out' enjoyment for oneself.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'they' form (3rd-person masculine plural): a completed action done by a group of males. The -ū ending means 'they.' The verb is of the 'seeking/asking-for' pattern (istafʿala), adding the nuance of pursuing the enjoyment for oneself; the prefixed fa- means 'so' or 'and then.'
11.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, to give enjoyment; provision, pleasure

12.meaning: With/by their portion — their allotted share or lot, especially of worldly goods. 'Khalāq' means an assigned portion or due share, often of good fortune in this life.
12.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'), which forces the -i (genitive) ending that you see before the pronoun. The attached -him means 'their' (a group of males); after the -i sound the pronoun appears as -him.
12.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, apportion; an allotted portion/share

13.meaning: So you sought enjoyment / took your fill of pleasure — you (a group) availed yourselves of and indulged in worldly gratification. The form conveys 'seeking out' the enjoyment for oneself.
13.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -tum ending, meaning 'you (all)' — a completed action done by a group being addressed (males or mixed). Built on the 'seeking/asking-for' pattern (istafʿala), it adds the sense of pursuing the enjoyment for oneself; the prefixed fa- means 'so' or 'and then.'
13.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — to enjoy, to give enjoyment; provision, pleasure

14.meaning: With/by your portion — your allotted share or lot, especially of worldly goods. 'Khalāq' is an assigned portion or due share, often of good fortune in this life.
14.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'), which requires the -i (genitive) ending seen before the pronoun. The attached -kum means 'your,' addressed to a group (males or mixed).
14.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, apportion; an allotted portion/share

15.meaning: 'Just as / in the same way that' — a phrase of comparison joining 'like / as' to 'what', meaning 'like that which...' or 'in the manner that...'.
15.grammar: The comparison particle ka- ('like / as') joined to mā ('what / that which'). Together they introduce a likeness or manner — 'just as...', 'in the same way that...' — comparing one thing or action to another.

16.meaning: A verb meaning 'he enjoyed' or 'he sought enjoyment / benefit' — to derive pleasure, profit, or use from something, taking advantage of it for a while.
16.grammar: A past-tense verb in a Form X (istafʿala) pattern, conveying the seeking or taking of enjoyment and benefit. The stem-final -a vowel marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he') and shows the action as completed; it is part of the verb form itself, not a separable suffix.
16.root: م-ت-ع (m-t-ʿ) — enjoyment, benefit, provision, to give use of

17.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
17.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

18.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
18.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

19.meaning: 'before you,' 'prior to you' — an expression of precedence in time or place, here relating that precedence to 'you (plural).' The core word denotes the 'before' side, what comes earlier or in front.
19.grammar: An adverb of time/place ('before') joined to the pronoun '-kum' ('you, plural'). The '-i' ending is genitive: such words of place/time regularly take this case, especially after a preposition, and the attached pronoun completes the sense as 'before you.'
19.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — precedence, being before/in front

20.meaning: With/by their portion — their allotted share or lot, especially of worldly goods. 'Khalāq' means an assigned portion or due share, often of good fortune in this life.
20.grammar: A noun governed by the preposition bi- ('with/by'), which forces the -i (genitive) ending that you see before the pronoun. The attached -him means 'their' (a group of males); after the -i sound the pronoun appears as -him.
20.root: خ-ل-ق (kh-l-q) — to create, apportion; an allotted portion/share

21.meaning: And you plunged in / waded into — you engaged deeply and recklessly in talk or affairs, especially vain, false, or improper discourse. The verb's image is of wading into water, hence diving heedlessly into something.
21.grammar: A past-tense verb with the -tum ending, meaning 'you (all)' — a completed action by a group being addressed (males or mixed). The base meaning is 'to wade into / plunge into,' often used of engaging in idle or false talk.
21.root: خ-و-ض (kh-w-ḍ) — to wade into water; to plunge into (esp. vain) talk

22.meaning: like the one who / as the one who — a comparison particle joined to a relative pronoun, introducing a single masculine person being likened to something: 'like him who…'.
22.grammar: The ka- prefix is a particle of comparison meaning 'like' or 'as'. Attached to it is the relative pronoun 'the one who / which', which is masculine singular and introduces a following descriptive clause.
22.root: — (comparison particle with relative pronoun)

23.meaning: They plunged in / waded into — they engaged deeply and heedlessly in (especially vain or false) talk or affairs. The image is of wading into water, hence diving recklessly into something.
23.grammar: A past-tense verb in the 'they' form (3rd-person masculine plural): a completed action by a group of males. The -ū ending means 'they.' The long ā inside reflects the base verb 'to wade / plunge into,' often used of indulging in idle or false talk.
23.root: خ-و-ض (kh-w-ḍ) — to wade into water; to plunge into (esp. vain) talk

24.meaning: 'those / those ones' — a demonstrative pointing to a group of people or things at a distance ('those there').
24.grammar: A plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those.' The -ka element adds the sense of pointing to something farther off (as opposed to 'these' near at hand). Being a fixed pronoun, it keeps one form regardless of case.
24.root: — (demonstrative; no root)

25.meaning: It came to nothing / became void / was wasted — of deeds, to be rendered worthless and to lose all reward.

parts.en: to come to nothing / be nullified

25.grammar: A past-tense verb describing a completed event. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('it/she'), used because the thing that becomes void (e.g. 'deeds') is grammatically feminine. The root pictures effort that swells up and then bursts into nothing.
25.root: ح-ب-ط (ḥ-b-ṭ) — coming to nothing, nullification of works

26.meaning: Their deeds / works / actions — the things they have done.
26.grammar: A broken (irregular) plural of 'deed', meaning 'deeds/works'. The attached -hum means 'their' (masculine plural), forming a possessive link. The -u before the pronoun is nominative, marking the whole phrase ('their deeds') as a subject. The -hum form keeps its u-vowel after this nominative ending.
26.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — working, doing, action

27.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
27.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

28.meaning: 'The nearer (life) / this world' — literally 'the nearest/lowest,' a name for the present worldly life as opposed to the Hereafter.
28.grammar: The definite article al- with dunyā, a feminine superlative/elative adjective ('the nearest, the lowest') used as a name for the present world. Its ending (alif maqṣūra) is invariable — it does not change for case — and it commonly describes 'the [worldly] life.'
28.root: د-ن-و (d-n-w) — nearness, being close or low; hence the 'near' present world

29.meaning: And the Hereafter / the final, lasting life — the world to come after death, contrasted with the present worldly life.
29.grammar: The prefix wa- means 'and' and al- means 'the'. The stem is a feminine adjective used as a noun, 'the Last (abode/life)', i.e. the Hereafter. The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun or follows a preposition or oath particle.
29.root: أ-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being last, coming after, the end

30.meaning: The compound 'and those (people); and these / such ones' — the connector 'and' joined to a far-pointing demonstrative meaning 'those' / 'such people'. The demonstrative points collectively to a group already in view, singling them out as 'those very ones'.
30.grammar: The connective 'and' (wa-) prefixed to a plural demonstrative pronoun, 'those'. As a demonstrative it does not take case endings; it is fixed in form. The final -ka is a particle of address/distance built into the word, giving the 'that/those (over there)' sense and pointing to a group of people.

31.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (masculine plural). Standing on its own, it typically adds emphasis or marks the group out as the focus ('they, specifically', 'it is they who').
31.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It takes no case endings; the base is hum, and the final vowel appears as -u (humu) as a connecting vowel to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a definite article. Standing alone, it commonly emphasises or isolates the subject.

32.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'the losers' or 'those who suffer loss' — people who end up in ruin, having forfeited what is of true value.
32.grammar: Definite plural noun (active participle in form) with the article al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine 'sound' plural in the nominative case (the form used for a subject or predicate). The participle names the agent: 'those who incur loss'.
32.root: خ-س-ر (kh-s-r) — to lose, suffer loss, be ruined

1.meaning: 'Did not…?' — a particle combining a question with negation, used to ask 'Have I/has he not…?', often expecting agreement or serving as a gentle reminder.
1.grammar: An interrogative prefix 'a-' ('?') joined to the negation 'lam'. 'lam' negates a verb and places it firmly in the past ('did not'), and grammatically puts the following present-tense verb into the jussive (clipped) form. Together they form a rhetorical or confirming question.

2.meaning: It comes to them / reaches them — said of news, a sign, or an event arriving at someone. From the verb 'to come, arrive, reach.'
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in the 'he/it' form (3rd-person masculine singular). The shortened ending (without a final long vowel) reflects a jussive/subjunctive shape — the form a present verb takes after certain particles (e.g. 'not yet') or in conditions. The attached -him means 'them' (a group of males) as those reached.
2.root: ا-ت-ي (ʾ-t-y) — to come, arrive, reach

3.meaning: Tidings, momentous news, an important report — not just any information, but weighty, significant news of consequence.
3.grammar: A noun in the subject (nominative) form with the -u ending, marking it as the thing being spoken about or the doer of the action (e.g. 'the news came'). 'Naba'' specifically denotes news of importance and significance.
3.root: ن-ب-ا (n-b-ʾ) — to inform, announce; weighty news, tidings

4.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
4.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

5.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
5.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.
5.root: — (preposition)

6.meaning: 'Before them' in time — denoting what came earlier, the period or persons preceding a masculine plural group.
6.grammar: An adverb of time, 'before,' carrying the genitive ending -i because it is linked to a following possessor. The attached 'him' means 'them' (a group of males or a mixed group), giving 'before them.' The -i ending reflects that the word is governed in a possessive link.
6.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to precede, come before; before/prior

7.meaning: "people, folk, nation" — a community or tribe, especially a group bound together by kinship or shared belonging.
7.grammar: A collective noun (grammatically singular, referring to a group). The -i ending is the genitive case, typically linking the word to a following noun ("… OF …") or following a preposition.
7.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a standing group/community

8.meaning: Noah — the proper name of the Prophet Nūḥ.
8.grammar: A proper name. The -in ending (nunation) shows it is treated as a fully declinable noun in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or to link to a preceding word. (Most personal names are partly indeclinable, but this short name takes full case endings.)

9.meaning: And ʿĀd — the name of an ancient Arabian people (the nation of the prophet Hūd), proverbial for their power and their destruction after rejecting their messenger.
9.grammar: A proper name (a people) carrying the -in ending (indefinite genitive 'tanwīn'), the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of …'). Here it takes regular case endings (it is 'fully inflected').

10.meaning: And Thamūd — the name of an ancient Arabian people (the nation of the prophet Ṣāliḥ), known for carving homes in the rock and destroyed after rejecting their messenger.
10.grammar: A proper name (a people) with an -a ending and no 'tanwīn' (no final -n): it is 'diptote,' meaning it does not take the indefinite -n and uses -a for both the object and the after-preposition/linked positions. So this single -a form covers what would otherwise be two different case endings.
10.root: — (proper name)
