13.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
13.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

14.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
14.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

15.meaning: A name/quality meaning 'the One who constantly turns with forgiveness' — the Ever-Relenting, who again and again accepts the repentance of those who turn back to Him. The intensive form stresses how abundantly and repeatedly He forgives.
15.grammar: The definite article l- ('the') with a noun in the intensive pattern (faʿʿāl), which signals doing something abundantly or habitually — here, turning to forgive again and again. The -u ending marks nominative case, typical of a subject or a word describing/identifying the subject.
15.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — turning back, repentance, returning

16.meaning: A name/quality meaning 'the Most Merciful' or 'the Bestower of mercy' — the One whose mercy is deeply felt and continually shown to His creation.
16.grammar: The definite article l- ('the') with an intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality of mercy. The -u ending marks nominative case, typical of a subject or of a word describing/identifying the subject.

1.meaning: "And say" — a command addressed to one male to speak or proclaim words.
1.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a single male ("you"). The base imperative is qul; the final -i here is a helping vowel added only to ease pronunciation before a following word beginning with a cluster — it is not a case or tense ending.

2.meaning: A command addressed to a group: 'Do!', 'Act!', 'Work!' — an imperative urging people to carry out deeds or labor.
2.grammar: An imperative (command) verb addressed to a plural 'you'. The '-ū' ending is the plural-subject marker, so it commands more than one person: 'all of you, do/act'. The initial alif is a helping vowel to begin the word.
2.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, to work, to act; deeds

3.meaning: "Then He / it will see" — the prefixed particle adds near-future force ("soon, presently") to the verb "to see, perceive, behold."
3.grammar: A present-tense verb (root ending in a weak letter, hence the long -ā) with the ya- prefix for "he," preceded by sa- marking the near future ("will / shall soon") and fa- meaning "then/so." Because the verb ends in a weak letter, its tense ending is hidden in the long final vowel.

4.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
4.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

5.meaning: Your deed(s) / work / action; what you (a group) do or accomplish. Joins the noun 'deed' with the possessor 'your'.
5.grammar: The noun 'deed/work' carrying the -a ending (accusative), which typically marks it as the object of a verb (the thing being done, seen, or affected), plus the possessive pronoun -kum 'your' (addressing a group).
5.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deed

6.meaning: "And His Messenger," the one sent with a message; "rasūl" denotes an envoy or apostle commissioned to deliver something, here belonging to "Him."
6.grammar: The "wa-" prefix means "and." The base "rasūl" is a noun of the faʿūl pattern meaning "one who is sent." The suffix "-hu" is the attached possessive pronoun "his," placing the noun in a possessive "messenger of Him" relationship; the pronoun occupies the genitive slot.
6.root: ر-س-ل (r-s-l) — to send; a message or the one sent with it

7.meaning: "and the believers" — those who have faith, who accept and trust; wa- joins it on and al- makes it definite ('the believers' as a group).
7.grammar: A masculine sound plural noun, 'believers.' The -ūna ending is the subject (nominative) form of the masculine plural, used when the word is the one doing the action; the matching object/possessive form would be -īna.
7.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — safety, security, faith, trust

8.meaning: "And you will be brought back / returned" — a passive: the subjects do not act but are made to return to someone or something. Addressed to a group.
8.grammar: A present-tense passive verb ("are/will be returned") with sa- marking the near future. The ta-…-ūna frame means "you" addressing a group of males; the ta- is the ordinary 2nd-person prefix — the same one used in the active — and the -ūna ending is the plain present form for a plural "you" subject. The passive is not a separate prefix but a vowel pattern: the prefix carries u (tu-) instead of the active a, and the stem takes -a- (-radd-), signalling that the action is done to the subject.
8.root: ر-د-د (r-d-d) — to return, send back, restore

9.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
9.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

10.meaning: 'Knower' — one who knows; specifically the active participle naming the one possessing knowledge. In its fullest sense it points to a knower of all things, both the hidden and the visible.
10.grammar: An active participle (a 'doer' noun: 'one who knows'). The final -i is the genitive case: it typically links the word to a following noun ('Knower OF …') or follows a preposition. The bare, unnunated ending also signals that the word is in a possessive construction with what follows it.
10.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — to know, knowledge

11.meaning: The unseen / the hidden realm — that which lies beyond perception and human knowledge: the realm and matters concealed from the senses, known fully only to Allah.
11.grammar: A masculine noun with the definite article al-. The final -i is the genitive ending, which marks the word as following a preposition or as the second term in a possessive link ('… of the unseen').
11.root: غ-ي-ب (gh-y-b) — to be absent, hidden, beyond perception

12.meaning: And the witnessed / the seen — joined by 'and,' this is the realm of what is visible, present, and openly perceived; the opposite of the hidden or unseen. (The word also carries the senses of testimony and witnessing.)
12.grammar: 'and' + definite feminine noun. The wa- prefix means 'and,' al- means 'the.' The final -i is the genitive case ending, typically appearing after a preposition or in an 'of' linkage with a preceding noun.
12.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, be present, testify

13.meaning: 'Then He will inform / tell you' — a verb of announcing weighty news or disclosing what was unknown, with 'He' as the informer and 'you (plural)' as those informed; preceded by 'then/so', linking it to what comes before.
13.grammar: A present-tense verb in the intensive pattern (faʿʿala: 'to inform thoroughly'), prefixed with fa- ('then/so') which connects it to a preceding statement as a result. The yu- prefix marks 'he'; the -u ending is the indicative mood, marking a plain, ongoing or future fact. The attached -kum is the object 'you (a group)'.

14.meaning: A phrase meaning 'in/with that which' or 'in what' — combining the sense of 'by means of' or 'concerning' with an unspecified thing ('whatever it may be').
14.grammar: The preposition bi ('in, with, by means of, concerning') attached to the relative/indefinite pronoun mā ('what, that which'). Both elements are invariable, so the phrase carries no case ending. A word governed by the preposition bi is understood to be in the genitive relationship.

15.meaning: A past-tense verb of 'being' addressed to a group: 'you (all) were', 'you (all) used to be'. From kāna, the core verb 'to be'. With a following predicate it often means 'you were (in a state of) …' or 'you used to …'.
15.grammar: This is a past-tense verb. The '-tum' suffix is the attached subject marker for a masculine plural 'you all'. Since the doer is built into the suffix, the verb stands in its base past form ('you all were').
15.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — to be, to exist, to come to be

16.meaning: You (all) do / work / act — to carry out deeds or labor.
16.grammar: A present-tense verb (Form I). The 'ta-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks the second-person masculine plural ('you all'). The '-ūna' (with final 'n') is the indicative form, marking a plain ongoing or habitual statement.
16.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: And others — additional ones, different persons besides those already mentioned. The base word means 'others/other ones', here in the masculine plural with the connector 'and'.
1.grammar: A noun/adjective 'other(s)' in the masculine plural. The -ūna ending is the sound masculine plural in the subject/nominative form — marking it as the subject or as something simply named. The opening wa is 'and'.
1.root: ا-خ-ر (ʾ-kh-r) — being later, an 'other', the remaining

2.meaning: "Ones who are deferred / postponed / left waiting" — people whose matter is held back and put off, their fate suspended pending a decision. A passive description of those being delayed.
2.grammar: A passive participle (a "being-…ed" describing word) in the masculine plural, naming those to whom the action is done. The -ūna/-na ending marks a plural masculine group in the subject/naming case; the mu- prefix with this pattern signals the passive ("ones who are deferred").
2.root: ر-ج-و (r-j-w) — to defer, postpone; also to hope

3.meaning: "For / to the command, affair, or matter" — the noun amr means an order or decree, and also a matter or affair; the prefix li- means "for" or "belonging to."
3.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition li- ("for, to, belonging to"). The final -i is the genitive ending, which is the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ("… of …").
3.root: ا-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command; a matter or affair

4.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
4.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

5.meaning: A conditional particle meaning 'if' or 'whether'; it often introduces alternatives ('if … or'/'whether … or'), pairing two possibilities. It is essentially 'in' (if) reinforced with 'mā', strengthening the conditional sense.
5.grammar: A particle, not a noun or verb, so it has no case ending. It functions as a connector that sets up a condition or a choice between options ('either … or', 'whether … or'), and it does not change form.

6.meaning: "He punishes / torments them" — to inflict punishment or chastisement upon a group; describes an ongoing or potential punishing. Includes the object "them."
6.grammar: A present-tense verb in an intensive pattern (doubled middle letter, meaning to punish severely or repeatedly) with the yu- prefix for "he," and the attached object pronoun -hum ("them," a male group). The -u vowel before the pronoun marks the plain present tense (not negated or commanded).
6.root: ع-ذ-ب (ʿ-dh-b) — to punish, torment, chastise

7.meaning: And if (ever), and whenever. Combines 'and' with a conditional particle that introduces a possibility, often paired with an emphatic verb ('and should it ever happen that...').
7.grammar: The conjunction wa- ('and') plus immā, a conditional particle (the conditional 'in' fused with emphatic '-mā'). It sets up a hypothetical — 'and if it should ever be that...' — and frequently precedes a verb stressed with a heavy 'definitely' ending.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: 'He/it turns in relenting / accepts repentance' — from tāba; of Allah it means He relents toward and accepts the return of a servant; of a person, he turns back to Allah.
8.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya- prefix marks a masculine singular subject, 'he/it.' The final -u ending is the ordinary present-tense (indicative) marker, indicating an action that is happening or customary.
8.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

9.meaning: A compound meaning 'upon them' or 'against them': the preposition ʿalā ('on, upon, over, against') joined to the plural pronoun 'them'. It conveys something resting on, being incumbent upon, or weighing against a group.
9.grammar: ʿalā shifts to the form ʿalay- before a pronoun. The suffix -him is the attached pronominal suffix for a masculine plural group ('them'); after a preposition it carries genitive/prepositional force, and the -i- vowel reflects its position after this preposition. Together they signal a relationship of something being over, upon, or burdensome to that group.
9.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

10.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
10.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
10.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

11.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
11.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.
11.root: ع-ل-م (ʿ-l-m) — knowledge, knowing

12.meaning: All-Wise: possessing perfect wisdom — placing everything in its right place with flawless knowledge, judgment, and purpose. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's consummate wisdom.
12.grammar: A masculine singular adjective/intensive noun on the faʿīl pattern, expressing a deep, settled quality of wisdom. The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and nominative — the case used for a subject or, very often, a predicate describing the doer ('[He is] All-Wise').
12.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, to be wise

1.meaning: 'And those who': a connective phrase introducing a specified group of people (masculine plural) about whom something will be said. It links them to what came before.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to the relative pronoun alladhīna ('those who'), which is masculine plural. A relative pronoun stands for a group and is normally followed by a clause describing them. Its form does not change for case; it stays alladhīna whatever its grammatical role.

2.meaning: Past-tense verb (reflexive form), third person plural: 'they took for themselves, adopted, chose.' A completed act of taking something on as one's own.
2.grammar: A completed-action (past) verb in a reflexive pattern (taking something for oneself). The '-ū' ending (with silent trailing alif) marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural). The opening 'i-' is a helping vowel that lets the cluster of consonants be pronounced.
2.root: أ-خ-ذ (ʾ-kh-dh) — to take, seize, grasp

3.meaning: "A place of prostration / a mosque" — a place where one bows down in worship; the building or spot set aside for prayer to Allah.
3.grammar: A singular masculine noun of place (the ma- prefix in its root form names the place where an action happens — here, the place of prostration). The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite ("a …") and in the object/accusative case.
3.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down in worship

4.meaning: Harming, injury, causing damage; the act of inflicting hurt or harm on someone, especially deliberately. The form suggests mutual or persistent harm-doing.
4.grammar: A verbal noun (naming the action itself) carrying the indefinite object (accusative) -an ending. In this case form it often functions to express purpose or manner — 'as harm' or 'so as to cause harm'.

5.meaning: And disbelief — the rejection of faith. Its root sense is to 'cover up' or conceal, so it pictures covering over the truth and being ungrateful for it.
5.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and' (its w is doubled in pronunciation to link smoothly). A verbal noun. The final -an (tanwīn) marks the accusative, indefinite case — used for the object of a verb or to specify a respect ('in respect of disbelief').
5.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover/conceal; to disbelieve, to be ungrateful

6.meaning: "And (as a means of) division / causing disunity" — splitting people apart and breaking their unity into factions. A verbal noun naming the act of dividing.
6.grammar: A verbal noun (the action of an intensive verb, naming the act of separating/dividing) in the masculine. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the object/accusative case — often expressing purpose ("as a means of …").
6.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to separate, split, divide

7.meaning: Between; in the midst of two things. An adverb of place marking the space separating or lying among parties or points.
7.grammar: An adverb of place ('between'). It always ends in -a and grammatically governs what follows it, putting the following noun(s) into the genitive 'of' relationship. It does not change to show 'the' or a case of its own; the fixed -a is simply how this word is formed.
7.root: ب-ي-ن (b-y-n) — separation, distinction, what lies between

8.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
8.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').

9.meaning: "And (as) a lookout post / an ambush / a means of lying in wait" — a station set up to watch for and lie in wait against someone. A verbal noun naming the act of lying in ambush or the place of it.
9.grammar: A verbal noun (the action of a verb, naming the act of watching for / lying in wait) in the masculine. The final -an (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the object/accusative case, often expressing purpose ("as …").
9.root: ر-ص-د (r-ṣ-d) — to watch, observe, lie in wait

10.meaning: A combined expression meaning 'to whom?' or 'for whom?' — it asks about the owner or the one to whom something belongs. It fuses the preposition 'to/for' with the question word 'who'.
10.grammar: A preposition ('to/for') joined to the interrogative 'who'. Together they pose the question 'to whom (does it belong)?'. The combination is fixed in form and does not change its ending.

11.meaning: "He waged war / fought / made war" — to engage in armed conflict and hostility against someone. A completed action.
11.grammar: A past-tense verb in the mutual/reciprocal pattern (the long ā after the first letter signals doing something against another — here, warring with). The bare stem with final -a means "he" did it (third-person masculine singular).
11.root: ح-ر-ب (ḥ-r-b) — war, fighting, hostility

12.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
12.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

13.meaning: 'And His Messenger' — the one sent with a message, an envoy or apostle, here joined by 'and' and tagged with 'His' (referring to Allah).
13.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine noun + the attached pronoun 'his'. The -a ending is accusative, marking the noun as an object of a verb; the suffix -hu ('his') links it in possession to a male referent.

14.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
14.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

15.meaning: An adverb of time meaning 'before / beforehand / previously,' pointing to a moment or state that precedes something else in time. When used with the final vowel -u (qablu), it stands cut off from an explicit following noun, conveying 'before(hand)' or 'previously' in an absolute sense — the thing it is 'before' is understood rather than stated.
15.grammar: An adverb of time. The final -u ending here is the indeclinable (mabnī) form taken when the word is severed from a following genitive: rather than 'before X,' it means 'before(hand)' on its own, with the reference point left implicit.
15.root: ق-ب-ل (q-b-l) — to come before, precede, be in front; to receive/accept

16.meaning: "And they will surely swear / take an oath" — to make a solemn oath; with two emphasis-markers attached, it conveys an absolute, certain insistence ("they will most assuredly swear").
16.grammar: A present/future-tense verb with the emphatic la- ("surely") at the front and the heavy emphatic ending -nna at the close — a combination giving the strongest assertion that the action will happen. The ya-…-(u)nna frame here carries a plural masculine "they" subject; the doubled -nn replaces the ordinary plural ending under emphasis.
16.root: ح-ل-ف (ḥ-l-f) — to swear, take an oath

17.meaning: The conditional particle 'in', meaning 'if'. It introduces a hypothetical or supposed condition, setting up a consequence that follows ('if … then …').
17.grammar: 'in' is an indeclinable conditional particle; it carries no case or tense ending of its own. It marks the clause after it as a supposition and leads the listener to expect a result clause.

18.meaning: we intended / we desired — to purpose, will, or aim at something. This is the 'we' form of the verb of intending, referring to a completed intention of the speakers.
18.grammar: A past-tense Form IV verb (arāda, 'to will/intend'). The suffix -nā is the subject ending meaning 'we' and marks the action as completed. In the past tense this Form IV verb shows the hamzah-a- prefix (ara-) rather than the present 'u-' prefix.

19.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
19.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
19.root: — (particle)

20.meaning: The best, the finest, the most beautiful (feminine form) — the supremely good outcome or reward; goodness in its highest degree.
20.grammar: A definite noun/adjective in the feminine superlative pattern ('the best, the finest'). Its long final 'ā' is a fixed ending that does not change for case; it denotes the utmost degree of goodness and often names the best reward or recompense.

21.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
21.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
21.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

22.meaning: 'he bears witness / testifies' — to give firm testimony, to attest to the truth of something with certain knowledge.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix means 'he' (the doer), and the -u ending marks the ordinary, unrestricted present tense ('he bears witness / does testify').
22.root: ش-ه-د (sh-h-d) — to witness, testify, be present

23.meaning: 'Indeed they' — the emphatic particle 'inna' ('truly, indeed') joined to the pronoun 'them/they', strongly affirming a statement about a group.
23.grammar: The emphatic particle inna ('indeed / truly'), which strengthens and affirms a sentence, with the attached pronoun -hum ('they'). Inna places its attached noun or pronoun in the accusative, so -hum here functions as 'they' serving as the subject of the emphasized statement ('indeed they...').

24.meaning: "Surely liars / ones who lie." The plural noun "liars" (those who speak falsehood), fronted by an emphatic "la-" meaning "surely / indeed."
24.grammar: An active-participle noun, masculine plural, meaning "ones who lie." The "-ūna" ending is the sound-masculine-plural in the nominative — the case used for a subject or for the completing word of a sentence ("they are …"). The emphatic la- ("surely") often pairs with the affirming particle inna.
24.root: ك-ذ-ب (k-dh-b) — to lie, speak falsehood

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: You stand / rise up — the act of getting to one's feet, taking a standing position; figuratively, to undertake or attend to something.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The 'ta-' prefix marks a second-person singular subject ('you,' one person). The final consonant carries no vowel (jussive/apocopated form), signalling that the verb is governed by a preceding particle such as a negator ('do not …') or conditional.
2.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise, undertake

3.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
3.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

4.meaning: An adverb meaning 'ever / forever / at any time' — used to stress that something will never (or always) be the case throughout all time, especially with a negative to mean 'never, not ever'.
4.grammar: A noun used adverbially. The ending -an is the indefinite accusative, the form regularly used to turn a word into an adverb of time ('… ever / forever'); the -n (nunation) marks it as indefinite. Paired with a negation it strengthens it to 'never, not ever'.

5.meaning: "Indeed a mosque / a place of prostration" — a place set aside for bowing in worship; the la- prefix adds emphasis ("truly, certainly a mosque").
5.grammar: A singular masculine noun of place (the ma- form names the place of an action — the place of prostration) carrying the emphatic prefix la- ("indeed, surely"). The final -un (nunation) marks it as indefinite and in the subject/naming case (nominative).
5.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow down in worship

6.meaning: "It was founded / established / had its foundation laid" — a passive: a building's base was set in place. From the sense of laying a foundation.

parts.en: be founded / have a foundation laid

6.grammar: A past-tense passive verb ("was founded") in an intensive pattern (doubled middle letter). The internal vowels (u-…-i-) mark the passive — the action was done to the subject — and the final -a means "it/he" (third-person masculine singular).
6.root: ا-س-س (ʾ-s-s) — foundation, to establish, lay a base

7.meaning: 'To / before / upon' — a preposition whose core sense is being on top of, above, or directed onto something; with a verb of presenting it carries the directional sense 'to / before / in front of,' and it can also convey obligation ('incumbent upon').
7.grammar: A preposition. Its basic meaning is 'on, upon, over,' but with verbs of displaying or presenting it shades into 'to / before / in front of.' It governs the following noun in the genitive case. It is fixed in form and takes no changing ending of its own (its final long -ā is an unchanging part of the word).
7.root: — (preposition; loosely related to the sense of 'height/elevation')

8.meaning: Taqwā — God-consciousness: a reverent awareness of Allah that moves one to guard against wrongdoing and to do what is right. It is a protective mindfulness, 'guarding oneself' by keeping Allah ever in view.
8.grammar: A noun with the definite article 'al-' ('the'). It ends in a fixed long vowel ('-ā', written as alif maqṣūra) which does not change for case; such words show their grammatical role only by context, not by a changing ending.

9.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
9.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

10.meaning: "First / foremost / earliest" — that which comes before all others in time or rank.
10.grammar: A singular masculine noun/adjective meaning "first." The final -i is the genitive ending — the form a word takes after a preposition or when linked to a following noun ("the first of …").
10.root: ا-و-ل (ʾ-w-l) — to be first, to return to an origin

11.meaning: a day — a day, the basic unit of daytime or a twenty-four-hour span; figuratively a time or occasion.
11.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending marks the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive is the case used after prepositions or to link this noun to a preceding word ('… of a day').
11.root: ي-و-م (y-w-m) — a day, a span of time

12.meaning: An adjective meaning 'more entitled, having a better/greater right, more deserving' of something.
12.grammar: A comparative/superlative adjective on the afʿal pattern, meaning 'more/most entitled'. The final -u is the nominative case ending, the form used when the word serves as the subject or as a predicate describing the subject.
12.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — truth, right, just claim, what is due

13.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
13.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'

14.meaning: "That you stand / you should stand" — to rise and stand upright; can also carry the sense of taking a standing position for worship. Addressed to one male in a softened, non-final mood.
14.grammar: A present-tense verb with the ta- prefix meaning "you" (one male). The final -a is the subjunctive ending, which appears after certain particles (such as "that / so that / to") and gives the sense of a possible, intended, or purposed action rather than a plain statement of fact.

15.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
15.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

16.meaning: 'In it / in him' — the preposition 'in, inside, within' joined to a pronoun referring to a single masculine or neuter thing. It locates something inside or as part of that referent.
16.grammar: A preposition with an attached object pronoun. The pronoun -hi refers to one masculine (or grammatically masculine) thing and stands as the object of the preposition; its vowel is -i because attached pronouns take that shape after the long -i of fi. Together they answer 'in what?' or 'in whom?'.

17.meaning: Men: adult male human beings. The plural noun denotes men as a group, sometimes carrying the sense of people of standing or strength.
17.grammar: A masculine plural noun (the plural of rajul, 'a man'). The -un ending is the nominative case with nunation, marking it as indefinite — 'men' rather than 'the men.'
17.root: ر-ج-ل (r-j-l) — man, manhood; also foot/on foot

18.meaning: "They love / cherish / hold dear" — to feel deep affection or fondness for someone or something. Describes an ongoing or habitual loving by a group.
18.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb with the yu-…-ūna frame meaning "they" (a group of males). The -ūna ending marks the plain present tense for a plural "they" subject (not negated, commanded, or made conditional). The yu- prefix belongs to this verb's particular pattern of loving.
18.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection, to hold dear

19.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
19.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
19.root: — (particle; no root)

20.meaning: "They purify / cleanse themselves" — to make oneself pure and clean, both physically and spiritually. A reflexive, intensive action done by a group to themselves.
20.grammar: A present-tense verb in the reflexive/intensive pattern (the ta- within the stem plus a doubled letter means doing the action thoroughly to oneself — "to purify oneself"). The ya-…-ū frame means "they" (a male group); the bare -ū ending (without final -na) shows the verb is in a softened, non-final mood after a particle such as "that / to."
20.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — purity, cleanliness, to be clean

21.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
21.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
21.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

22.meaning: He loves / likes / holds dear. To have affection for and approval of something or someone.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb in the fourth pattern, third-person masculine singular ('he…'). The yu- prefix signals a single masculine subject, and the final -u ending marks the indicative mood, presenting the action as an established fact or ongoing reality.
22.root: ح-ب-ب (ḥ-b-b) — love, affection; to hold dear

23.meaning: "Those who purify / cleanse themselves" — people characterized by making themselves pure and clean. A doer-noun describing such persons.
23.grammar: A definite active participle (a "doer" describing-word) in a reflexive pattern ("ones who purify themselves"), masculine plural, with the prefix al- ("the"). The -īna ending marks a plural masculine group in the object or genitive case — the form used as the object of an action, after a preposition, or linked to a following noun.
23.root: ط-ه-ر (ṭ-h-r) — purity, cleanliness, to be clean

1.meaning: An interrogative formed from three pieces meaning roughly 'Is then the one who…?' It opens a rhetorical question that compares two parties. The 'a-' is a question marker, 'fa-' links to a preceding statement and means 'then/so', and 'man' is the relative pronoun 'the one who / whoever'.
1.grammar: A combination of particles plus the relative pronoun 'man'. The leading 'a-' turns the sentence into a yes/no question (often rhetorical). 'fa-' is a connective meaning 'then/so', tying the question to what came before. 'man' refers to a person and introduces a clause describing them ('the one who…'); it does not change its ending for case.

2.meaning: He founded, established, or laid the foundation of something — to set the base or groundwork on which a structure rests.
2.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in the basic third-person masculine singular form: 'he founded'. The doubled middle consonant marks an intensive/causative pattern (Form II), giving the sense of deliberately laying a foundation. The final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending for 'he'.
2.root: أ-س-س ('-s-s) — foundation, to found

3.meaning: His building or structure — a constructed edifice belonging to him, joined with the pronoun 'his'.
3.grammar: A noun meaning 'building/edifice' with the attached possessive pronoun '-hu' ('his/its'). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used when a noun is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The suffix '-hu' marks third-person masculine singular ownership.

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

5.meaning: Taqwā — God-consciousness: a vigilant, reverent awareness of Allah that makes one guard against wrongdoing and shield oneself by obeying Him. Often rendered 'piety' or 'fear of Allah', but its core is protective mindfulness of the divine.
5.grammar: A feminine verbal noun ending in a long final 'ā' (written with the dagger-alif / alif maqṣūra). Because it ends in this fixed long vowel, its ending does not change for grammatical case. It names an abstract quality — the state of being mindfully on guard before Allah.
5.root: و-ق-ي (w-q-y) — to guard, protect, shield

6.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
6.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

7.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
7.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

8.meaning: Good pleasure, acceptance, and approval — especially the gracious good pleasure of Allah, His being pleased with someone, which is the highest of favors.
8.grammar: The prefix 'wa-' means 'and'. The word is a verbal noun ('good pleasure'). The ending '-in' (with tanwīn, an unattached 'n' sound) marks the genitive case and indefiniteness — typically following a preposition or linked after another noun ('… of good pleasure').
8.root: ر-ض-و / ر-ض-ي (r-ḍ-w / r-ḍ-y) — to be pleased, content, satisfied

9.meaning: 'Better / best; good' — an adjective of comparison meaning more good, preferable, or superior. It also serves broadly for 'goodness' and that which is good and beneficial.
9.grammar: A noun/adjective bearing the ending -un (nunation): the doubled-u 'n' sound marks the word as both indefinite ('a/an', no 'the') and nominative — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the predicate that describes it.
9.root: خ-ي-ر (kh-y-r) — good, goodness, that which is choice and beneficial

10.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'or', specifically the 'or' that pairs with a preceding question to offer an alternative ('…or…?'). It links two possibilities being weighed against each other, often after an opening interrogative.

parts.en: or (in alternatives, esp. after a question)

10.grammar: An indeclinable particle (no case or tense ending). It typically introduces the second branch of a two-part question or a balanced alternative, presenting the two as equally consequential.
10.root: — (particle; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
11.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

12.meaning: He founded, established, or laid the foundation of something — to set the base or groundwork on which a structure rests.
12.grammar: A past-tense (completed-action) verb in the basic third-person masculine singular form: 'he founded'. The doubled middle consonant marks an intensive/causative pattern (Form II), giving the sense of deliberately laying a foundation. The final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending for 'he'.

13.meaning: His building or structure — a constructed edifice belonging to him, joined with the pronoun 'his'.
13.grammar: A noun meaning 'building/edifice' with the attached possessive pronoun '-hu' ('his/its'). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used when a noun is the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). The suffix '-hu' marks third-person masculine singular ownership.

14.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'on' or 'upon' — resting on top of, or being over something. By extension it carries ideas of obligation ('it is upon someone to…'), being upheld or guided by something, or being against something, depending on usage.
14.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable (its form never changes) and it governs the following noun, putting it in the genitive case. Its basic spatial meaning is 'on top of / over'.

15.meaning: The edge, brink, or rim of something — the very lip of a drop or hollow, the point right before falling in.
15.grammar: A noun meaning 'edge/brink'. It ends in a fixed long ā and does not change its shape for case, so the ending carries no separate case marker. It commonly stands in front of another noun to mean 'the edge OF …', evoking the narrow margin at the very lip of something.
15.root: ش-ف-و (sh-f-w) — edge, brink, rim

16.meaning: A bank or edge that has been undercut and eroded — the crumbling brink of a cliff or ravine that has been hollowed out underneath and is liable to give way.
16.grammar: A masculine noun in the indefinite genitive case. The '-in' ending (nunation) signals both that it is indefinite ('a…') and in the genitive case — the case used after a preposition or when one noun is linked to another in an 'of' relationship.

17.meaning: Crumbling, tottering, on the verge of collapse — describing something so weakened it is about to fall apart.
17.grammar: An active participle (a describing word, like an adjective) meaning 'crumbling/collapsing'. It is indefinite and in the genitive case, shown by the '-in' ending (nunation), which commonly appears when the word describes a preceding genitive noun or follows a preposition.

18.meaning: So it collapsed — and so it caved in and crumbled down. Built from 'fa-' ('so/then') plus a verb describing a structure or mass falling apart.
18.grammar: The connective 'fa-' ('so/then', expressing result or sequence) attached to a past-tense verb in the reflexive/passive-effect pattern (Form VII), meaning 'it collapsed of itself'. The final '-a' is the past-tense ending for third-person masculine singular ('it/he').

19.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
19.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

20.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
20.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

21.meaning: Fire — blaze, flame; the burning element, and by extension the Fire of punishment.
21.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The -i (genitive) ending typically marks the word as following a preposition (e.g. 'in / from the fire') or as the second term of a possessive phrase ('… OF the fire').
21.root: ن-و-ر (n-w-r) — blazing, giving off light and heat; the source of fire and flame

22.meaning: Jahannam — a proper name for the Fire of punishment in the Hereafter, the abode of torment. It is a name rather than a descriptive common noun.
22.grammar: A proper name. Because it is a special, non-fully-inflecting noun (it does not take tanwīn), it shows the -a ending in places where most nouns would otherwise take -i; here the single -a serves for both accusative and genitive positions. As a name it carries no general dictionary 'meaning' but designates the abode of punishment.
22.root: — (a proper name; commonly treated as having no Arabic triliteral root)

23.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
23.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
23.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

24.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
24.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

25.meaning: 'He guides / leads on the right way' — to show someone the correct path, direct them rightly, or lead them to a goal, whether literally or in matters of belief and conduct.
25.grammar: A present-tense verb, third-person masculine singular: the ya- prefix means 'he'. The verb ends in a long -ī (a weak final letter); in this indicative form the long vowel stands in place of the usual -u mood marker, still conveying a plain, ongoing statement ('he guides').
25.root: ه-د-ي (h-d-y) — guidance, showing the way, leading rightly

26.meaning: the people / the folk — a body of people, a community or group regarded collectively (here in the accusative form).
26.grammar: The l- prefix is the definite article 'the'. The final -a ending is accusative. Since the verb it follows is passive (and so takes no direct object), this accusative is adverbial — marking the circumstance or setting of the action ('before / in front of the people') rather than a thing being acted upon.
26.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to arise; a people standing together

27.meaning: The wrongdoers — those who do wrong or injustice; literally those who put things out of their rightful place, transgressing limits and harming themselves or others. The root sense is darkness.
27.grammar: 'al-' is 'the' (its 'l' assimilates into the 'ẓ', doubling it). The stem is an active participle ('one who wrongs') made plural for masculine people. The -īna ending is the object/genitive form of the sound masculine plural, marking the word as an object of a verb or governed by a preposition.

1.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
1.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

2.meaning: A verb meaning 'to cease / to stop being'. In negative constructions ('does not cease…') it conveys continuity — that something keeps on being the case.
2.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb, third-person masculine singular ('he/it ceases'). The 'ya-' prefix marks 'he/it', and the final '-u' is the ending used when the verb stands in its plain indefinite (indicative) state, expressing ongoing or general action. This is one of the 'sisters of kāna', typically paired with a negation to mean 'keeps on / still is'.
2.root: ز-و-ل (z-w-l) — to cease, depart, pass away

3.meaning: Their building or structure — a constructed edifice belonging to them (a group), joined with the pronoun 'their'.
3.grammar: A noun 'building' with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their', for a masculine group), here voweled '-humu' for ease of pronunciation before a following word. The '-u' before the suffix is the nominative ending, the case typically used when the noun is the subject (the doer or topic of the sentence).

4.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
4.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

5.meaning: They built / they constructed — a group of people raised up a structure.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they built'). The '-aw' ending marks 'they' (a masculine group) as the doers; the trailing alif is a silent spelling convention that accompanies this plural ending and is not pronounced.
5.root: ب-ن-ي (b-n-y) — to build

6.meaning: A source of nagging doubt and disquiet — misgiving, suspicion, or unease that unsettles the heart and prevents settled certainty.
6.grammar: A feminine singular noun, indefinite and in the accusative case. The final '-tan' combines the feminine ending with nunation (the '-an' that marks both indefiniteness and the accusative). The accusative is the case used for the direct object of a verb or similar roles.
6.root: ر-ي-ب (r-y-b) — doubt, suspicion, disquiet

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
7.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
7.root: — (particle)

8.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
8.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
8.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

9.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
9.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

10.meaning: A particle meaning 'that / to,' used to introduce a following verb and turn the action into something like a noun ('that he should do…' or 'to do…'). It links a verb to what comes before, often after verbs of wishing, intending, or being able.
10.grammar: A subordinating particle that places the following present-tense verb into the subjunctive mood, so the verb's final vowel becomes -a. It bundles the verb into a noun-like clause meaning 'to …' or 'that … should …'
10.root: — (particle; no root)

11.meaning: It was torn to pieces / cut up into fragments — to be repeatedly and thoroughly severed or shredded apart.

parts.en: it was cut to pieces / fell to pieces

11.grammar: A past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular. Its pattern (Form V, with the 'ta-' prefix and doubled middle consonant) conveys an intensive action turned back on the subject — being cut up repeatedly or falling to pieces. The final '-a' is the standard past-tense ending for 'he/it'.
11.root: ق-ط-ع (q-ṭ-ʿ) — to cut, sever

12.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the hearts belonging to a masculine plural group. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' is the seat of understanding, intention, feeling, and faith, not merely the physical organ.
12.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') in the nominative, shown by the -u before the pronoun, which typically marks it as the subject of a sentence. The attached 'hum' means 'their' (a group of males or mixed group), giving 'their hearts.'
12.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, fluctuate

13.meaning: 'and Allah' — the conjunction 'and' joined to the proper name Allah, the unique divine name of the One God.
13.grammar: A conjunction plus a proper name. wa- means 'and'. The name ends in -u, the nominative case, which typically marks the subject of a sentence or the word that begins a statement about it.
13.root: Most Arabic grammarians derive Allāh from إله (ʾilāh, 'deity / god'), root ʾ-l-h, with the definite article fused on ('the God'); some treat the name as a unique proper noun without a derived root.

14.meaning: An intensive adjective/name meaning 'All-Knowing / fully aware' — one whose knowledge is complete, deep, and all-encompassing; as a divine attribute it denotes Allah's perfect knowledge.
14.grammar: An intensive adjective (the pattern faʿīl conveys 'thoroughly, abundantly'). The ending -un is the indefinite nominative — the nominative case marks it as the subject or the quality being affirmed, and the -n (nunation) signals 'a / an', i.e. indefinite. So it reads '(is) all-knowing'.

15.meaning: 'All-Wise,' 'profoundly wise.' It describes one whose every judgement, decree, and act is perfectly sound, fitting, and placed exactly where it should be. As a divine attribute of Allah it points to flawless wisdom in all things.
15.grammar: An intensive adjective on the faʿīl pattern, conveying a deep, settled quality of wisdom. It is in the nominative case with indefinite marking, shown by -un, the form used for a predicate or descriptive noun that is not made definite.
15.root: ح-ك-م (ḥ-k-m) — to judge, decide wisely; wisdom, governance

1.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
1.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

2.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
2.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.
2.root: — (proper name)

3.meaning: He bought / purchased — and, by extension, he traded or bartered one thing for another, exchanging something he has for something he wants.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the reflexive/self-interested pattern (Form VIII), meaning 'he bought/acquired for himself'. It is third-person masculine singular ('he'), ending in the long final 'ā' (written with alif maqṣūra) characteristic of verbs whose root ends in a weak letter.
3.root: ش-ر-ي (sh-r-y) — to buy/sell, to trade or exchange

4.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
4.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

5.meaning: A plural noun meaning 'the believers' — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm. The Form IV participle denotes one who brings about belief and security within.
5.grammar: A definite plural active participle of Form IV (āmana 'to believe'). The -īna ending marks a sound masculine plural in the accusative/genitive (object or oblique) state. The prefixed mu- marks it as a Form IV participle ('one who has/gives faith').
5.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — faith, safety, security

6.meaning: A noun meaning 'their own selves' or 'themselves' — the plural of 'nafs' (self, soul, person, inner self), joined to the pronoun 'their.' It commonly conveys the reflexive idea of acting upon one's own self.
6.grammar: A noun (a broken/irregular plural of 'nafs') with the attached possessive pronoun '-hum' ('their/them,' masculine plural). The -a case ending before the pronoun is accusative, typically marking the word as the direct object of a verb — i.e. the self upon which the action falls.
6.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self, soul, person; breath

7.meaning: And their wealth / their possessions — material property and riches belonging to them (a group), joined with 'and' and the pronoun 'their'.
7.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') joined to the plural noun 'amwāl' ('wealth/properties') with the attached possessive '-hum' ('their'). The '-a' before the pronoun is the accusative ending, the case typically used when the noun is the direct object of a verb. 'amwāl' is itself a broken plural of 'māl' (property).
7.root: م-و-ل (m-w-l) — wealth, property

8.meaning: A two-part connector meaning 'because / by reason of the fact that'. It combines the preposition 'with/by' and anna ('that…'), together introducing a cause or explanation for what precedes.
8.grammar: The preposition bi- ('with/by') attached to the emphatic particle anna ('that…'). anna introduces and stresses a following statement and grammatically puts the noun after it into the accusative; the pairing as a whole signals 'because / due to the fact that'.

9.meaning: To them / for them — the preposition li- ('to, for') joined to the pronoun 'them'. It expresses that something is directed toward, belongs to, or is for the benefit of a group.
9.grammar: The preposition li- ('to/for') combined with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). When li- takes a pronoun its vowel becomes 'la-'. The final -u here is a connecting vowel added to ease pronunciation before a following word; it carries no case meaning of its own.

10.meaning: The Garden / Paradise — the place of lush, shaded greenery promised as the abode of bliss; literally a garden whose foliage covers the ground.
10.grammar: 'al-' is 'the'. 'janna' is a feminine noun (the tā marbūṭa ending). The final -a is accusative, the form typically marking a word as the object of a verb or, with place-nouns, the destination/location toward which an action occurs.
10.root: ج-ن-ن (j-n-n) — to cover, conceal, hide

11.meaning: 'They fight' or 'they do battle' — engaging in mutual combat or warfare. The pattern (qātala) conveys fighting against an opponent, a reciprocal struggle rather than mere striking.
11.grammar: A present/ongoing-tense verb in the mutual-action pattern (fā'ala) meaning 'to fight against'. The -ūna ending marks a masculine-plural 'they' subject and the indicative mood, which states an action as an ongoing or habitual fact.
11.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — killing, fighting, combat

12.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
12.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

13.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
13.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

14.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
14.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

15.meaning: So they kill / and they slay — built from 'fa-' ('so/then') plus a verb of one group fighting and killing others.
15.grammar: The connective 'fa-' ('so/then') attached to a present/ongoing-tense verb, third-person masculine plural ('they kill'). The 'ya-' prefix marks third-person and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they') in the verb's plain indicative state (ongoing or habitual action).
15.root: ق-ت-ل (q-t-l) — to kill, slay

16.meaning: And they are killed / and they are slain — built from 'wa-' ('and') plus the passive form, where the group are the ones killed rather than the ones killing.
16.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') joined to a present/ongoing-tense verb in the passive voice, third-person masculine plural ('they are killed'). The 'yu-' prefix with the inner 'a' vowel marks the passive (the subject receives the action), and the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural ('they') in the indicative state.

17.meaning: A promise / a pledge — a binding commitment to do something, here in the sense of a solemn assurance given.
17.grammar: A masculine singular verbal noun, indefinite and in the accusative case, shown by the '-an' ending (nunation written over an alif). The accusative often marks a direct object or, as with such verbal nouns, an emphatic confirmation ('… as a promise / a sure promise').

18.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
18.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

19.meaning: A right, a due, or an obligation — that which is true, real, and rightfully owed; an established duty. As an adverbial accusative it conveys "as a duty/obligation, in truth, bindingly."
19.grammar: A noun in the indefinite accusative. The '-an' (nunation on the fatḥa, with a following alif) often functions adverbially here — "as a binding duty" or "in truth" — describing the manner or affirming the statement.
19.root: ح-ق-ق (ḥ-q-q) — to be true, right, established; truth, right

20.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
20.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

21.meaning: The Torah — the revealed scripture given to the Prophet Moses (Mūsā).
21.grammar: The al- prefix means 'the' (its 'l' is pronounced as a doubled 't' merging into the following letter). The final -i is the genitive case, fitting a word that follows a preposition or is linked to a preceding noun ('… of the Torah'). Because it carries 'the', it takes a single -i (not tanwīn).

22.meaning: And the Injīl — the Gospel, the revealed Scripture given to Jesus (ʿĪsā). Joined with 'and' and 'the'.
22.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') plus the definite article 'al-' ('the') on the proper name 'Injīl' (the Gospel). The final '-i' is the genitive ending, the case used after a preposition or when the word is linked to another in an 'of' relationship, or when joined by 'and' to a preceding genitive noun.

23.meaning: And the Qur'ān — the recited Scripture revealed to the Prophet Muḥammad; the name derives from a root meaning 'to recite/read'. Joined with 'and' and 'the'.
23.grammar: The connective 'wa-' ('and') plus the definite article 'al-' ('the') on the noun/name 'Qur'ān'. The final '-i' is the genitive ending — the case used after a preposition, in an 'of' relationship, or when joined by 'and' to a preceding genitive word. The word is a verbal noun meaning 'the reciting/recitation'.

24.meaning: And whoever / and the one who — a joining word plus a relative pronoun introducing a person (or persons) defined by whatever they do; often sets up a condition ('whoever does X …').
24.grammar: A particle 'and' joined to the relative/conditional pronoun man ('whoever, who'). Man does not change its ending; it refers to people and frequently functions as a conditional, so the verb that follows it typically takes the shortened jussive mood.
24.root: — (pronoun/particle; no triliteral root)

25.meaning: A verb meaning 'he fulfilled / he keeps faithfully' — to discharge a commitment or keep a promise completely and faithfully. Here it describes one who fulfills his covenant in full.
25.grammar: A perfect-form (past) verb of the form-IV pattern (af'ala), 3rd-person masculine singular ('he'), built from the root for fulfilling. The initial a- is the form-IV prefix and the final long -ā is the root's weak letter, written as alif maqṣūra. Though the af'al pattern looks identical to an elative ('more/most ___') adjective, here it functions as a verb ('he who fulfills/keeps his pledge').
25.root: و-ف-ي (w-f-y) — to fulfill, complete, keep faithfully, render in full

26.meaning: A noun phrase meaning 'his covenant / his pledge' — a solemn, binding agreement or promise, with the attached pronoun showing it belongs to a male party. A covenant carries the weight of a commitment owed.
26.grammar: A noun preceded by the preposition bi- ('with / by') and followed by the possessive pronoun -hi ('his'). The -i ending is genitive, the case required after a preposition; it links 'covenant' to the preceding particle and to its owner.
26.root: ع-ه-د (ʿ-h-d) — covenant, pledge, binding agreement, charge

27.meaning: 'from,' 'out of,' 'some of' — a preposition marking origin, source, starting-point, or a part taken from a whole. It points to where something comes from or what it is drawn out of.
27.grammar: A preposition meaning 'from / out of.' Its final 'n' is always fully pronounced (min). Here it carries an added '-a' (mina) purely as a helping vowel to join smoothly to a following word that begins with a definite article — the 'n' is still sounded, and the added vowel does not change the meaning.

28.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
28.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

29.meaning: So rejoice! / receive glad tidings! — built from 'fa-' ('so/then') plus a command to a group to be glad and welcome good news with joy.
29.grammar: The connective 'fa-' ('so/then') attached to a command (imperative) verb in the seeking/seeking-for-oneself pattern (Form X), addressed to a masculine plural 'you'. The '-ū' ending marks the plural addressees, and the trailing silent alif is the spelling convention that accompanies it.

30.meaning: In/with your transaction — the buying-and-selling deal or bargain that belongs to you (a group). Built from 'bi-' ('with/in') plus 'sale/transaction' plus 'your'.
30.grammar: The preposition 'bi-' ('with/in/by') joined to the noun 'bayʿ' ('sale/transaction') with the attached possessive '-kum' ('your', masculine plural), voweled '-kumu' before a following word. The '-i' is the genitive ending, required because the noun follows the preposition 'bi-'.

31.meaning: A relative pronoun meaning 'the one who' or 'which' — it points back to a masculine singular person or thing and introduces a clause that describes or identifies it. It works like the English 'who/which/that' that opens a defining clause.
31.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) masculine singular relative pronoun: its form does not change for case, so the ending stays -ī whatever grammatical role it fills. It always needs a following clause to complete its meaning.

32.meaning: You concluded a bargain / pledged a mutual contract — you (a group) entered a binding deal or sworn pact, each side committing to the other (a give-and-take agreement, as in a pledge of allegiance).
32.grammar: A past-tense verb in the mutual/reciprocal pattern (Form III), conveying a two-sided dealing ('you made a deal/pledge with another'). The '-tum' ending marks the doers as a masculine plural 'you' acting in completed past time.
32.root: ب-ي-ع (b-y-ʿ) — to sell, trade; (Form III) to pledge mutually

33.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
33.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

34.meaning: 'And that' — a connective 'and' plus the demonstrative 'that', pointing to something distant or already mentioned (masculine).
34.grammar: Connective 'and' + a masculine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'that (one)'. Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the -ka element is a particle directing attention to a distant referent.

35.meaning: 'He' — the standalone (independent) pronoun for a single masculine person or thing, used for emphasis or to stand as the subject on its own.
35.grammar: An independent (detached) personal pronoun, third-person masculine singular. It does not take case endings; its fixed final -a is part of the word. It serves to name or emphasize the subject ('He is the one who…').

36.meaning: 'The success' / 'the triumph' — attainment of what is sought and safety from what is feared; winning, salvation, the great achievement. With the article it is 'the (true) success'.
36.grammar: A definite masculine noun. The -u ending is the nominative case, marking it as a subject or as the thing identified (e.g. 'that IS the success').
36.root: ف-و-ز (f-w-z) — to win, triumph, attain salvation

37.meaning: 'the Most Great / the Immense' — vast, mighty, and tremendous in greatness and grandeur. As a divine name it conveys overwhelming magnificence and majesty.
37.grammar: A definite adjective/noun in an intensive pattern ('the Magnificent'). The -u ending is nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or for an appositive descriptive title attached to such a subject.
37.root: ع-ظ-م (ʿ-ẓ-m) — to be great, mighty, immense

1.meaning: Those who turn back in repentance — people who repeatedly return to Allah, abandoning wrongdoing and coming back to obedience. 'The' marks them as a defined group.
1.grammar: A definite (with 'al-', 'the') active participle in the masculine plural — 'the ones who repent'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case, the case used when the word is the subject or topic of the sentence (the doers/describers). As a participle it names those characterized by the action of repenting.

2.meaning: Those who worship and serve — people devoted to the worship of Allah, humbly serving Him. 'The' marks them as a defined group.
2.grammar: A definite (with 'al-', 'the') active participle in the masculine plural — 'the ones who worship/serve'. The '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case, used when the word functions as the subject or topic. As a participle it names those characterized by worship and devoted service.
2.root: ع-ب-د (ʿ-b-d) — to worship, serve, devote oneself

3.meaning: Those who praise — people who give praise, expressing gratitude and acknowledging the goodness and worth of the One praised. A plural active participle naming praisers as a steady type or class.
3.grammar: An active participle (the 'one who does X' form) made plural and definite with al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the subject (nominative) case — 'those who…'; it would shift to -īna when the word is an object or follows a preposition.

4.meaning: Those who travel or journey about — and, by extension in religious usage, those who devote themselves through fasting, the soul roaming free of food as a wanderer roams the land. A plural active participle naming such people as a class.
4.grammar: An active participle ('one who does X') made plural and definite with al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the subject (nominative) case — 'those who…'; it becomes -īna in the object/prepositional case.
4.root: س-ي-ح (s-y-ḥ) — to travel, roam, flow forth

5.meaning: Those who bow down — people who bend low in worship, the deep bow of reverence and submission before Allah. A plural active participle naming the bowers as a type.
5.grammar: An active participle ('one who does X') made plural and definite with al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the subject (nominative) case — 'those who…'; it shifts to -īna in the object/prepositional case.
5.root: ر-ك-ع (r-k-ʿ) — to bow, bend the body in worship

6.meaning: Those who prostrate — people who lay themselves down with the forehead to the ground, the posture of utmost humility and submission to Allah. A plural active participle naming the prostrators as a type.
6.grammar: An active participle ('one who does X') made plural and definite with al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the subject (nominative) case — 'those who…'; it becomes -īna in the object/prepositional case.
6.root: س-ج-د (s-j-d) — to prostrate, bow the forehead to the ground

7.meaning: Those who command or enjoin — people who order and urge others toward something, calling them to do it. A plural active participle naming such commanders as a type.
7.grammar: An active participle ('one who does X') made plural and definite with al- ('the'). The -ūna ending marks a masculine sound plural in the subject (nominative) case — 'those who…'; it shifts to -īna in the object/prepositional case.
7.root: ء-م-ر (ʾ-m-r) — to command, order, enjoin

8.meaning: 'In a fitting / honourable / customary way' — bi- ('with/in') joined to al-ma'rūf, literally 'that which is known and recognised', i.e. what is right, decent, and approved by sound custom and morality.

parts.en: what is right / recognised as good

8.grammar: The bi- prefix is a preposition 'with / in'. The l- is 'the'. The stem is a passive participle meaning 'that which is known/recognised (as good)'. The final -i is the genitive case, the form taken after a preposition like bi-.
8.root: ع-ر-ف (ʿ-r-f) — to know, recognise; hence what is recognised as good

9.meaning: And those who forbid — people who prohibit and restrain others from something, warning them away from it. The leading 'and' joins it to a preceding item; the rest is a plural active participle naming such forbidders as a type.
