20.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
20.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

21.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
21.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

22.meaning: It strikes, befalls, or afflicts them — reaching and hitting its target, used of hardship reaching someone.
22.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, the imperfect of the form IV (af'ala) verb 'aṣāba.' The 'yu-' prefix is simply the third-person masculine singular marker ('it/he'); the form IV pattern itself shows in the stem (a short prefix vowel plus the hollow 'ī'). The attached '-hum' ('them') is its object.
22.root: ص-و-ب (ṣ-w-b) — hitting the mark, befalling correctly

23.meaning: Thirst — the craving for water and the distress of going without it.
23.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' ending (tanwīn ḍamma) is indefinite and nominative — the case typically used for the subject of a sentence or the thing simply being named ('thirst').

24.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
24.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

25.meaning: Fatigue, weariness, toil, or hardship — the exhaustion that comes from effort and strain.
25.grammar: A masculine singular noun. The '-un' ending (tanwīn ḍamma) is indefinite and nominative — the case for a subject or a thing simply being named ('fatigue').
25.root: ن-ص-ب (n-ṣ-b) — toil, weariness, exertion (also setting up)

26.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
26.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

27.meaning: Hunger, famine, or the pang of an empty stomach — severe lack of food.
27.grammar: A feminine noun on the 'maf'ala' pattern (a state or occasion of something). The '-un' ending (tanwīn ḍamma) is indefinite and nominative — the case for a subject or a thing being named ('hunger').
27.root: خ-م-ص (kh-m-ṣ) — emptiness of the belly, hunger, leanness

28.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
28.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

29.meaning: 'path, way, road' — a route or course; figuratively a cause or way of life one travels along. In construct ('the way OF ...').
29.grammar: A singular noun with the '-i' (genitive) ending, which typically links it to a following noun ('the way OF ...') or follows a preposition. It marks the word as connected to or possessed by what comes after.

30.meaning: The proper name of the One God in Arabic: 'Allah' — the unique, absolute Deity, the sole object of worship, beside whom there is no other.
30.grammar: This is a proper name. The '-i' ending is the genitive case, the form a noun takes after a preposition or when linked to a preceding noun ('… of Allah', or 'besides Allah'). The leading 'al-' is fused into the name itself.

31.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
31.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

32.meaning: They tread, step on, or set foot upon — placing the foot down on a place or ground.
32.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks a masculine plural 'they …'; the full '-ūna' ending signals the indicative mood — a plain, ongoing statement of fact ('they tread').

33.meaning: A treading-place, a spot where the foot is set — and by extension any ground gained or step taken.
33.grammar: A noun of place on the 'maf'il' pattern ('a place of treading'). The '-an' ending (tanwīn fatḥa) is indefinite and accusative — the case typically used for the object of a verb (the thing trodden or gained).

34.meaning: It enrages, angers, or galls — stirring up fury and resentment in someone.
34.grammar: A present/imperfect verb, the imperfect of the form I hollow verb 'ghāẓa' (a hollow 'y'-type root, whose middle radical surfaces as 'ī' here). The 'ya-' prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject: 'it/he enrages.' Form I of this root already carries the transitive, causative sense ('to make furious').

35.meaning: The disbelievers, those who reject faith — people who actively cover over and deny the truth and are ungrateful for it; an intensive plural stressing entrenched rejection.
35.grammar: An intensive plural on the pattern fuʿʿāl, stressing the strength of rejection. The prefix al- is the definite article 'the'. The final -a is the accusative case ending: it typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon). With the definite article there is no nunation.
35.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, reject, be ungrateful

36.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
36.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

37.meaning: They attain, reach, obtain, or inflict — getting hold of something or bringing it upon another.
37.grammar: A present/imperfect verb. The 'ya-…-ūna' frame marks a masculine plural 'they …'; the full '-ūna' ending signals the indicative mood — a plain statement of fact ('they attain/obtain').

38.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
38.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

39.meaning: A noun/adjective meaning 'an enemy' or 'hostile (party)' — one who shows enmity and opposition.
39.grammar: Noun, masculine singular, indefinite. The final -in (tanwīn kasra) is the indefinite genitive: it typically follows a preposition or links to a preceding noun in an 'of …' relation.

40.meaning: An affliction or harm that befalls someone; a hit or hurt that is suffered or inflicted. From a root meaning to attain or reach, it carries the sense of something that 'lands on' a person — a blow, injury, or setback that touches them.

parts.en: an attaining / something that befalls (harm, hurt)

40.grammar: A masculine indefinite noun. The final -an (accusative, with nunation) marks it as an indefinite object or as something undergone or received; it commonly answers 'what was attained / suffered?' The shadda (doubling) on the nūn is not part of the root — the root ن-ي-ل has a single nūn — but results from a preceding lām (such as the lām of a particle or article) assimilating into the following nūn.
40.root: ن-ي-ل (n-y-l) — to attain, reach, obtain (and so what befalls one)

41.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
41.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.

42.meaning: 'It has been prescribed / decreed / made obligatory' — also literally 'it was written'. A past-tense passive verb conveying that something has been ordained and laid down as a binding command.
42.grammar: The internal vowel pattern (u–i) makes this passive: the action was done, with no doer named. The final -a is the default third-person masculine singular ending of a past-tense verb (it is a verbal person-marker, not a noun's case ending), so the verb reads 'it was prescribed'.

43.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
43.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

44.meaning: 'with it,' 'by it,' 'by means of it' — the instrumental/accompaniment preposition 'with/by' joined to 'it' (referring to a masculine singular thing). It marks the means or instrument through which something is done.
44.grammar: A preposition ('with/by') joined to the attached pronoun '-hi' ('it/him'), referring back to a masculine singular thing. The pronoun takes the '-i' vowel form ('hi') because it follows a word ending in an '-i' sound, marking it as the object of the preposition: 'by means of it.'

45.meaning: A deed, an action, a piece of work — something that a person actively does or performs, whether good or bad. It denotes purposeful conduct and labour, the concrete carrying-out of an act.
45.grammar: A masculine indefinite noun. The final -un (nominative, with nunation) typically marks the word as the subject of a sentence or the thing being identified ('a deed [is] …').

46.meaning: Righteous, upright, sound and wholesome — describing a person or thing that is good, in good order, and acting rightly. As an active participle it pictures one who 'does what is right' and is fit and beneficial.
46.grammar: An active participle used as an adjective, masculine and indefinite. The final -un (nominative, with nunation) marks it as nominative — it commonly describes a nominative noun or stands as a subject/predicate ('[is] righteous').
46.root: ص-ل-ح (ṣ-l-ḥ) — to be sound, good, upright, set right

47.meaning: An emphasis particle placed at the start of a statement to strengthen and affirm it — roughly 'indeed', 'truly', 'verily'. It assures the listener that what follows is certainly the case.
47.grammar: An emphasising particle that introduces a nominal sentence. It puts the following noun (its subject) into the accusative case, while the predicate that comes after stays nominative. Its function is to affirm and stress the whole statement; it carries no tense or person of its own.

48.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
48.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

49.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
49.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

50.meaning: A verb meaning 'he lets go to waste / squanders / allows to be lost'. The core sense is causing something to be neglected, ruined, or forfeited rather than preserved.

parts.en: cause to be lost / let go to waste (stem)

50.grammar: An imperfect verb. The yu- prefix marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it') and identifies the verb as belonging to a derived (augmented) form whose imperfect takes yu- rather than the ya- of the basic form; the meaning here is causative ('to cause to be lost'). The final -u ending marks the indicative mood — a plain statement.
50.root: ض-ي-ع (ḍ-y-ʿ) — to be lost, wasted, neglected

51.meaning: Means 'reward, wage, recompense'. The word denotes the due return for work or conduct — payment, compensation, or the reward earned by deeds.
51.grammar: A noun in the accusative case, shown by the -a ending. The accusative typically marks the direct object of a verb (the thing acted upon, e.g. 'the reward' as what is given or not wasted) or the first term of a possessive pair when it is itself an object ('the reward of…').

52.meaning: 'The doers of good / those who act with excellence and beauty'. It denotes people who do what is good and do it well — acting righteously, generously, and with sincerity, as if conscious of being watched by Allah.

parts.en: good-doers / those who excel in doing good

52.grammar: A definite plural active participle (the 'doer' form of the verb 'to do good'). The prefixed al- means 'the'. The ending -īna marks a sound masculine plural in the object/oblique state — the form used when the noun is a direct object or follows a preposition. It refers to male (or mixed) persons characterized by the action.
52.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — to be good, beautiful; to do well and excellently

1.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
1.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

2.meaning: 'They spend/give out': to expend wealth or provision, especially by giving it away in charity and in good causes. The word centers on disbursing what one has rather than hoarding it.
2.grammar: A present/future-tense verb in Form IV (anfaqa, 'to spend, expend'). The imperfect prefix is only yu-; the nūn that follows is the first root letter (of ن-ف-ق), not part of the prefix. The yu- prefix together with the -ūna ending marks the subject as 'they' (masculine plural) doing the action now or habitually. The -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood, the default 'plain' form used for ongoing or repeated action.
2.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, give out

3.meaning: An expenditure or outlay — that which is spent or given out, especially money or resources laid out for a purpose. It is the noun for the act and amount of spending.
3.grammar: A feminine indefinite noun (the tā' marbūṭa marks the feminine). The final -tan (accusative, with nunation) marks it as an indefinite object — typically the thing affected by the verb ('they spend a … ').
3.root: ن-ف-ق (n-f-q) — to spend, expend, lay out

4.meaning: Small, little, slight in size or amount; also young. It describes something of minor measure or low quantity.
4.grammar: A feminine indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern (tā' marbūṭa for the feminine). The final -tan (accusative, with nunation) marks it as accusative — it typically modifies a feminine accusative noun ('a small …').
4.root: ص-غ-ر (ṣ-gh-r) — to be small, little, young

5.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
5.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

6.meaning: Big, large, great — large in size, amount, or significance. It describes something of major measure or weight, and can also imply 'great' in importance.
6.grammar: A feminine indefinite adjective on the faʿīl pattern (tā' marbūṭa for the feminine). The final -tan (accusative, with nunation) marks it as accusative — it typically modifies a feminine accusative noun ('a big …').
6.root: ك-ب-ر (k-b-r) — to be big, great, large

7.meaning: 'And not' — a connector 'and' joined to the negative particle 'not,' negating a following statement.
7.grammar: Two particles: the joining 'and' (wa) plus the negator lā ('not'). Lā commonly negates a present-tense verb or a noun. Neither particle takes case endings.

8.meaning: They cut, sever, or cross through. From a root meaning to cut, it extends to traversing or 'cutting across' a stretch of ground — covering or passing through a distance.
8.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they (masculine plural) do' the action ongoing or habitually; the final nūn marks the indicative (a plain statement, not a command or subjunctive).

9.meaning: A valley — a watercourse or low-lying tract between hills or mountains, often a dry riverbed that channels water when it rains. By extension, any such stretch of land one travels through.
9.grammar: A masculine indefinite noun (originally a defective/weak noun ending in yā'). The final -an (accusative, with nunation) marks it as an indefinite object — typically the thing affected, e.g. that which is crossed ('a valley').

10.meaning: A particle of exception meaning 'except,' 'save,' or 'only.' It carves out something from a preceding general statement — most often a preceding negation — so that the excepted item alone is affirmed, giving the strong sense 'none … but' or 'nothing other than.'
10.grammar: An exceptive particle (originally a fusion of 'in' + 'lā'). It is invariable — it has no case ending and does not change form. It introduces the item being excepted from, or restricted within, the preceding statement.
10.root: — (particle)

11.meaning: 'It has been prescribed / decreed / made obligatory' — also literally 'it was written'. A past-tense passive verb conveying that something has been ordained and laid down as a binding command.
11.grammar: The internal vowel pattern (u–i) makes this passive: the action was done, with no doer named. The final -a is the default third-person masculine singular ending of a past-tense verb (it is a verbal person-marker, not a noun's case ending), so the verb reads 'it was prescribed'.
11.root: ك-ت-ب (k-t-b) — to write, record, ordain

12.meaning: 'To them' or 'for them' — directing something toward, or assigning it to, a group of males (or a mixed group).
12.grammar: The preposition li- ('to / for'), here voweled 'la-', joined to the attached pronoun -hum ('them'). The preposition expresses direction, recipient, or possession ('to / for'), and -hum identifies a third-person masculine plural object, 'them'.

13.meaning: So that He may repay / reward / requite them — to give back to people the due return for what they have done, whether recompense for good or requital for ill. Combines a purpose particle, the verb 'to repay,' and the object 'them.'
13.grammar: A present-tense verb with the purpose particle li- ('so that'), which puts the verb in the subjunctive — hence the final -a on the stem (yajziya) expressing intended result. The ya- prefix means 'he/it'; the attached -humu is the object 'them' (its vowel shifted to -u before the following word).

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
14.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

15.meaning: A verb meaning 'he did good / acted well, excellently' — to do what is beautiful, fine, and right; also 'he was good (at something)'.
15.grammar: A Form IV (afʿala) past-tense verb, third-person masculine singular 'he'; the bare -a ending marks a completed action by 'he'. Form IV here gives the sense of doing/making good, acting with excellence.
15.root: ح-س-ن (ḥ-s-n) — goodness, beauty, excellence

16.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
16.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

17.meaning: 'They were' or 'they used to' — a past-tense form of the verb 'to be' for a group. It often expresses a continued or habitual state in the past, especially when paired with a following verb ('they used to do...').
17.grammar: A past-tense verb from the verb 'to be'. The -ū ending marks the third-person masculine plural subject, 'they'. As a past form of 'to be', it sets a past frame; with a following present-tense verb it typically conveys a habitual or ongoing past ('they used to...').
17.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existing, coming to be

18.meaning: 'They do / they work, they act' — a present-tense verb of doing and working, covering deeds and actions carried out by a group.
18.grammar: Present/imperfect verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a third-person masculine plural subject, 'they (do).' The -ūna ending also marks the indicative mood, the plain statement form, as opposed to command or negated-future forms.
18.root: ع-م-ل (ʿ-m-l) — to do, work, act; deeds

1.meaning: A connective phrase meaning 'and what' or 'and that which'. It adds a further item and points to an unspecified thing or category.
1.grammar: The connector wa ('and') joined to mā ('what, that which'). Here mā functions as a relative/indefinite pronoun ('that which'); the same word can elsewhere serve as a negator. It is invariable and takes no case ending.

2.meaning: He/it was, or there was — the past tense of the verb 'to be', expressing that something existed or used to be the case.

parts.en: to be, was, used to be

2.grammar: A past-tense verb (a 'hollow' verb of being), third-person masculine singular ('he/it was'). The final '-a' marks the ordinary past tense for 'he/it'. Paired with a following present-tense verb, it often conveys 'used to' do something.
2.root: ك-و-ن (k-w-n) — being, existence; to be

3.meaning: The believers — those who have faith, who inwardly trust and affirm the truth and give it their security and assent.
3.grammar: A definite noun, the active participle of form IV ('mu'min,' 'one who believes/grants security'). The plural ending '-ūna' marks a masculine human plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or doer ('the believers' as those performing the action).

4.meaning: So that they may go forth / set out — to march out, mobilize, or sally forth, especially in the sense of moving out as a body for a campaign or undertaking. Combines a purpose particle with the verb 'to go forth.'
4.grammar: A present-tense verb with the purpose particle li- ('so that'), which makes it subjunctive — so the indicative nūn is dropped, leaving the plural ending -ū ('they', with a silent spelling alif). It expresses purpose or intended action.
4.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to go forth, set out, mobilize

5.meaning: "all together, entirely, as a whole" — a term stressing totality and completeness: the whole group acting or being addressed without exception.
5.grammar: An indefinite noun used adverbially (a ḥāl/circumstantial). The -an ending (here written on the tā' marbūṭa as -tan) is the accusative, which is the case used for adverbs of manner describing how something is done — 'all together / in full'.
5.root: ك-ف-ف (k-f-f) — to restrain, hold back; (in this form) totality, all-encompassing

6.meaning: "So if not / then were it not for" — combines 'so/then' with 'lawlā', which introduces a 'were it not for…' condition (something whose absence would change the outcome) and can also urge 'why not…?'.

parts.en: were it not for / why not

6.grammar: A connective 'fa' ('so, then', often marking a result) plus the particle 'lawlā'. As a conditional particle 'lawlā' sets up 'were it not for X (then Y would not be)'; as an incitement it means 'why do you not…?'. It is a function word, not inflected.

7.meaning: He went forth / set out / marched out — the past-tense act of going out or sallying forth, the same notion of mobilizing and moving out as a group toward something.

parts.en: he (3rd person masculine singular, past tense)

7.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The bare stem with final -a means 'he did' the action — a completed act by a single masculine subject. It can also serve as the base from which other persons are formed.
7.root: ن-ف-ر (n-f-r) — to go forth, set out, mobilize

8.meaning: 'From, out of': a preposition marking the starting point or source of something — the origin from which a thing comes, or a part taken from a whole.
8.grammar: A preposition expressing origin, source, or partition ('from, out of, some of'). A noun governed by min stands in the genitive relationship and would typically take an -i type ending. The particle itself is invariable.

9.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
9.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.

10.meaning: A group, party, or detachment — a portion of people separated off from a larger body. From a root meaning to part or divide, it denotes a distinct band or contingent.
10.grammar: A feminine indefinite noun (tā' marbūṭa for the feminine). The final -tin (genitive, with nunation) marks it as genitive — typically following a preposition or linked to a preceding noun ('of/from a group').
10.root: ف-ر-ق (f-r-q) — to part, separate, divide

11.meaning: 'Among them / from them / some of them' — the preposition 'min' ('from, of, among') joined to the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them').
11.grammar: The preposition 'min' ('from / of / among') with the attached pronoun 'hum' ('them'), referring to a masculine plural group. Together they often express 'part of them' or 'some among them'.

12.meaning: Indefinite noun meaning 'a group,' 'a party,' 'a band,' or 'a portion' of people — a section or company of a larger body.
12.grammar: A feminine singular noun. The final '-tun' (feminine ending with tanwīn ḍamma) marks it indefinite ('a group') and in the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or a stand-alone predicate.
12.root: ط-و-ف (ṭ-w-f) — to go around, circle; a band or group (that moves about)

13.meaning: So that they may gain deep understanding — specifically to become learned and discerning in religion, acquiring careful comprehension and insight. The form intensifies the verb to mean 'to attain thorough understanding.'

parts.en: gain deep understanding / become learned (in religion)

13.grammar: A present-tense reflexive/intensive verb (Form V) with the purpose particle li- ('so that'), which makes it subjunctive — so the indicative nūn is dropped, leaving the plural ending -ū ('they', silent spelling alif). The pattern conveys deliberately acquiring understanding for oneself. (The shadda on the lām of li- here reflects assimilation of the article's lām on the following word, not a doubling within this prefix.)
13.root: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h) — to understand, comprehend deeply (esp. in religion)

14.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
14.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

15.meaning: A term for 'the religion, the faith, the way of life and obedience owed to Allah'. It covers belief, worship, law, and the system of accountability and recompense — broader than the English word 'religion'.
15.grammar: A definite noun ('the religion'); the al- prefix means 'the'. The -i ending is genitive, the case used after a preposition or in a possessive link ('… of …').
15.root: د-ي-ن (d-y-n) — religion, judgment, requital, obedience, debt

16.meaning: And so that they may warn — to caution, alert, or admonish others of a danger or coming consequence, putting them on their guard. The form means 'to make someone wary' by giving warning.
16.grammar: A present-tense causative verb (Form IV) with the joining word wa- ('and') and the purpose particle li- ('so that'), which makes it subjunctive — so the indicative nūn is dropped, leaving the plural ending -ū ('they'). The yu- prefix is the present marker for this causative pattern ('to give warning').

17.meaning: Their people / their folk — the community, kinsfolk, or tribe to which 'they' belong.
17.grammar: A masculine singular noun meaning a body of people, with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a ending is accusative, which typically marks the noun as the direct object of a verb ('… their people' as the thing acted upon).
17.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, to rise; a people who stand together

18.meaning: 'When' — a particle introducing a time or circumstance, generally pointing to something expected or definite to come ('when/whenever it happens'). It sets up a condition or moment whose outcome then follows.
18.grammar: An indeclinable adverb/particle of time; it has no case ending and never changes form. It typically introduces a clause about a future or recurring event ('when …'), and is normally followed by a verb describing what takes place.

19.meaning: They returned / came back — the completed act of going back to a place or state, or turning back. A straightforward past-tense of returning.
19.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb. The plural ending -ū means 'they (masculine) did' the action as a completed event; the written alif after it is silent. It states something already accomplished.
19.root: ر-ج-ع (r-j-ʿ) — to return, come back, turn back

20.meaning: A particle-and-pronoun unit meaning 'toward them / to them' — indicating direction or the goal of a motion, attention, or address aimed at a group.
20.grammar: The preposition ilā ('to / toward'), which shifts to the form ilay- when a pronoun attaches, plus the suffix -him ('them'). The pronoun is in the genitive/oblique form required after a preposition; the whole expresses direction toward a goal.
20.root: — (preposition with attached pronoun; no triliteral root)

21.meaning: 'So that they may / perhaps they will.' A particle expressing hope, expectation, or purpose, fused with the pronoun 'them'; it introduces a hoped-for or intended outcome.

parts.en: perhaps / so that / in hope that

21.grammar: The particle laʿalla ('perhaps, in the hope that, so that') with the attached pronoun -hum ('them'), which serves as its subject. Laʿalla belongs to a family of particles that put a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; -hum is that fixed object form. It conveys hope or an intended purpose rather than certainty.
21.root: — (particle with pronoun; no root)

22.meaning: They take heed / beware / guard themselves — to be cautious and on one's guard against something harmful, taking warning and steering clear of it.
22.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending means 'they (masculine plural) do' the action ongoing or habitually; the final nūn marks the indicative (a plain statement, not a command or subjunctive).
22.root: ح-ذ-ر (ḥ-dh-r) — to beware, be cautious, take heed

1.meaning: 'O…!' — a compound vocative expression used to call out and summon an audience before addressing them. It fuses the call-particle 'yā' ('O') with a noun that means 'the one(s) addressed,' yielding an emphatic 'O you…!' that introduces direct address.
1.grammar: A vocative (calling) construction. 'Yā' is the particle for calling out; 'ayyu' carries a nominative '-u' as the one being summoned; 'hā' is an attention-drawing particle. Together they function as 'O you…!,' setting up the noun of address that follows.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
3.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

4.meaning: Fight! / Do battle! — a command to engage in combat against an opponent. Form III implies mutual fighting (one party against another).
4.grammar: An imperative (command) verb in Form III, addressed to a group. The '-ū' ending directs the order to a masculine plural 'you all.' Form III conveys reciprocal action — to fight against an opposing party.

5.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
5.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

6.meaning: They are next to / adjoin / are near you — to be close by and bordering, immediately adjacent. Combines the verb 'to be next to / follow closely' with the object 'you (plural).'

parts.en: are next to / adjoin / are near

6.grammar: A present-tense verb (from a weak root) with the indicative ending -ūna ('they'), here followed by the attached object pronoun -kum ('you all'). The ya-…-ūna frame means 'they (masculine plural) are/do' as an ongoing state.
6.root: و-ل-ي (w-l-y) — to be near, adjoin, be next to / follow closely

7.meaning: From, out of, of — a preposition marking a starting point, origin, or source, or singling part out of a whole. Its core sense is movement or derivation away from a point.
7.grammar: A preposition. Its base form is min; the final vowel appears as -a (mina) when it is followed by a word beginning with the definite article 'al-', to ease pronunciation. It causes the following noun to take the genitive case.

8.meaning: The disbelievers / the ungrateful — those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The plural form (kuffār) stresses persistent, often defiant denial; the root sense is 'to cover/conceal,' hence to deny what is true and be ungrateful.
8.grammar: A definite plural noun (intensive pattern fuʿʿāl) with the article al- ('the'). The final -i is genitive: it typically links the word to a preceding noun ('… of the disbelievers') or follows a preposition.
8.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal; to disbelieve, be ungrateful

9.meaning: And let them find / so let them find — a command directed at others ('let them …') to find or encounter something. Combines a joining word, the imperative particle, and the verb 'to find.'
9.grammar: A present-tense verb made into a command of the third person by the prefixed lām of command (l-, 'let …'), joined by wa- ('and'). This puts the verb in the jussive — the indicative nūn is dropped, leaving the plural -ū ('let them find'); the written alif is silent.
9.root: و-ج-د (w-j-d) — to find, come upon, encounter

10.meaning: Among you / in you: locates something within a group of people addressed in the plural.
10.grammar: A preposition 'in/among' with an attached pronoun -kum meaning 'you' for a group of males (or mixed group). Words after the preposition fī stand in the genitive, which is why the pronoun takes this object form. The whole expresses presence or location within the addressed group.

11.meaning: Harshness, sternness, roughness — hardness of manner or toughness, the opposite of softness and gentleness. It denotes a severe, firm, unyielding quality.
11.grammar: A feminine indefinite noun (tā' marbūṭa for the feminine). The final -tan (accusative, with nunation) marks it as an indefinite object — typically the thing found, shown, or encountered ('harshness').
11.root: غ-ل-ظ (gh-l-ẓ) — to be thick, hard, harsh, stern

12.meaning: And know! — the connector 'and' joined to a command to know, realize, or be aware of something. A direct summons to a group to take firm notice.
12.grammar: A command (imperative) verb directed at a group. The ending -ū marks the masculine plural addressee ('you all, know!'). Prefixed with wa- ('and').

13.meaning: An emphatic particle meaning 'that' (as in 'I know that...') or 'indeed/surely.' It introduces a statement and gives it certainty and emphasis, presenting what follows as an established fact.
13.grammar: An emphatic particle that introduces a noun-clause ('that...'). It puts the following noun into the accusative case and lends the whole statement a sense of certainty and assertion. It typically comes after verbs of knowing, saying, or informing.

14.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the sole divine Being worshipped, unique and without partner. It is a definite, unparalleled name, not a common noun for any 'god.'
14.grammar: A proper name. The final -a is the accusative case, which typically marks the word as the direct object of a verb, or as the noun governed by certain particles. The name is inherently definite and does not take a separate 'al-'.

15.meaning: With, together with, alongside — indicating company, accompaniment, or being in the same place or time as another.
15.grammar: A preposition of accompaniment ('with, alongside'); grammatically it is an adverbial of place/time (ẓarf) that governs the genitive. It is placed before a following noun to put one thing in the company of another, and that following noun stands in the genitive. The -a is its fixed ending.

16.meaning: The God-conscious / the mindful — those who guard themselves against wrongdoing out of reverent awareness of Allah (taqwā), shielding their souls by dutiful caution. The "al-" makes it definite ("the mindful ones").

parts.en: one who is God-conscious / guards himself

16.grammar: A definite active participle in the masculine sound plural (singular "muttaqin"). The "-īna" ending is the plural form in the genitive/accusative (oblique) case — used for governed nouns, objects, or after prepositions.

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: It (feminine) was sent down / revealed — a completed act in which something (such as a passage of scripture) was brought down from on high, with a feminine subject.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice of the 'afʿala' pattern ('was caused to come down / was revealed'). The internal vowel pattern (u–i) marks it as passive ('was …-ed' rather than 'did'). The '-at' ending marks a feminine singular subject: 'it (fem.) was sent down.'
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come/send down, descend, reveal

4.meaning: A chapter or section of revelation — a discrete, named unit of the Qur'an, complete in itself. The word denotes an enclosed division of the sacred text, like a wall or row that bounds a distinct portion. Being indefinite, it means 'a chapter / some chapter' rather than a specific one.

parts.en: chapter (of the Qur'an); the stem already ends in the feminine tā' marbūṭa (ة)

4.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final nunation (the -un sound, written as the two-ḍamma sign) marks it as indefinite ('a chapter / some chapter'), and that nunation is built on the ḍamma vowel, which is the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being named/described. The tā' marbūṭa (ة) that gives the word its feminine form belongs to the stem itself, not to this ending.
4.root: س-و-ر (s-w-r) — to enclose, wall round; a row or tier (hence a bounded section)

5.meaning: "so / and among them / of them (there are)" — the preposition min ('from, among, of') with the pronoun 'them', expressing 'among them' or 'some of them', introduced by 'so/and'.
5.grammar: A connective particle plus a preposition with an attached pronoun. Fa- means 'so/and then', linking to what precedes. Min ('from/among') takes no case ending; the suffix -hum is 'them' (third-person masculine plural). The phrase often introduces a partition ('among them are…').

6.meaning: A versatile word meaning 'who / whoever / the one who.' It can ask a question ('who?') or introduce a clause ('whoever does…'), referring to persons.
6.grammar: An indeclinable particle/pronoun with a fixed form (it does not change for case). Used for rational beings ('who'), functioning either as an interrogative ('who?') or as a conditional/relative ('whoever, the one who').

7.meaning: He says / he is saying — the act of speaking or uttering words, attributed to a single male (or generic) subject in the ongoing or habitual sense.
7.grammar: A present/imperfect-tense verb. The prefix ya- marks a third-person masculine singular subject ('he'). Here the ya is written with a shadda (doubled, yya-) because a preceding word's final consonant assimilates into it and merges (idghām); the doubling belongs to that sound-merger, not to the verb itself. The final -u is the indicative ending, the default mood used for a plain statement of fact about an action that is ongoing or habitual ('he says / he is saying').
7.root: ق-و-ل (q-w-l) — to say, speak, utter

8.meaning: Which of you? / which one of you? — an interrogative meaning 'which?' joined to 'you (plural),' singling out one or some from among a group of people being addressed.
8.grammar: An interrogative noun 'which?' in a possessive (genitive) link with the attached pronoun -kum ('of you all'), forming 'which of you?' The -u on ayyu is its nominative ending, marking it as the subject/topic of the question.

9.meaning: It increased him/it / added to him — the past-tense act of making more or augmenting, with an attached object. From a root meaning to grow or add, here 'something increased him' in some quality or amount.
9.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb (from a hollow root, written with alif). The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it [did]'); the attached -hu is the object 'him/it.' So the frame means 'it [feminine] increased him.'

10.meaning: Feminine singular demonstrative pronoun, 'this (one)' — pointing to a single nearby thing that is grammatically feminine.
10.grammar: A demonstrative ('this') for a single feminine thing close at hand, contrasting with the masculine 'hādhā.' Demonstratives in Arabic do not change for grammatical case; the form stays fixed whether subject, object, or after a preposition.
10.root: — (demonstrative pronoun; no triliteral root)

11.meaning: Faith — a deep, trusting belief and inner security of heart; to affirm and entrust oneself to the truth. More than intellectual assent, it conveys trust, fidelity, and the safety that comes from believing.
11.grammar: A verbal noun (Form IV, conveying 'to bring about security/belief'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('tanwīn'): it commonly marks an indefinite object of a verb or specifies in what respect something occurs ('in respect of faith').
11.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust; freedom from fear and the faith built upon it.

12.meaning: 'Then as for …' A connective opening that introduces and singles out a topic for comment, often paired later with a response. The fa- means 'then/so,' and 'ammā' sets up 'as for (such-and-such)…' to highlight one case among others.
12.grammar: A connector fa- ('then, so') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā introduces a subject for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that gives the comment about it. Neither part takes case endings.

13.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
13.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

14.meaning: A verb meaning 'they believed / they came to have faith' — they affirmed the truth and placed trustful, secure faith in Allah. The Form IV pattern turns the root idea of safety/trust into the act of entering into faith.
14.grammar: A past/perfect verb, Form IV, third-person masculine plural. The -ū ending means 'they (masc.) did' a completed action — here, that they came to believe. The written final alif after -ū is a silent spelling convention and is not pronounced.

15.meaning: So it increased them / then it added to them — the same act of augmenting, with the connector 'so/then' at the front and 'them' as the object. From a root meaning to grow or add: 'so something increased them' in some respect.
15.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb (from a hollow root) prefixed with fa- ('so/then'), which links it as a result or sequel to what precedes. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it [did]'); the attached -hum is the object 'them.'
15.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, grow, add

16.meaning: Faith — a deep, trusting belief and inner security of heart; to affirm and entrust oneself to the truth. More than intellectual assent, it conveys trust, fidelity, and the safety that comes from believing.
16.grammar: A verbal noun (Form IV, conveying 'to bring about security/belief'). The -an ending is the indefinite accusative ('tanwīn'): it commonly marks an indefinite object of a verb or specifies in what respect something occurs ('in respect of faith').
16.root: ء-م-ن (ʾ-m-n) — security, safety, trust; freedom from fear and the faith built upon it.

17.meaning: 'And they.' The opening 'and' joined to the standalone subject pronoun 'they' (a group of males). A standalone pronoun like this typically begins or emphasizes a statement about its referent.
17.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') with the detached subject pronoun hum ('they,' masculine plural). As an independent (not attached) pronoun, it serves as the subject of a clause and often lends emphasis to the ones spoken about.

18.meaning: A verb meaning 'they receive glad tidings / rejoice at good news', and in this intensive (derived) form 'they eagerly welcome and delight in good news'. The face brightens at the arrival of something good.
18.grammar: An imperfect (present/ongoing) verb. The ya- prefix with the -ūna ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'); the -ūna ending also signals the indicative mood — a plain statement that this is happening.

1.meaning: 'And as for …' A connective that introduces and sets apart a new topic for separate comment, usually anticipating a matching response clause. The 'and' joins it on; 'ammā' means 'as for (such-and-such)…'
1.grammar: The conjunction wa ('and') joined to the detailing/conditional particle ammā ('as for…'). Ammā singles out a topic for separate treatment and normally anticipates a matching clause (often introduced by 'fa-') that supplies the comment. Neither part takes case endings.

2.meaning: 'Those who' — a relative pronoun for a group of masculine (or mixed) persons, introducing a clause that describes them: 'the ones who …'. It links a following statement back to the people it refers to.
2.grammar: A masculine plural relative pronoun. Although it ends in -ina, it is indeclinable — fixed in this one form for every grammatical position — and simply means 'those who'. It must be completed by a following clause that tells what those people do or are.

3.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
3.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.

4.meaning: 'Their hearts' — the plural of qalb ('heart'), joined to the pronoun 'their'. In Qur'anic usage the 'heart' (qalb) is the seat of understanding, intention, faith, and feeling, not merely the physical organ.
4.grammar: Qulūb is the broken (irregular) plural of qalb, 'hearts'. The -i ending is genitive: here it appears because the noun follows a preposition and because it is possessed by an attached pronoun. The suffix -him means 'their' (a masculine plural group), and its -i- vowel matches the preceding genitive ending. So the whole means 'hearts belonging to them'.
4.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — heart; to turn over, turn about, change

5.meaning: A noun meaning 'a disease,' 'sickness,' or 'ailment' — a disorder that afflicts the body, and figuratively a corruption or malady of the heart (such as doubt, hypocrisy, or ill intent).
5.grammar: A common noun, masculine singular. The final '-un' (nunation/tanwīn) marks it as indefinite ('a disease') and in the nominative case, which typically identifies it as a subject or as the thing stated to exist. (When the word follows another ending in a consonant, that consonant may assimilate onto its first letter in recitation, but this gemination is external and not part of the word itself.)
5.root: م-ر-ض (m-r-ḍ) — to be sick, diseased, ailing

6.meaning: So it increased them / then it added to them — the same act of augmenting, with the connector 'so/then' at the front and 'them' as the object. From a root meaning to grow or add: 'so something increased them' in some respect.
6.grammar: A past-tense (perfect) verb (from a hollow root) prefixed with fa- ('so/then'), which links it as a result or sequel to what precedes. The -at ending marks a feminine singular subject ('she/it [did]'); the attached -hum is the object 'them.'
6.root: ز-ي-د (z-y-d) — to increase, grow, add

7.meaning: Filth, impurity, defilement — that which is unclean or foul, whether physically dirty or morally and spiritually corrupt. It denotes a polluting, abominable quality.
7.grammar: A masculine indefinite noun. The final -an (accusative, with nunation) marks it as an indefinite object or specifier — often the thing added or the respect in which something is described ('filth / in impurity').
7.root: ر-ج-س (r-j-s) — to be filthy, unclean, impure

8.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
8.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

9.meaning: Their filth, impurity, or moral defilement — something foul and unclean, used both literally (physical dirt) and figuratively for spiritual corruption, sin, or inner rottenness. The attached pronoun makes it belong to a group of males.

parts.en: connector vowel (links the noun to the attached pronoun)

9.grammar: A noun carrying the attached pronoun -him ('their'), referring to a group of males. When a pronominal suffix attaches directly to a noun, the noun's own case vowel is suppressed and replaced by the linking vowel the suffix requires — here the -i- before -him. This connector vowel appears regardless of the noun's underlying case, so it is not itself a readable case marker.

10.meaning: And they died — a third-person masculine plural past verb: their lives came to an end.
10.grammar: Prefix 'wa' = 'and.' Past-tense verb. The -ū ending marks the subject as 'they,' and the perfect form presents the action as completed: 'they died.'
10.root: م-و-ت (m-w-t) — death, dying

11.meaning: 'While they / and they' — the word 'wa' (here 'while' or 'and') joined to the standalone pronoun 'hum' ('they'), referring to a masculine plural group.
11.grammar: A connective 'wa' — often circumstantial 'while' — plus the independent subject pronoun 'hum' ('they'), used for a masculine plural group. As an independent pronoun it usually stands as the subject of a following statement.

12.meaning: Disbelievers / deniers: those who reject faith and cover over the truth. The active participle names people characterized by ungrateful rejection of what should be acknowledged.
12.grammar: A masculine plural active participle. The -ūna ending marks a masculine plural in the nominative case — the form used when the word is the subject or predicate (as opposed to -īna for object/genitive).
12.root: ك-ف-ر (k-f-r) — to cover, conceal, disbelieve, be ungrateful

1.meaning: A compound opener meaning roughly 'And do …not …?' — combining a yes/no question marker, a connective 'and,' and the negative 'not,' used to pose a rhetorical question that affirms its point.
1.grammar: A cluster of particles, not a word with case or tense: a question marker a-, the connective wa- ('and'), and the negator lā ('not'). Together they introduce a rhetorical question of the type 'Do they not …?', expecting the listener to acknowledge what follows.

2.meaning: They see, they perceive; also to realize or witness. Looking upon something with the eyes or the understanding.
2.grammar: A present-tense verb. The ya- prefix together with the -na ending marks a third-person masculine plural subject ('they'). The -na ending is the indicative mood, used for a plain statement of fact ('they see / they will see').
2.root: ر-ا-ي (r-ʾ-y) — to see, perceive, consider

3.meaning: 'That they…' — an emphatic connector 'anna' ('that, indeed') fused with the pronoun 'they,' used to introduce an affirmed clause as the content of a thought or statement.
3.grammar: Built on the particle 'anna' ('that…, indeed'), which introduces and affirms a following clause (often after verbs of knowing, thinking, or saying) and puts its noun into the accusative. The attached '-hum' is the pronoun 'they/them' for a male-inclusive group.

4.meaning: They are tested, tried, or put through trial — placed under affliction or temptation to prove and expose what is truly within a person. The verb is passive: the subject undergoes the testing rather than carrying it out.
4.grammar: A present-tense passive verb. The yu- prefix with the internal vowel pattern marks the passive ('are being …-ed'), and the -ūna ending means the subject is 'they' (a group of males) with the action ongoing or habitual. Passive voice means the doers are the ones acted upon.
4.root: ف-ت-ن (f-t-n) — to test, try, tempt, afflict

5.meaning: A preposition meaning 'in,' 'within,' or 'inside.' It locates something inside a place, a time, a state, or a matter — physically or figuratively (e.g. 'in' a condition or 'concerning' a matter).
5.grammar: A preposition. It is invariable (it does not change form) and places the following noun into the genitive case, indicating containment or location 'in / within' something.
5.root: — (particle)

6.meaning: 'every,' 'each,' or 'all' — a word expressing totality or completeness. It indicates the entirety of something: when joined to a singular indefinite noun it means 'every (single) one,' and when joined to a definite noun it can mean 'all of' or 'the whole of.'
6.grammar: A noun of totality. The final '-i' ending is genitive (the 'of/possession' case): it marks the word as governed by a preceding preposition or as the first term of a possessive link to a following noun, so it typically reads 'of every…' or 'every…' leading into what follows.
6.root: ك-ل-ل (k-l-l) — totality, comprising the whole

7.meaning: a year — a full year, a complete cycle of time; sometimes carrying the sense of a year of plenty or season.
7.grammar: A singular masculine noun. The final -in ending shows the genitive case together with the indefinite 'a/an'. The genitive here is typical of a noun being counted after a number ('a hundred of year') or linked to a preceding word.
7.root: ع-و-م (ʿ-w-m) — a year, an annual cycle

8.meaning: One time, once — a single occurrence or instance of something. It is the noun for a 'time' in the counting sense (as in 'one time, two times').
8.grammar: A feminine noun in the accusative case, shown by the -an ending (indefinite accusative, 'tanwīn'). The accusative commonly marks an adverbial sense of measure or frequency — telling 'how many times' an action happens.
8.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass by; a passing, hence an instance/time

9.meaning: Or — a particle offering an alternative or another option, linking two possibilities ('this… or that…'). It can also introduce an approximation or a different case.
9.grammar: A fixed connecting particle (a conjunction) with no case ending. It joins two words or clauses to present an alternative between them.

10.meaning: Two times, twice — exactly two occurrences of something. It is the dual ('exactly two') form of the noun meaning 'a time/instance'.
10.grammar: A dual noun, meaning 'exactly two' of the thing. The -ayni ending marks the dual in the accusative or genitive state; for an adverb of frequency this conveys 'two times / twice'. Arabic has a special dual distinct from the plural (three or more).
10.root: م-ر-ر (m-r-r) — to pass by; a passing, hence an instance/time

11.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
11.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

12.meaning: A particle of negation, 'no' or 'not'. In one common usage it denies the existence of an entire category ('there is no … at all'); it also serves as a simple 'no' and can negate verbs in certain constructions. Its core function is to cancel or rule out what follows.
12.grammar: An indeclinable negating particle: it has no case, tense, or number and never changes shape. It works by governing the word after it — for instance driving a following indefinite noun to a bare form to express absolute negation ('there is no …').

13.meaning: 'They turn back in repentance' — from tāba; describes a group repeatedly or presently returning to Allah from sin.
13.grammar: A present/ongoing verb. The ya-…-ūna frame marks a masculine-plural subject ('they') doing the action now or habitually. The full -ūna ending (rather than shortened -ū) signals the ordinary, unaltered present-tense (indicative) form.
13.root: ت-و-ب (t-w-b) — to turn back, repent, return

14.meaning: And not / but not — a connective 'and' joined to a negating particle that rules out or forbids what follows.
14.grammar: 'wa' is 'and'. 'lā' is a negating particle; placed before a verb of command it expresses prohibition ('do not ...'), and before other verbs/nouns it expresses negation ('not ...'). It carries no case ending.

15.meaning: An independent (standalone) pronoun meaning 'they' (referring to a group of males, or a mixed group). Because it stands on its own rather than being attached to a verb or noun, it often adds emphasis, singling out or stressing the subject ('they themselves', 'it is they who').
15.grammar: A detached subject pronoun, third person masculine plural. It does not take case endings; the fixed -m simply marks the plural 'they'. Standing alone, it commonly serves to emphasise or isolate the subject.

16.meaning: 'They take heed / call to mind' — to be reminded, to reflect and remember a lesson or truth, said of a group, in the present tense.
16.grammar: Present-tense reflexive verb (an assimilated form of 'yatadhakkarūna,' the self-reminding pattern). The 'ya-' prefix with the '-ūna' ending marks a masculine plural subject ('they'); '-ūna' is the indicative mood, signalling an ongoing or repeated action.

1.meaning: 'And when...' — a linking phrase joining 'and' to 'when', used to introduce a circumstance or a recurring situation: 'and whenever / and at the time that...'.
1.grammar: The connector wa- ('and') attached to idhā ('when'). Idhā is a particle pointing to a time or condition, generally referring to something expected or recurring in the future ('when / whenever' it happens), and it normally introduces a following clause that states what occurs at that time.

2.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
2.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

3.meaning: It (feminine) was sent down / revealed — a completed act in which something (such as a passage of scripture) was brought down from on high, with a feminine subject.
3.grammar: A past-tense verb in the passive voice of the 'afʿala' pattern ('was caused to come down / was revealed'). The internal vowel pattern (u–i) marks it as passive ('was …-ed' rather than 'did'). The '-at' ending marks a feminine singular subject: 'it (fem.) was sent down.'
3.root: ن-ز-ل (n-z-l) — to come/send down, descend, reveal

4.meaning: A chapter or section of revelation — a discrete, named unit of the Qur'an, complete in itself. The word denotes an enclosed division of the sacred text, like a wall or row that bounds a distinct portion. Being indefinite, it means 'a chapter / some chapter' rather than a specific one.

parts.en: chapter (of the Qur'an); the stem already ends in the feminine tā' marbūṭa (ة)

4.grammar: A singular feminine noun. The final nunation (the -un sound, written as the two-ḍamma sign) marks it as indefinite ('a chapter / some chapter'), and that nunation is built on the ḍamma vowel, which is the nominative case — the case used for the subject of a sentence or the thing being named/described. The tā' marbūṭa (ة) that gives the word its feminine form belongs to the stem itself, not to this ending.
4.root: س-و-ر (s-w-r) — to enclose, wall round; a row or tier (hence a bounded section)

5.meaning: He looked, glanced, or gazed — to direct one's sight toward something; by extension to observe, consider, or reflect upon a matter.
5.grammar: A past-tense verb. The bare stem with a final -a vowel marks a completed action done by 'he' (a single male). Arabic past-tense verbs carry the doer within the verb itself, so no separate pronoun is needed.
5.root: ن-ظ-ر (n-ẓ-r) — to look, see, observe, consider

6.meaning: 'Some of them' / 'a part of them' — a noun meaning 'a portion, part, or some' joined to an attached pronoun 'them'. Often paired with itself to express 'one another / each other'.
6.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the nominative case (the -u ending), which typically marks it as the subject or doer. The suffix -hum is a genitive (possessive) pronoun meaning 'their' (masculine plural); attached to a noun this way it sits in the possessor slot, giving 'some of them'.
6.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

7.meaning: A preposition meaning 'to,' 'toward,' or 'up to' — pointing to the end-point, goal, or limit of a motion, direction, or extent.
7.grammar: A preposition (a small linking word). It governs the noun after it, putting that noun in the genitive case, and points to a destination or limit ('to,' 'toward,' 'as far as').

8.meaning: 'Some (others)' / 'a part' — the same noun for 'a portion or some,' here left indefinite, often functioning as the counterpart in the 'one another' construction.
8.grammar: A noun 'part/some' in the genitive case with indefinite marking (the -in ending, called tanwīn). The genitive typically follows a preposition or links it to a preceding noun ('… of …'); the doubled -n sound marks it as indefinite ('a part / some').
8.root: ب-ع-ض (b-ʿ-ḍ) — a part, portion, or some of a whole

9.meaning: An interrogative particle that turns a statement into a yes/no question, roughly "is it that…?" or "do…?". It can also carry a rhetorical or expectant tone rather than a literal request for information.
9.grammar: A question particle placed before a sentence to ask whether something is the case. It has no case ending and does not change form; it simply marks the words that follow as a yes/no question.

10.meaning: 'He sees you (plural)' — the act of seeing or watching a group, said of a single observer, in the present tense.
10.grammar: Present-tense verb 'yarā' (he sees) from a weak-ending root, with the 'ya-' prefix marking a third-person masculine singular subject ('he/it'). It ends in a long '-ā' (the weak final letter) for the indicative; the attached '-kum' is the object pronoun 'you all.'
10.root: ر-ء-ي (r-ʾ-y) — seeing, perceiving

11.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
11.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

12.meaning: One; anyone; a single individual. Often used in negative or conditional contexts to mean 'anyone (at all)'.
12.grammar: An indefinite noun in the genitive case. The -in ending combines the genitive marker -i (the form taken after a preposition or in a possessive link, '… of …') with nunation (-n), the sign of an indefinite 'a / any'.

13.meaning: A connective particle meaning 'then' or 'thereafter' that links two statements in sequence, but unlike a simple 'and' it signals an ordered succession with a sense of delay or interval — one thing happens, and after some lapse the next follows.
13.grammar: An invariable connective particle; it has no case ending and never changes form. Its function is to coordinate clauses in temporal or logical order, implying that what follows comes after a gap or interval.

14.meaning: They turned away, departed, or went off — to turn oneself aside and leave, withdrawing from a place or situation. The base verb conveys turning and diverting away.
14.grammar: A past-tense verb in the reflexive/middle pattern (the in- prefix gives the sense of the action turning back on the doer — 'turned themselves away'). The -ū ending means the doers are 'they' (a group of males) and the action is completed.
14.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn away, divert, dispose, dispel

15.meaning: He turned (something) away, diverted, or averted it — to cause a thing or person to turn aside, to divert or dispel it from its course.
15.grammar: A past-tense verb. The bare stem ending in -a marks a completed act by 'he' (a single male). This basic form is transitive — it normally takes an object: he turned/diverted something. The doer is built into the verb.
15.root: ص-ر-ف (ṣ-r-f) — to turn away, divert, dispose, dispel

16.meaning: The proper name Allah — the One True God, the unique and supreme Deity worshipped in Islam, without partner or equal. The name itself denotes the sole object of worship. Here it stands in the nominative case (as a subject or topic).
16.grammar: A proper noun (the divine name). Every letter of اللّٰه, including the final ه, is an integral consonant of the name; it is not built from separable affixes. Only the short vowel damma (-u) written over the final ه is a grammatical marker: it is the nominative case ending, the form a noun takes when it is the doer/subject of a verb or the topic of a sentence. So the damma marks Allah as the one performing the action or the subject being described, while the consonant ه remains part of the name itself.

17.meaning: 'Their hearts.' The noun denotes the heart as the inner seat of feeling, understanding, and intention; its very name evokes turning and fluctuation, since the heart is what shifts and changes.
17.grammar: A plural noun ('hearts') with the attached possessive -hum ('their'). The -a vowel on the noun is the accusative ending, which typically marks the word as the object of a verb (the thing being acted upon).
17.root: ق-ل-ب (q-l-b) — to turn over, change; hence the heart, which turns

18.meaning: A connector meaning 'because they…' or 'by reason that they…'. It fuses the preposition bi- (here giving a cause, 'because of') with anna ('that', an emphatic particle introducing a fact) and the attached pronoun -hum ('they').
18.grammar: bi- here gives a causal sense ('because of'). anna is an emphatic particle meaning 'that' which introduces a statement of fact and takes a following noun or pronoun in the accusative; the attached -hum is that pronoun, a masculine plural 'they'. Together they give a reason: 'because they …'.

19.meaning: 'A people / folk / community' — a group of people bound together, often by kinship, tribe, or shared identity.
19.grammar: An indefinite collective noun ('a people'), grammatically singular but referring to a group. The -un ending is indefinite ('a') and nominative, the case typically used for the subject of a sentence.
19.root: ق-و-م (q-w-m) — to stand, rise; a group that stands together

20.meaning: 'Not' — a particle of negation. Depending on context it denies a present fact, forbids an action, or rules something out ('do not / there is no').
20.grammar: A negating particle, 'not / no'. It is used to deny or prohibit — negating present-tense statements, expressing 'there is no...', or, with a command form, forbidding an action ('do not...').

21.meaning: Verb meaning 'they understand / comprehend deeply' — to grasp the inner meaning of something with discernment, a perceptive, penetrating understanding.
21.grammar: A present-tense verb, masculine third-person plural. The complete '-ūna' ending (with the 'nūn' intact) signals the indicative mood — a plain ongoing statement, 'they understand.' The root connotes deep, discerning comprehension rather than mere hearing.
21.root: ف-ق-ه (f-q-h) — to understand deeply, comprehend with insight (source of the word fiqh)

1.meaning: A two-part emphasis particle meaning 'surely, indeed (already)' — 'la-' strongly affirms, and 'qad' before a past verb stresses that the action has definitely occurred.
1.grammar: Two particles fused for emphasis. 'la-' is the affirming prefix 'surely / truly.' 'qad,' when it precedes a past-tense verb, confirms and intensifies that the action really happened ('has indeed …'). Together they give a strong oath-like assurance to the statement that follows.

2.meaning: "he/it came to you" — a past verb "came" with the pronoun "you" as the one reached, i.e. something arrived at or reached a group of people.
2.grammar: A past-tense verb in its base third-person masculine singular form ("he/it came"), with no extra subject suffix. The verb "to come" is intransitive, so the attached -kum is not a direct object but an indirect (dative) pronoun — "to you" (masculine plural), equivalent to "came to you (all)."
2.root: ج-ي-ء (j-y-ʾ) — to come, arrive

3.meaning: "a messenger" — one who is sent bearing a message; an envoy or apostle, here in the indefinite sense "a messenger."
3.grammar: The -un ending is nominative with nunation: the -u marks it as a subject (the doer/topic), and the final -n signals that it is indefinite ("a messenger," not "the messenger").

4.meaning: A preposition whose core sense is 'from' — marking a starting point or origin (from a place, time, or source). It also commonly means 'of' or 'among' (part of a larger whole) and 'than' in comparisons.
4.grammar: A preposition. It is indeclinable and governs the following noun in the genitive case. Its primary force is point of origin ('starting from'), and it frequently expresses partitioning ('some of / part of').

5.meaning: 'Yourselves' — literally 'your own selves/souls.' Anfus is the plural of nafs ('self, soul, person'); with the attached pronoun it expresses the reflexive 'your own selves.'
5.grammar: A plural noun ('selves') with an attached possessive pronoun -kum ('your,' masculine plural). The -i ending is genitive: the noun is governed by a preceding preposition or stands in a possessive ('of …') construction.
5.root: ن-ف-س (n-f-s) — self / soul / breath

6.meaning: Mighty, invincible, and supremely honoured; one who possesses overwhelming power and dignity such that none can overcome or resist Him. As a divine descriptor it conveys unassailable might joined with exalted worth.
6.grammar: A descriptive noun (adjective) on an intensive pattern, conveying a deep, enduring quality. The -un ending is indefinite and nominative: it typically marks the word as a subject or as a predicate describing something ("is mighty").
6.root: ع-ز-ز (ʿ-z-z) — might, honour, strength

7.meaning: A preposition fused with a pronoun, meaning 'upon him', 'on him', or 'toward him'. It marks the one to whom an action is directed or upon whom something rests.
7.grammar: The preposition 'upon/on' with an attached object pronoun -hi ('him', third-person masculine singular); its -i vowel is the regular form the pronoun takes after the 'y' sound. Paired with a verb of turning, this 'upon/toward him' marks the person the action reaches.

8.meaning: A versatile word most often meaning 'what' or 'that which' — it can introduce a relative idea ('the thing that…'), ask a question ('what?'), or in other uses serve as a negating particle. Its core job is to stand in for an unspecified thing.
8.grammar: A fixed (indeclinable) particle with no case ending; its sense is set by context. As a relative it means 'that which' and needs a following clause; as an interrogative it means 'what?'.

9.meaning: 'You suffered hardship / fell into distress' — from a verb meaning to undergo difficulty, trouble, or harm; to be in a state of grievous strain.
9.grammar: A past-tense verb. The suffix -tum marks a second-person masculine plural subject ('you all did…'). (The stem's final t merges with the t of the ending, giving the doubled -tt-.) Past tense states a completed action.
9.root: ع-ن-ت (ʿ-n-t) — to suffer hardship, distress, difficulty; to come to harm

10.meaning: Eager, keenly desirous, deeply concerned — one who is intensely solicitous about something, anxious for its good and grieved at its loss. It describes an abiding, earnest care or covetous longing.
10.grammar: An adjective (intensive pattern, denoting a deep-seated quality) in the nominative case, shown by the -un ending (indefinite nominative, 'tanwīn'). The nominative typically marks the subject of a sentence or the thing being described.
10.root: ح-ر-ص (ḥ-r-ṣ) — to be eager, covetous, solicitous, intensely caring

11.meaning: 'Upon you (all)' — the preposition 'upon/on/over' joined to the plural 'you,' indicating something resting on or directed at a group.
11.grammar: The preposition 'ʿalā' ('upon/on/over') in its joined form 'ʿalay-' plus the attached pronoun '-kum' ('you all,' masculine plural). It marks the group as the recipients or target of whatever is laid 'upon' them.
11.root: — (preposition; no triliteral root)

12.meaning: With/in the believers — 'the believers' being those who have faith, who trust and affirm and are inwardly secure in belief. The word combines a preposition meaning 'with/by/in/toward' and the definite plural 'the believers'.
12.grammar: A preposition bi- ('with/by/toward') attached to the definite noun 'the believers'. The noun is in the genitive case — its sound masculine plural ending is -īna here — because words after a preposition take the genitive. The plural -īn(a) refers to three or more males (or a mixed group).

13.meaning: Most kind, gentle, and compassionate; one who is full of tender pity and gentleness. Raʾūf is an intensive form stressing deep, abundant kindness — a name/attribute of Allah meaning 'the Ever-Gentle, Most Compassionate.'

parts.en: full of kindness / most gentle (the final -un is the nominative ending with tanwīn, marking an indefinite predicate)

13.grammar: An intensive adjective ('one full of …') describing abundant kindness. The final '-un' is the nominative case ending together with tanwīn (the '-n' that marks an indefinite noun): it typically marks the word as a subject or, as here, a predicate/description ('… is most kind'). The intensive pattern stresses depth and constancy of the quality.

14.meaning: Most merciful, ever-merciful; one whose mercy is constant and abundant. As a divine attribute it denotes Allah's enduring, all-embracing compassion toward His creation.
